source: Written 2026-10-17 by Claude Sonnet and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin. Hand-written fixture questions are "approved".

notes.NC26.M1.RMM.1: All questions are text only; models are linear, exponential and quadratic as in NC Math 1. Contexts are different from the 9 existing questions (taxi, candle, plant, savings, tank, flyers, bacteria, car, tree).
notes.NC26.M1.ANFR.2: Text only: tables are written out as lists of values and graphs as points written (x, y). 90 new questions across eight skills; no skill has more than 12.
notes.NC26.M1.ANFR.3: Text only: functions are given by equations, short lists of values or points written (x, y). 90 new questions across eight skills (average rate of change 13, the others 10 to 12).
notes.NC26.M1.ANFR.5: Solving by graph or technology is not tested (needs a figure or a tool); the exponential equation question is solved by inspection of powers.
notes.NC26.M1.ANFR.6: Graphing the solution region is not tested (needs a figure); questions use points, boundary lines and interpretation in context.
notes.NC26.M1.ANFR.7: Graphing is tested through lines given by equations, points and written tables, never a picture. Inequalities are tested through checking points and building models in context.
notes.NC26.M1.SGMR.1: Figures are given by coordinates in the question text; no picture is referred to.
notes.NC26.M1.SGMR.2: Text only: the congruence criteria are tested by described measurements; no figures. Hypotenuse-leg is deliberately left out (not clearly part of the Math 1 summary).
notes.NC26.M1.SGMR.3: All coordinates are written out. Triangle area uses a horizontal base so no shoelace formula is needed.
notes.NC26.M1.SDSR.1: Two-way tables are given as sentences listing every cell. Probabilities may be entered as equivalent fractions or decimals.
notes.NC26.M1.SDSR.2: Mostly conceptual, so mostly choice questions; two numeric ones (response rate, count of statistical questions).
notes.NC26.M1.SDSR.3: Datasets are given as counts in words. The splitting-by-a-third-variable item gives all the numbers so the explanation can be checked.
notes.NC26.M1.SDSR.4: Written from the standard's summary only. All displays are described in words or lists of coordinates. Questions on a "scatter plot" give the points as written lists.
notes.NC26.M1.SDSR.5: No regression is computed by hand (it needs technology); questions use given lines, r values and a described residual plot.
notes.NC26.M1.SDSR.6: Text-only standard on communicating an investigation: about 40% numeric (percents, means and medians, scaling a sample to a population, margin of error) because most of the skills (critiquing, reporting, limits) are judgments best asked as choices. Count-the-correct-statements numeric items are used for a few conclusions skills. Margin of error appears only as a given "give or take" and as an interval read off; no formulas.

questions.skill: Name an assumption built into a model
questions.stem: Maya models the cost of a taxi ride with $C = 3 + 2m$, where $C$ is the cost in dollars and $m$ is the number of miles. Which assumption is built into this model?
choices: Longer rides cost more per mile
Every mile costs the same amount
There is no charge before the ride begins
The cost changes with the time of day
questions.answer: Every mile costs the same amount
questions.solution: In $C = 3 + 2m$ the cost rises by 2 dollars for every extra mile, so each mile costs the same. The 3 is a starting charge, and time of day does not appear in the model.

solve.answer: Every mile costs the same amount
solve.work: C = 3 + 2m: a fixed 3 dollars plus 2 dollars for each mile, so every mile adds the same 2 dollars (constant rate). Time of day is not in the model; cost per mile does not grow; and at m = 0 the cost is 3, so there IS a charge before any miles, making the last option false.

questions.skill: Use a model to make a prediction
questions.stem: A candle is 20 centimeters tall when lit and burns down 2 centimeters each hour. A student models its height with $h = 20 - 2t$, where $h$ is the height in centimeters after $t$ hours. According to the model, how tall is the candle after 6 hours, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Put $t = 6$ into the model: $h = 20 - 2 \times 6 = 20 - 12 = 8$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Revise a model when it disagrees with measurements
questions.stem: A student's model predicts that a plant will be 30 centimeters tall after 4 weeks. After 4 weeks the plant is measured and is 22 centimeters tall. What should the student do next?
choices: Revise the model so it fits the measurement better
Keep the model, because the prediction must be correct
Change the measurement to match the prediction
Decide that plants cannot be modeled
questions.answer: Revise the model so it fits the measurement better
questions.solution: A model is tested against real data. The prediction is 8 centimeters too high, so the student should look for what the model missed and revise it. Changing the measurement or giving up is not how the modeling cycle works.

solve.answer: Revise the model so it fits the measurement better
solve.work: Prediction 30, measurement 22: the model does not fit the data, so in the modeling cycle the student revises the model. Changing data, insisting the model is right, or giving up are all wrong.

questions.skill: Identify the problem a model should answer
questions.stem: Rosa wants to know how long it will take to save for a bike. Which of these is the clearest problem for a model to answer?
choices: Why do people like riding bikes more than saving money?
Is a bike a better purchase than a skateboard for everyone?
In how many weeks will my savings reach the 180 dollars the bike costs?
Which kind of bike is the nicest one for a young person?
questions.answer: In how many weeks will my savings reach the 180 dollars the bike costs?
questions.solution: A model needs a question about quantities. Only the first can be answered by calculating how savings grow until they reach the bike's price.

solve.answer: In how many weeks will my savings reach the 180 dollars the bike costs?
solve.work: Only the first is a measurable question a model can answer (weeks until savings reach 180).

questions.skill: Identify the problem a model should answer
questions.stem: Dev wants to build a model of the cost of renting a canoe. What should he do first?
choices: Decide exactly what question the model needs to answer
Check the model's predictions against newly measured data
Revise the equation until it matches his first guess
Tell the class what the finished model shows
questions.answer: Decide exactly what question the model needs to answer
questions.solution: The modeling cycle starts by identifying the problem. Checking, revising and reporting come after a model exists.

solve.answer: Decide exactly what question the model needs to answer
solve.work: The modeling cycle starts by identifying the problem/question.

questions.skill: Name quantities and variables
questions.stem: A model answers the question, "How many days will a 60 pound bag of rice last if a family uses 4 pounds each day?" Which quantity does the question ask for?
choices: The pounds of rice the family uses each day
The 60 pounds of rice in the bag at the start
The pounds of rice left
The number of days the rice lasts
questions.answer: The number of days the rice lasts
questions.solution: The question asks "how many days", so the unknown quantity is the number of days the rice lasts. The 60 and the 4 are given.

solve.answer: The number of days the rice lasts
solve.work: The question asks how many days, so the quantity sought is the number of days (60/4 = 15).

questions.skill: Name quantities and variables
questions.stem: A gym charges 20 dollars to join plus 15 dollars each month. In a model of the total cost $C$ after $m$ months, what does the variable $m$ stand for?
choices: The total cost in dollars
The number of months
The 15 dollar monthly fee
The 20 dollar joining fee
questions.answer: The number of months
questions.solution: The letter $m$ was chosen for months, so it stands for the number of months. The total cost is $C$, and the two fees are fixed numbers.

solve.answer: The number of months

questions.skill: Name quantities and variables
questions.stem: A scooter rental costs 6 dollars to start plus 2 dollars per mile. Which quantity depends on how many miles are ridden?
choices: The 6 dollar starting fee
The total cost of the rental
The 2 dollar price per mile
The color of the scooter
questions.answer: The total cost of the rental
questions.solution: The starting fee and the price per mile are fixed. The total cost changes with the number of miles, so it depends on the miles ridden.

solve.answer: The total cost of the rental
solve.work: Total = 6 + 2(miles) depends on miles; fees are constants.

questions.skill: Identify the assumptions of a model
questions.stem: A model says a puppy gains exactly 2 pounds every week. Which assumption is built into this model?
choices: The puppy's weight doubles every week
The puppy weighs 2 pounds at the moment it is born
The puppy stops gaining after 2 weeks
The puppy gains the same amount each week
questions.answer: The puppy gains the same amount each week
questions.solution: "Exactly 2 pounds every week" means a constant weekly gain. That is the assumption of the model.

solve.answer: The puppy gains the same amount each week
solve.work: Constant gain of 2 lb/week assumes equal weekly gain (linear).

questions.skill: Identify the assumptions of a model
questions.stem: Sam finds the cost of 3 notebooks priced at 2 dollars each by calculating $3 \times 2$. What is he assuming?
choices: Every notebook costs the same price
Notebooks get cheaper when more are bought
A sales tax is added to the total
He plans to buy more than 3 notebooks later
questions.answer: Every notebook costs the same price
questions.solution: Multiplying the number of notebooks by one price only works if every notebook costs that same price.

solve.answer: Every notebook costs the same price
solve.work: 3 x 2 assumes each notebook costs 2 dollars, same price.

questions.skill: Identify the assumptions of a model
questions.stem: A baker says that $b$ batches of cookies make $24b$ cookies. What does this model assume?
choices: Each batch is a little larger than the batch before it
The baker makes exactly 24 batches every single day
Every batch makes the same number of cookies
Every cookie in a batch has exactly the same flavor
questions.answer: Every batch makes the same number of cookies
questions.solution: Multiplying the batches by 24 assumes each batch gives exactly 24 cookies.

solve.answer: Every batch makes the same number of cookies
solve.work: 24b assumes 24 cookies per batch, every batch.

questions.skill: Build a model from a situation or data
questions.stem: A pottery studio charges 30 dollars to register plus 12 dollars for each class. Which equation gives the total cost $C$ after $n$ classes?
questions.solution: The 30 dollar registration is paid once. The 12 dollar fee is paid for each of the $n$ classes, so the total is $30 + 12n$.

questions.skill: Build a model from a situation or data
questions.stem: A video is seen by 3 people on day 0, and the number of viewers doubles every day. Which equation gives the number of viewers $V$ after $d$ days?
choices: $V = 3 \times 2^d$
$V = 2 \times 3^d$
questions.answer: $V = 3 \times 2^d$
questions.solution: Starting at 3 and doubling each day means multiplying by 2 a total of $d$ times: $3 \times 2^d$.

solve.answer: $V = 3 \times 2^d$
solve.work: Starts at 3, doubles daily: V = 3 x 2^d. Check d=0: 3.

questions.skill: Build a model from a situation or data
questions.stem: A pool holds 90 gallons and drains at a steady rate of 6 gallons per minute. The model is $G = 90 - mt$, where $t$ is the time in minutes. What is the value of $m$?
questions.solution: The rate of draining is 6 gallons each minute, so $m = 6$.

questions.skill: Build a model from a situation or data
questions.stem: A population is 4, 8, 16 and 32 at times $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$. The model $y = 4b^x$ fits these values. What is $b$?
questions.solution: Each value is double the one before, so the growth factor is $b = 2$. Check: $4 \times 2^3 = 32$.

questions.skill: Analyse a model to predict or solve
questions.stem: A rain barrel holds 90 liters and loses 5 liters each day. The model $L = 90 - 5d$ gives the liters left after $d$ days. How many liters are left after 7 days?

questions.skill: Analyse a model to predict or solve
questions.stem: The model $P = 25 + 10w$ gives the points $P$ a player has after $w$ weeks of a reading challenge. After how many weeks does the model say a player reaches 125 points?
questions.solution: Solve $25 + 10w = 125$. Subtract 25 to get $10w = 100$, so $w = 10$.

questions.skill: Analyse a model to predict or solve
questions.stem: Use $V = 3 \times 2^d$, the model for the viewers of a video after $d$ days. How many viewers does it predict after 4 days?
questions.solution: Put $d = 4$: $3 \times 2^4 = 3 \times 16 = 48$.

questions.skill: Analyse a model to predict or solve
questions.stem: The model $W = 40t$ gives the words $W$ typed after $t$ minutes. How many minutes does the model say it takes to type 360 words?
questions.solution: Solve $40t = 360$. Divide by 40: $t = 9$.

questions.skill: Analyse a model to predict or solve
questions.stem: The model $y = 3x + 2$ gives the dollars $y$ paid for $x$ sandwiches at 3 dollars each plus a 2 dollar bag fee. How many dollars does the model give for 9 sandwiches?

questions.skill: Test a conjecture or model against data
questions.stem: A model predicts that a bus ride will take 45 minutes. A student times the ride and gets 52 minutes. By how many minutes does the model miss?
questions.solution: Compare the prediction with the measurement: $52 - 45 = 7$ minutes.

questions.skill: Test a conjecture or model against data
questions.stem: A student has a conjecture that a bean plant grows about 3 centimeters each week. Which is the best way to test it?
choices: Measure the plant once after one day and decide that is enough
Ask several friends whether the plant looks like it has grown
Measure only the tallest bean plant that can be found in a store
Measure the plant every week for several weeks and compare with 3 each week
questions.answer: Measure the plant every week for several weeks and compare with 3 each week
questions.solution: A conjecture about weekly growth is tested by measuring over several weeks and comparing with the claimed growth.

solve.answer: Measure the plant every week for several weeks and compare with 3 each week
solve.work: Repeated weekly measurements compared with 3 cm/week test the conjecture.

questions.skill: Test a conjecture or model against data
questions.stem: A model predicts 30 and the measured value is 31. What does this suggest?
choices: The model must be thrown away
The model fits well at this point
The new measurement should simply be ignored
The model's value was too high
questions.answer: The model fits well at this point
questions.solution: The prediction and the measurement differ by only 1, so the model fits well here. The model predicted slightly too low, not too high.

solve.answer: The model fits well at this point
solve.work: 30 vs 31, off by 1: close fit. Model was too low, not too high.

questions.skill: Revise a model
questions.stem: A model's predictions are always exactly 5 too high. Which is a sensible revision?
choices: Raise the model's starting value by an extra 5
Lower the model's starting value by 5
Multiply the model's rate of change by 5
Throw away all of the data
questions.answer: Lower the model's starting value by 5
questions.solution: If every prediction is 5 too high, lowering the starting value by 5 shifts all predictions down to match the measurements.

solve.answer: Lower the model's starting value by 5
solve.work: Constant overestimate of 5: subtract 5 from the starting value.

questions.skill: Revise a model
questions.stem: A student has revised her model after it missed the data. What should she do next?
choices: Stop, because a revised model is always correct now
Delete the measurements that disagree with the model
Change the question the model was built to answer
Test the revised model against the data again
questions.answer: Test the revised model against the data again
questions.solution: A revised model must be tested again, since the revision might not have fixed the problem.

solve.answer: Test the revised model against the data again

questions.skill: Explain what a model's parts mean
questions.stem: In the model $T = 8 + 5h$, $T$ is the dollars a tutor charges for $h$ hours. How many dollars does each extra hour add to the charge?
questions.solution: The number multiplying $h$ is the amount added for each hour. It is 5.

questions.skill: Explain what a model's parts mean
questions.stem: In the model $N = 5 \times 3^t$, $N$ is the number of bacteria after $t$ hours. How many bacteria does the model say there are at the start, when $t = 0$?
questions.solution: Put $t = 0$: $5 \times 3^0 = 5 \times 1 = 5$.

questions.skill: Critique a model and its limits
questions.stem: A model for a sale says $N = 100 - 20d$ items are left after $d$ days. On day 8 it gives $-60$. What does this show?
choices: The model does not make sense for that many days
The store sold 60 items on day 8
The store owes its customers 60 items
The sale lasted exactly 8 days
questions.answer: The model does not make sense for that many days
questions.solution: A store cannot have a negative number of items. The stock runs out at day 5, so the model only applies up to then.

solve.answer: The model does not make sense for that many days
solve.work: 100 - 160 = -60 items is impossible; model domain exceeded (stock runs out at d = 5).

questions.skill: Critique a model and its limits
questions.stem: A model says 7.5 buses are needed for a field trip. What is the fewest buses the school can order so that everyone can go?
questions.solution: You cannot order half a bus, and 7 buses would be too few. Round up to 8.

questions.skill: Choose the model that fits the data
questions.stem: At $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$ the values of $y$ are 5, 7, 9, 11. Which model fits all four values?
choices: $y = 5 \times 2^x$
questions.solution: The value goes up by 2 each time, starting at 5, so $y = 5 + 2x$. Check $x = 3$: $5 + 6 = 11$.

solve.work: Start 5, +2 each step: y = 5 + 2x. Check 5x+2: 2 at x=0 no; 7x-2: -2 no; 5*2^x: 5,10 no.

questions.skill: Choose the model that fits the data
questions.stem: At $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$ the values of $y$ are 81, 27, 9, 3. Which model fits all four values?
choices: $y = 81\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^x$
$y = 81 \times 3^x$
questions.answer: $y = 81\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^x$
questions.solution: Each value is one third of the one before, starting at 81. Check $x = 3$: $81 \times \frac{1}{27} = 3$.

solve.answer: $y = 81\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^x$
solve.work: Ratio 1/3: 81(1/3)^x gives 81,27,9,3. 81-26x gives 55 at x=1; 81-27x gives 54 at x=1; 81*3^x grows.

questions.skill: Order the steps of the modeling cycle
questions.stem: Which list puts these modeling steps in a sensible order? (1) Check predictions against data. (2) Decide what question to answer. (3) Write an equation. (4) Revise the model.
questions.solution: First decide the question (2), then write an equation (3), then check it against data (1), and revise if needed (4).

questions.skill: Order the steps of the modeling cycle
questions.stem: A student reports her model, her assumptions and her results to the class so they can question it. Which part of modeling is this?
choices: Identifying the problem
Choosing the variables
Writing and simplifying the equation
Explaining and defending the model
questions.answer: Explaining and defending the model
questions.solution: Presenting the model, its assumptions and its results so that others can question it is explaining and defending the model.

solve.answer: Explaining and defending the model
solve.work: Reporting to others for questioning = explaining/defending.

questions.skill: Compare a model prediction with observed data
questions.stem: A student models her savings with $S = 40 + 15w$, where $S$ is her savings in dollars after $w$ weeks. After 3 weeks she really has 90 dollars. How many dollars more is her real savings than the model predicts?
questions.solution: The model predicts $S = 40 + 15 \times 3 = 85$ dollars. She really has 90 dollars, which is $90 - 85 = 5$ dollars more.

questions.skill: Critique a model using measured data
questions.stem: A student models a tank that starts with 100 liters and empties at a constant 4 liters per minute: $V = 100 - 4t$. Measurements show 60 liters after 10 minutes and 35 liters after 20 minutes. Which statement is the best critique of the model?
choices: The tank empties faster over time, so the rate should be larger
The model matches at 10 minutes, so it is right at every time
The model is wrong because the tank cannot start with 100 liters
The tank empties more slowly over time, so a constant rate is a poor assumption
questions.answer: The tank empties more slowly over time, so a constant rate is a poor assumption
questions.solution: At 10 minutes the model gives $100 - 40 = 60$ liters, which matches. At 20 minutes it gives $100 - 80 = 20$ liters, but 35 liters were measured. The tank has more water left than predicted, so it empties more slowly as time goes on. Matching at one time does not make a model right everywhere.

solve.answer: The tank empties more slowly over time, so a constant rate is a poor assumption
solve.work: Model: V(10) = 60 (matches), V(20) = 20 but measured 35. Data: lost 40 L in first 10 min (4 L/min), 25 L in next 10 min (2.5 L/min), so draining slows; constant rate is a poor assumption. Option 1 overgeneralizes, option 3 is unsupported, option 4 has the direction wrong.

questions.skill: Use a model to answer a question within a limit
questions.stem: Printing $n$ flyers costs $C = 12 + 0.25n$ dollars. A club has 62 dollars to spend. What is the greatest number of flyers the club can print?
questions.solution: The club can spend at most 62 dollars: $12 + 0.25n \le 62$, so $0.25n \le 50$ and $n \le 200$. The greatest number is 200 flyers.

questions.skill: Identify the problem a model should answer
questions.stem: A school club needs to raise 500 dollars by selling cookies at 2 dollars each. Which is the best question for a model to answer?
choices: Do students enjoy cookies more than they enjoy any other snack?
How many cookies must be sold to reach 500 dollars?
Which flavor of cookie should the club choose to sell at the event?
Is it fair to ask students to buy cookies?
questions.answer: How many cookies must be sold to reach 500 dollars?
questions.solution: Only the first question can be answered by calculating with the given quantities: $500 \div 2 = 250$ cookies.

solve.answer: How many cookies must be sold to reach 500 dollars?

questions.skill: Identify the problem a model should answer
questions.stem: Which question can be answered using a mathematical model?
choices: Is saving money for the future more fun than spending it right away?
How many weeks until saving 15 dollars a week reaches 240 dollars?
Who is the best at saving money among all the students in the class?
Should students be paid an allowance for doing their chores at home?
questions.answer: How many weeks until saving 15 dollars a week reaches 240 dollars?
questions.solution: A model works with quantities. The first question asks for a number of weeks from a rate of saving and a target; the others are matters of opinion or comparison.

solve.answer: How many weeks until saving 15 dollars a week reaches 240 dollars?
solve.work: Only the savings question is quantitative: 240/15 = 16 weeks.

questions.skill: Name quantities and variables
questions.stem: Mia is modeling how many weeks she needs to save for a 300 dollar tablet. She saves 20 dollars a week. Which piece of information is not needed for the model?
choices: The tablet's price
Her saving each week
Her savings so far
The color of the tablet
questions.answer: The color of the tablet
questions.solution: The model needs the price, the weekly saving and the amount saved already. The color has no effect on the number of weeks.

solve.answer: The color of the tablet
solve.work: Color is irrelevant; price, current savings and weekly saving all affect the weeks.

questions.skill: Name quantities and variables
questions.stem: In a model, $d$ is a distance in miles and $t$ is a time in hours. What does $\frac{d}{t}$ represent?
choices: Speed in miles per hour
Time in hours for each mile
Distance in miles
Time in hours
questions.answer: Speed in miles per hour
questions.solution: Distance divided by time is a rate of travel: miles per hour, or speed.

solve.answer: Speed in miles per hour

questions.skill: Identify the assumptions of a model
questions.stem: A model for a trip says the time is $t = \frac{d}{50}$ hours for a distance of $d$ miles. Which real-world factor does this model ignore?
choices: The total length of the trip in miles, which the model uses
The assumed speed of 50 miles per hour on the whole trip
Traffic and stops that slow the average speed
The units of the distance
questions.answer: Traffic and stops that slow the average speed
questions.solution: The model assumes a steady 50 miles per hour, so it ignores anything that changes the speed, such as traffic and stops.

solve.answer: Traffic and stops that slow the average speed
solve.work: d/50 assumes constant 50 mph; ignores traffic and stops. Other options are things the model uses.

questions.skill: Identify the assumptions of a model
questions.stem: A model for a town is $P = 2000(1.05)^t$ people after $t$ years. Which assumption does it make?
choices: The population grows by the same number of people each year
The population stops growing altogether after 5 years
The population grows by the same percent each year
The population falls by 5% of its size every single year
questions.answer: The population grows by the same percent each year
questions.solution: Multiplying by 1.05 each year is growth of 5% of the current population every year, which is a constant percent, not a constant number of people.

solve.answer: The population grows by the same percent each year
solve.work: Factor 1.05 each year: constant percent growth (5%).

questions.skill: Identify the assumptions of a model
questions.stem: Dan models the time to fill a bathtub by assuming the faucet runs at a steady rate. Which event would break this assumption?
choices: The water pressure drops while others use water in the house
The tub turns out to hold more water than expected
Dan fills the tub in the evening instead of the morning
Dan measures the water in liters, not gallons
questions.answer: The water pressure drops while others use water in the house
questions.solution: A change in pressure changes how fast the water flows, so the rate is no longer steady. The other events do not affect the rate.

solve.answer: The water pressure drops while others use water in the house
solve.work: A pressure drop changes flow rate, breaking the steady-rate assumption.

questions.skill: Build a model from a situation or data
questions.stem: A hot tub holds 500 gallons and drains 25 gallons each minute. Which equation gives the gallons $G$ left after $m$ minutes?
questions.solution: The tub starts at 500 gallons and loses 25 gallons for each of the $m$ minutes, so $G = 500 - 25m$.

questions.skill: Build a model from a situation or data
questions.stem: A savings account starts with 800 dollars and earns 3% interest each year. Which equation gives the balance $A$ after $t$ years?
choices: $A = 800 \times 3^t$
questions.solution: Each year the balance is multiplied by 1.03 (100% plus 3%), so after $t$ years it is $800(1.03)^t$.

questions.skill: Build a model from a situation or data
questions.stem: A seedling is 12 centimeters tall at week 0 and 42 centimeters tall at week 5. If it grows by the same amount each week, how many centimeters does it grow per week?
questions.solution: It grows $42 - 12 = 30$ centimeters in 5 weeks, so $30 \div 5 = 6$ centimeters each week.

questions.skill: Build a model from a situation or data
questions.stem: A culture had 80 cells at hour 0, 120 cells at hour 1 and 180 cells at hour 2. The cells grow by the same factor each hour. What is that factor?
questions.solution: Divide each count by the one before: $120 \div 80 = 1.5$ and $180 \div 120 = 1.5$.

questions.skill: Build a model from a situation or data
questions.stem: A farmer has 40 meters of fence for a rectangular pen. If the width is $w$ meters, which equation gives the area $A$ in square meters?
questions.solution: Two widths and two lengths use 40 meters, so width plus length is 20. The length is $20 - w$, and the area is $w(20 - w)$.

questions.skill: Analyse a model to predict or solve
questions.stem: The model $M = 200 \times (0.5)^h$ gives the milligrams of a medicine in the blood $h$ hours after a dose. How many milligrams does it give after 3 hours?

questions.skill: Analyse a model to predict or solve
questions.stem: A baker sells loaves at 4 dollars each. Each loaf costs 1.50 dollars to make. In a model of profit, how many dollars of profit come from selling 40 loaves?
questions.solution: Profit per loaf is $4 - 1.50 = 2.50$ dollars. For 40 loaves: $40 \times 2.50 = 100$ dollars.

questions.skill: Analyse a model to predict or solve
questions.stem: The height of a thrown ball is modeled by $h = -5t^2 + 40t$ meters after $t$ seconds. What height does the model give after 3 seconds, in meters?

questions.skill: Analyse a model to predict or solve
questions.stem: Plan A costs 15 dollars plus 4 dollars per visit. Plan B costs 7 dollars per visit. For how many visits do the two plans cost the same?
questions.solution: Set $15 + 4v = 7v$. Then $15 = 3v$, so $v = 5$. Both plans cost 35 dollars.

questions.skill: Analyse a model to predict or solve
questions.stem: A parking garage charges $P = 3 + 2h$ dollars for $h$ hours. For how many hours can a driver park with 15 dollars?
questions.solution: Solve $3 + 2h = 15$. Then $2h = 12$, so $h = 6$.

questions.skill: Test a conjecture or model against data
questions.stem: The model $P = 12 + 3d$ gives the pages $P$ read after $d$ days. A student has really read 31 pages after 5 days. By how many pages is the real number above the prediction?
questions.solution: The model predicts $12 + 3 \times 5 = 27$ pages. The real number is 31, which is $31 - 27 = 4$ more.

questions.skill: Test a conjecture or model against data
questions.stem: A student claims the values 3, 6, 12, 24 at times 0, 1, 2, 3 follow a linear pattern. Which statement is correct?
choices: The claim is true, because each value is larger than the value before it
The claim is true, because the first two values differ by 3
The claim is false, because the values are all multiples of 3
The claim is false, because the differences 3, 6 and 12 are not equal
questions.answer: The claim is false, because the differences 3, 6 and 12 are not equal
questions.solution: A linear pattern has a constant difference. These differences keep doubling, so the pattern is not linear (it is exponential).

solve.answer: The claim is false, because the differences 3, 6 and 12 are not equal
solve.work: Differences 3, 6, 12 not constant, so not linear.

questions.skill: Test a conjecture or model against data
questions.stem: A model predicts temperatures of 77, 74 and 71 degrees at minutes 1, 2 and 3. The measured temperatures are 77, 73 and 69 degrees. What is the total of the amounts by which the model is too high?
questions.solution: The model is too high by $77 - 77 = 0$, then $74 - 73 = 1$, then $71 - 69 = 2$. The total is $0 + 1 + 2 = 3$ degrees.

questions.skill: Revise a model
questions.stem: A student's straight-line model of a plant's height fit the first 6 weeks, but it overpredicts later as the plant's growth slows. Which revision is best?
choices: Choose a model whose weekly growth gets smaller over time
Make the weekly growth larger so the line climbs faster than before
Remove the later weeks from the data
Keep the straight line, since it fit the first six weeks of data very well
questions.answer: Choose a model whose weekly growth gets smaller over time
questions.solution: The data show growth slowing, which a straight line cannot show. A revised model should let the weekly growth shrink.

solve.answer: Choose a model whose weekly growth gets smaller over time
solve.work: Growth slows, so use a model with decreasing growth rate.

questions.skill: Revise a model
questions.stem: A model $C = 20 + 5h$ gives a charge in dollars for $h$ hours. The real charges are always 3 dollars higher than the model's. What starting value (the constant) should the revised model have?
questions.solution: Adding 3 to every prediction raises the constant from 20 to 23, giving $C = 23 + 5h$.

questions.skill: Revise a model
questions.stem: A sales model $S = 100 + mt$ gives sales after $t$ months. A revised line must start at 100 when $t = 0$ and pass through the real sales of 260 at month 10. What should $m$ be?
questions.solution: The line must rise $260 - 100 = 160$ in 10 months, so $m = 160 \div 10 = 16$.

questions.skill: Explain what a model's parts mean
questions.stem: In the model $N = 250(1.06)^t$, $N$ is the number of members after $t$ years. By what percent does the membership grow each year?
questions.solution: The factor 1.06 means 100% of last year plus 6% more, so the membership grows 6% each year.

questions.skill: Explain what a model's parts mean
questions.stem: The model $h = -5t^2 + 30t$ gives the height in meters of a ball $t$ seconds after it is thrown. At what time $t$ above 0 does the ball return to the ground?
questions.solution: Set $h = 0$: $-5t(t - 6) = 0$, so $t = 0$ or $t = 6$. The ball lands at 6 seconds.

questions.skill: Critique a model and its limits
questions.stem: A model predicts that a bacteria colony will cover the whole planet within 3 years. What best explains the problem?
choices: Bacteria stop reproducing once the first day has passed, so growth ends
The colony shrinks whenever someone measures or counts it
Food and space limit the growth, which the model ignores
Population models must always be linear, never exponential
questions.answer: Food and space limit the growth, which the model ignores
questions.solution: Real colonies run out of food and space, so unlimited growth stops. A model that ignores these limits predicts impossible sizes.

solve.answer: Food and space limit the growth, which the model ignores
solve.work: Unlimited exponential growth ignores limits on food and space.

questions.skill: Critique a model and its limits
questions.stem: A tutor's model says a score is $60 + 5h$ after $h$ hours of study. It gives 110 for 10 hours, but scores cannot exceed 100. What is the best critique?
choices: The model is correct, since more study always adds 5 points
The model should use a negative slope
The model needs an upper limit because scores cannot go above 100
The model fails for any study time above 0 hours
questions.answer: The model needs an upper limit because scores cannot go above 100
questions.solution: The model works for small $h$, but it predicts an impossible score for large $h$, so it must be limited to values that make sense.

solve.answer: The model needs an upper limit because scores cannot go above 100
solve.work: Scores capped at 100; model needs a limit (valid until h = 8).

questions.skill: Choose the model that fits the data
questions.stem: At $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$ the values of $y$ are 2, 6, 18, 54. Which model fits all four values?
questions.solution: Each value is 3 times the one before, starting at 2, so $y = 2(3)^x$. Check $x = 3$: $2 \times 27 = 54$.

solve.work: Ratio 3, start 2: y = 2(3)^x gives 2,6,18,54. 3(2)^x gives 3 at 0; 2+4x gives 6,10; 2x^2+4x gives 0 at 0.

questions.skill: Choose the model that fits the data
questions.stem: At $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$ the values of $y$ are 0, 5, 8, 9. Which model fits all four values?
choices: $y = 5 \times 2^x - 5$
questions.solution: The differences 5, 3, 1 drop by 2 each time, which suggests a quadratic with $-x^2$. Check: $-1 + 6 = 5$, $-4 + 12 = 8$, $-9 + 18 = 9$.

questions.skill: Order the steps of the modeling cycle
questions.stem: A student's model matches the data well. What is the best next step?
choices: Delete the data afterwards so that no one can question or challenge the model
Use the model to answer the original question and state its limits
Start a completely new model
Change the assumptions without testing
questions.answer: Use the model to answer the original question and state its limits
questions.solution: Once a model has been tested and fits, it is used to answer the question it was built for, and its limits are explained.

solve.answer: Use the model to answer the original question and state its limits
solve.work: A good fit: use it to answer the question and report limits.

questions.skill: Choose the model that fits recorded data
questions.stem: A scientist counts bacteria each hour and records 800, 1200, 1800 and 2700 at hours 0, 1, 2 and 3. Which model fits all of these counts?
questions.solution: Each count is 1.5 times the one before: $800 \times 1.5 = 1200$, $1200 \times 1.5 = 1800$, $1800 \times 1.5 = 2700$. So $N = 800(1.5)^t$. The linear model $800 + 400t$ matches only the first two counts (it gives 1600 at hour 2).

questions.skill: Test a model against a dealer value and find the error
questions.stem: A student models the value of a car with $V = 20{,}000(0.8)^t$ dollars after $t$ years, assuming it loses 20% of its value each year. A dealer says the car is worth $10{,}500$ dollars after 3 years. How many dollars more is the dealer's value than the model predicts?
questions.solution: The model predicts $V = 20{,}000(0.8)^3 = 20{,}000 \times 0.512 = 10{,}240$ dollars. The dealer says $10{,}500$, which is $10{,}500 - 10{,}240 = 260$ dollars more.

questions.skill: Judge the limits of a model
questions.stem: A student models the height of a young tree with $h = 2 + 3t$ meters after $t$ years, and uses it to predict a height of 152 meters after 50 years. Which is the best critique of this prediction?
choices: The model assumes steady growth, but trees slow down as they get very tall
The model is invalid because the tree starts above zero height
The prediction is reliable because the formula was worked out correctly
The model is invalid because time is measured in years
questions.answer: The model assumes steady growth, but trees slow down as they get very tall
questions.solution: The model adds 3 meters every year without end, which gives an unrealistic 152 meters. A good critique looks at whether the assumption (constant growth) still makes sense far from the data. The starting height and the unit of time are not problems.

solve.answer: The model assumes steady growth, but trees slow down as they get very tall
solve.work: h(50) = 2 + 150 = 152 m, arithmetically right but unrealistic: a linear model assumes the tree keeps growing 3 m a year forever, while real trees slow down. Units in years and a nonzero start are not flaws; correct arithmetic does not make the extrapolation reliable.

questions.skill: Identify the problem a model should answer
questions.stem: A theater owner wants the ticket price that earns the most money. Each 1 dollar rise in price loses 20 customers. Which question is the most complete problem for her model?
choices: Will customers be happy about a higher ticket price at the theater this year?
Which price earns the most if each 1 dollar rise loses 20 customers?
What is the best possible price for someone to pay for a ticket to the theater?
How many customers came to the theater last year?
questions.answer: Which price earns the most if each 1 dollar rise loses 20 customers?
questions.solution: The first question names the quantity to find (the price), what to optimize (revenue) and the relationship between price and customers.

solve.answer: Which price earns the most if each 1 dollar rise loses 20 customers?
solve.work: Option includes goal and the price-customer relationship.

questions.skill: Identify the problem a model should answer
questions.stem: A town manager wants to know whether the town's water tank will last through a dry summer. Which information should the model builders gather first?
choices: The color of the tank and the age of its paint and fittings
The names and home addresses of all of the town's residents
The price of water in the towns that are nearby, per gallon
The tank's volume, the daily use and how it may change
questions.answer: The tank's volume, the daily use and how it may change
questions.solution: To model how long the supply lasts, they need how much water there is and how fast it is used.

solve.answer: The tank's volume, the daily use and how it may change
solve.work: Tank volume and usage rate (and changes) are the relevant quantities.

questions.skill: Name quantities and variables
questions.stem: Which definition tells a reader exactly what a variable means, including its units?
choices: Let $s$ be Maya's savings in dollars after $w$ weeks
Let $s$ be Maya's savings
Let $s$ be a number of dollars
Let $s$ be the weeks until she has saved enough
questions.answer: Let $s$ be Maya's savings in dollars after $w$ weeks
questions.solution: A clear definition names the quantity, its units and what it depends on. Only the first says whose savings, in what unit, and at what time.

solve.answer: Let $s$ be Maya's savings in dollars after $w$ weeks
solve.issues: Minor: option D also names a unit (weeks) but is vague ("enough"); B is clearly best.
solve.work: Only B names who, what quantity, the unit (dollars) and the dependence on w.

questions.skill: Name quantities and variables
questions.stem: A school trip costs a fixed 300 dollars for the bus plus 7.50 dollars per student for lunch. What is the total cost per student, in dollars, when 40 students go?
questions.solution: The bus cost per student is $300 \div 40 = 7.50$ dollars. Add the lunch: $7.50 + 7.50 = 15$ dollars.

questions.skill: Identify the assumptions of a model
questions.stem: A shop models its weekly sales as $N = 300 - 20p$, where $p$ is the price in dollars. What does the model assume?
choices: Each 1 dollar rise in price raises weekly sales by 20 items
Weekly sales stay at 300 whatever the price is
Each 1 dollar rise in price lowers weekly sales by 20
Each 20 dollar rise in price lowers sales by 1
questions.answer: Each 1 dollar rise in price lowers weekly sales by 20
questions.solution: The coefficient $-20$ means every 1 dollar increase in $p$ lowers $N$ by 20, at every price.

solve.answer: Each 1 dollar rise in price lowers weekly sales by 20
solve.work: Slope -20: each 1 dollar rise lowers sales by 20.

questions.skill: Identify the assumptions of a model
questions.stem: The model $A = 500(1.04)^t$ gives a savings balance after $t$ years. Which assumption must hold for its prediction at year 5 to be accurate?
choices: The balance grows by exactly 4 dollars each year, whatever its size
The balance stops growing after year 4
The 4% rate stays fixed and no money is added or removed
The rate rises by another 4% each year, so the growth keeps speeding up
questions.answer: The 4% rate stays fixed and no money is added or removed
questions.solution: The model multiplies by 1.04 each year, so it needs the same 4% rate every year and no deposits or withdrawals.

solve.answer: The 4% rate stays fixed and no money is added or removed
solve.work: Compound model assumes constant 4% and no deposits/withdrawals.

questions.skill: Build a model from a situation or data
questions.stem: At a price of $p$ dollars, a shop sells $300 - 20p$ items a week. Which equation gives the weekly revenue $R$ in dollars?
questions.solution: Revenue is the price times the number sold: $R = p \times (300 - 20p)$.

questions.skill: Build a model from a situation or data
questions.stem: A fund was worth 500 dollars at the start and 600 dollars one year later. If it keeps growing by the same percent each year, what is it worth after 3 years, in dollars?
questions.solution: The growth factor is $600 \div 500 = 1.2$. After 3 years: $500 \times 1.2^3 = 500 \times 1.728 = 864$ dollars.

questions.skill: Build a model from a situation or data
questions.stem: A kayak rental costs 22 dollars for 2 hours and 34 dollars for 4 hours, and the cost is linear in the number of hours. What would 7 hours cost, in dollars?
questions.solution: The cost rises $34 - 22 = 12$ dollars for 2 extra hours, so 6 dollars per hour. From 2 to 7 hours is 5 more hours: $22 + 6 \times 5 = 52$ dollars.

questions.skill: Build a model from a situation or data
questions.stem: Sam has 50 dollars and saves 8 dollars a week. Lia has 20 dollars and saves 14 dollars a week. Which equation can be solved to find the number of weeks $w$ until they have the same amount?
questions.solution: Sam has $50 + 8w$ after $w$ weeks and Lia has $20 + 14w$. They have the same amount when these are equal.

questions.skill: Analyse a model to predict or solve
questions.stem: Pool A holds 400 liters and fills at 30 liters a minute. Pool B holds 700 liters and drains at 20 liters a minute. After how many minutes do the two pools hold the same amount?
questions.solution: Set $400 + 30m = 700 - 20m$. Then $50m = 300$, so $m = 6$. Both pools then hold 580 liters.

questions.skill: Analyse a model to predict or solve
questions.stem: A shop's weekly revenue is modeled by $R = p(300 - 20p)$ dollars at a price of $p$ dollars. What revenue does the model give at $p = 6$, in dollars?

questions.skill: Analyse a model to predict or solve
questions.stem: The height of a thrown ball is modeled by $h = -5t^2 + 20t + 1$ meters after $t$ seconds. What is the greatest height the model gives, in meters?
questions.solution: For $-5t^2 + 20t + 1$ the greatest value is at $t = \frac{-20}{2 \times (-5)} = 2$ seconds. Then $h = -5 \times 4 + 40 + 1 = 21$.

questions.skill: Analyse a model to predict or solve
questions.stem: A culture is modeled by $N = 40 \times 2^t$ cells after $t$ hours. After how many whole hours does the model first exceed 1000 cells?
questions.solution: At $t = 4$ the model gives $40 \times 16 = 640$, which is not above 1000. At $t = 5$ it gives $40 \times 32 = 1280$, which is. So $t = 5$.

questions.skill: Analyse a model to predict or solve
questions.stem: A club has 120 dollars to spend on a hall. The hall costs 35 dollars plus 8.50 dollars per guest. What is the greatest number of guests the club can afford?
questions.solution: Solve $35 + 8.50g \le 120$. Then $8.50g \le 85$, so $g \le 10$.

questions.skill: Analyse a model to predict or solve
questions.stem: Using $A = 500(1.04)^t$ for a savings balance, what balance does the model give after 2 years, in dollars?

questions.skill: Test a conjecture or model against data
questions.stem: A student conjectures that $y = 3x + 5$. The data points are (1, 8), (2, 11) and (3, 15). Which statement is true?
choices: It fits all three of the points (1, 8), (2, 11) and (3, 15)
It fits (1, 8) and (2, 11) but not (3, 15)
It fits (3, 15) but neither of the other two
It fits none of the three points (1, 8), (2, 11) or (3, 15)
questions.answer: It fits (1, 8) and (2, 11) but not (3, 15)
questions.solution: At $x = 1$: 8. At $x = 2$: 11. At $x = 3$ the conjecture gives 14, not 15. So one point is a counterexample.

solve.answer: It fits (1, 8) and (2, 11) but not (3, 15)

questions.skill: Test a conjecture or model against data
questions.stem: A model $N = 10 \times 3^t$ predicts counts at hours 1, 2 and 3. The measured counts are 30, 80 and 250. What is the total amount by which the model's predictions are too high?
questions.solution: The predictions are 30, 90 and 270. The differences are $30 - 30 = 0$, $90 - 80 = 10$ and $270 - 250 = 20$. The total is 30.

questions.skill: Revise a model
questions.stem: A caterer's model is $C = 12 + 4n$ dollars for $n$ guests. At 10 guests the real cost was 58 dollars. Keeping the starting value 12, what slope would make the revised model match that real cost?
questions.solution: The revised line must rise $58 - 12 = 46$ over 10 guests, so the slope is $46 \div 10 = 4.6$.

questions.skill: Revise a model
questions.stem: A hot drink's temperature is modeled by a straight line falling 2 degrees each minute, so it eventually predicts temperatures below the room's. Which revision is best?
choices: Make the line steeper so that it falls even faster
Use a model in which the drink levels off near room temperature
Stop measuring after 10 minutes so the problem never shows
Assume the room is colder than it really is
questions.answer: Use a model in which the drink levels off near room temperature
questions.solution: A cooling drink cannot get colder than the room around it, so a good revision has the temperature leveling off near the room's temperature.

solve.answer: Use a model in which the drink levels off near room temperature
solve.work: Cooling levels off at room temperature; use a model that approaches it.

questions.skill: Revise a model
questions.stem: A model $y = 100b^t$ gives the milligrams of medicine left after $t$ hours. The measured amount at $t = 2$ is 64 milligrams. What value of $b$, with $0 < b < 1$, makes the model match?

questions.skill: Explain what a model's parts mean
questions.stem: The revenue model is $R = p(300 - 20p)$ dollars for a ticket price of $p$ dollars. At what price above 0 is the revenue 0?
questions.solution: $R = 0$ when $300 - 20p = 0$. Then $p = 15$: at that price nobody buys a ticket, so the revenue is 0.

questions.skill: Explain what a model's parts mean
questions.stem: In the model $y = 100(0.8)^t$, by what percent does $y$ decrease each period?
questions.solution: Multiplying by 0.8 keeps 80% of the previous value, so it decreases by $100 - 80 = 20$ percent each period.

questions.skill: Explain what a model's parts mean
questions.stem: The model $T = 20 + 60(0.5)^m$ gives a drink's temperature in degrees $m$ minutes after it is poured. What does the 20 represent?
choices: The temperature of the drink at the moment when it is poured
The number of minutes the drink takes to cool
The degrees the drink loses each minute
The temperature the drink approaches as time passes
questions.answer: The temperature the drink approaches as time passes
questions.solution: As $m$ grows, $(0.5)^m$ gets close to 0, so $T$ gets close to 20. That is the temperature of the surroundings. At $m = 0$ the drink is at $20 + 60 = 80$ degrees.

solve.answer: The temperature the drink approaches as time passes
solve.work: As m grows, 60(0.5)^m -> 0, T -> 20: the level it approaches (room temp). At m=0 T=80.

questions.skill: Critique a model and its limits
questions.stem: The model $h = -5t^2 + 20t + 1$ gives $h = -24$ at $t = 5$. What is the best critique of this result?
choices: The ball has landed, so the model does not apply at that time
The ball is 24 meters below the ground at that time, still falling
The model is correct for every value of $t$ that anyone could choose
The ball is still rising at that time
questions.answer: The ball has landed, so the model does not apply at that time
questions.solution: A negative height would mean below the ground. The ball lands before $t = 5$, so the model only applies until then.

solve.answer: The ball has landed, so the model does not apply at that time
solve.work: Roots of -5t^2 + 20t + 1 = 0 near t = 4.05; at t = 5 the ball has landed; negative height meaningless.

questions.skill: Critique a model and its limits
questions.stem: A model fits monthly data and shows ice cream sales and swimming accidents rising together. A student concludes that ice cream sales cause the accidents. What is the best critique?
choices: The model is wrong because it compares two different quantities at once
Ice cream sales must cause the accidents, since the data fit so well
Both rise in hot weather, so the data show a link, not a cause
The model should only compare the months in which there were no accidents
questions.answer: Both rise in hot weather, so the data show a link, not a cause
questions.solution: A model can fit data that rise together without one causing the other. A third factor, hot weather, raises both.

solve.answer: Both rise in hot weather, so the data show a link, not a cause
solve.work: Correlation from a common cause (hot weather), not causation.

questions.skill: Critique a model and its limits
questions.stem: A model for future sales is built only from three unusually good months. What is the best critique?
choices: It uses too few operations
It must be accurate, because the months were good
It uses data that are not typical, so it will probably overpredict
It cannot be used because sales are positive
questions.answer: It uses data that are not typical, so it will probably overpredict
questions.solution: A model is only as good as the data it is built from. Unusually good months make predictions too high for typical months.

solve.answer: It uses data that are not typical, so it will probably overpredict
solve.work: Unrepresentative good months bias predictions high.

questions.skill: Choose the model that fits the data
questions.stem: The values 2, 3, 6 and 11 occur at $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$ and follow a quadratic pattern. What is the next value, at $x = 4$?
questions.solution: The differences are 1, 3, 5, which grow by 2 each time. The next difference is 7, so the next value is $11 + 7 = 18$. (This is $y = x^2 + 2$.)

questions.skill: Choose the model that fits the data
questions.stem: The values 80, 72 and 64.8 occur at $x = 0, 1, 2$ and follow an exponential pattern. What is the value at $x = 3$?
questions.solution: Each value is 0.9 times the one before ($72 \div 80 = 0.9$ and $64.8 \div 72 = 0.9$). Next: $64.8 \times 0.9 = 58.32$.

questions.skill: Order the steps of the modeling cycle
questions.stem: A student built a model, tested it, found it too high, revised it, and tested it again. What does this show about modeling?
choices: Modeling is a cycle that repeats until the model is good enough
The first model is always right
Testing is needed only once
Revising a model means starting again from nothing every single time
questions.answer: Modeling is a cycle that repeats until the model is good enough
questions.solution: Modeling is a cycle: build, test, revise, test again. Each pass improves the model until it fits well enough to use.

solve.answer: Modeling is a cycle that repeats until the model is good enough
solve.work: Build, test, revise, test again: a cycle.

questions.skill: Multiply powers with the same base
questions.stem: Simplify $x^3 \cdot x^4$.
questions.solution: When you multiply powers with the same base, add the exponents: $x^3 \cdot x^4 = x^{3+4} = x^7$.

solve.work: Same base, add exponents: x^(3+4) = x^7.

questions.skill: Evaluate zero and positive integer exponents
questions.stem: What is the value of $5^0 + 3^2$?
questions.solution: Any nonzero number to the power 0 is 1, so $5^0 = 1$. Also $3^2 = 9$. The sum is $1 + 9 = 10$.

questions.skill: Add polynomials by combining like terms
questions.stem: Add $(4x^2 + 3x + 1) + (x^2 + 6x + 5)$. What is the coefficient of $x$ in the sum?
questions.solution: Combine like terms: $(4x^2 + x^2) + (3x + 6x) + (1 + 5) = 5x^2 + 9x + 6$. The coefficient of $x$ is 9.

questions.skill: Multiply powers with the same base
questions.stem: The product $3^{4} \cdot 3^{2}$ is equal to $3^{n}$. What is the value of $n$?
questions.solution: When you multiply powers with the same base, you add the exponents: $3^{4} \cdot 3^{2} = 3^{4+2} = 3^{6}$. So $n = 6$.

solve.work: Same base, add exponents: 3^4 * 3^2 = 3^(4+2) = 3^6, so n = 6.

questions.skill: Multiply powers with the same base
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $y^{5} \cdot y^{3}$?
questions.solution: Multiplying powers with the same base means adding the exponents: $y^{5} \cdot y^{3} = y^{5+3} = y^{8}$. Multiplying the exponents (15) or subtracting them (2) are common mistakes.

solve.work: y^5 * y^3 = y^(5+3) = y^8. Distractors: y^15 multiplies exponents, 2y^8 adds coefficients wrongly, y^2 subtracts.

questions.skill: Divide powers with the same base
questions.stem: Complete the equation $\frac{7^{9}}{7^{4}} = 7^{n}$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: When you divide powers with the same base, you subtract the exponents: $\frac{7^{9}}{7^{4}} = 7^{9-4} = 7^{5}$. So $n = 5$.

questions.skill: Divide powers with the same base
questions.stem: Simplify $\frac{x^{10}}{x^{6}}$, where $x$ is not zero.
questions.solution: Subtract the exponent in the bottom from the exponent in the top: $10 - 6 = 4$. So $\frac{x^{10}}{x^{6}} = x^{4}$.

questions.skill: Raise a power to a power
questions.stem: The expression $(4^{2})^{3}$ equals $4^{k}$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: To raise a power to a power, multiply the exponents: $(4^{2})^{3} = 4^{2 \times 3} = 4^{6}$. So $k = 6$.

questions.skill: Raise a power to a power
questions.stem: Simplify $(x^{4})^{2}$.
questions.solution: Multiply the exponents: $4 \times 2 = 8$. So $(x^{4})^{2} = x^{8}$. Adding the exponents (6) is a different rule, for multiplying powers.

questions.skill: Raise a product or quotient to a power
questions.stem: Simplify $(xy)^{3}$.
choices: $3xy$
questions.solution: A power of a product is the product of the powers: $(xy)^{3} = x^{3}y^{3}$. Both factors get the exponent 3.

solve.work: Power of a product: (xy)^3 = x^3 y^3.

questions.skill: Raise a product or quotient to a power
questions.stem: The expression $(2x)^{3}$ can be written as $kx^{3}$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: The exponent applies to both the 2 and the $x$: $(2x)^{3} = 2^{3}x^{3} = 8x^{3}$. So $k = 8$. (It is not $2 \times 3 = 6$.)

questions.skill: Zero and negative exponents
questions.stem: What is the value of $(-4)^{0}$?
questions.solution: Any nonzero number raised to the power 0 equals 1. So $(-4)^{0} = 1$.

solve.work: Any nonzero number to the power 0 is 1: (-4)^0 = 1.

questions.skill: Zero and negative exponents
questions.stem: Which number is equal to $2^{-3}$?
questions.solution: A negative exponent means a reciprocal: $2^{-3} = \frac{1}{2^{3}} = \frac{1}{8}$. It is not negative, and it is not $2 \times 3$.

questions.skill: Zero and negative exponents
questions.stem: If $5^{-2}$ is written as the fraction $\frac{1}{n}$, what is $n$?

questions.skill: Combine several exponent properties
questions.stem: Write $\frac{2^{5} \cdot 2^{3}}{2^{4}}$ as a single power of 2. What exponent does it have?
questions.solution: Add the exponents in the top: $5 + 3 = 8$, so the top is $2^{8}$. Then divide by $2^{4}$ by subtracting: $8 - 4 = 4$. The result is $2^{4}$, so the exponent is 4.

questions.skill: Compare polynomial and integer operations
questions.stem: Adding two integers always gives an integer. Which statement about adding two polynomials is true?
choices: The sum is always an integer
The sum is a polynomial only if both have the same degree
The sum always has a greater degree than either polynomial
The sum is always a polynomial
questions.answer: The sum is always a polynomial
questions.solution: Polynomials are closed under addition, just as integers are: adding two polynomials always gives a polynomial. It need not be an integer, and the degree of the sum can be the same or even lower (for example, $x^{2} + (-x^{2} + 1) = 1$).

solve.answer: The sum is always a polynomial
solve.work: Polynomials are closed under addition, like integers: the sum of two polynomials is always a polynomial. Not always an integer; degrees need not match; degree can stay the same or drop.

questions.skill: Compare polynomial and integer operations
questions.stem: Place value connects whole numbers and polynomials. If $x = 10$, the polynomial $3x^{2} + 4x + 5$ names a whole number. What is that number?
questions.solution: With $x = 10$: $3x^{2} + 4x + 5 = 3 \times 100 + 4 \times 10 + 5 = 300 + 40 + 5 = 345$. The coefficients are the digits of the number.

questions.skill: Add polynomials
questions.solution: Add the $x$ terms: $2x + 4x = 6x$. Add the constants: $5 + 3 = 8$. The sum is $6x + 8$. The $x$ terms and the constants are different kinds of terms, so they stay separate.

questions.skill: Add polynomials
questions.stem: Two boards are laid end to end. One is $(2x + 1)$ feet long and the other is $(5x + 3)$ feet long. Together they are $ax + b$ feet long. What is $a + b$?
questions.solution: Total length: $(2x + 1) + (5x + 3) = 7x + 4$. So $a = 7$ and $b = 4$, and $a + b = 11$.

questions.skill: Subtract polynomials
questions.stem: Subtract: $(6x + 9) - (2x + 4)$.
questions.solution: Subtract each term of the second polynomial: $6x - 2x = 4x$ and $9 - 4 = 5$. The result is $4x + 5$.

questions.skill: Subtract polynomials
questions.stem: A tank holds $(8x + 15)$ liters of water. Then $(3x + 6)$ liters are used. The water left is $ax + b$ liters. What is $b$?

questions.skill: Multiply a monomial by a polynomial
questions.stem: When $5(2x + 3)$ is written as $ax + b$, what is $a + b$?
questions.solution: Distribute the 5: $5(2x + 3) = 10x + 15$. So $a = 10$ and $b = 15$, and $a + b = 25$.

questions.skill: Multiply a monomial by a polynomial
questions.stem: Expand: $x(x + 7)$.
questions.solution: Multiply $x$ by each term: $x \cdot x = x^{2}$ and $x \cdot 7 = 7x$. The result is $x^{2} + 7x$.

questions.skill: Multiply a monomial by a polynomial
questions.stem: A rectangle is 4 feet wide and $(x + 9)$ feet long. Its area is $4x + c$ square feet. What is $c$?
questions.solution: Area is width times length: $4(x + 9) = 4x + 36$. So $c = 36$.

questions.skill: Multiply two binomials
questions.stem: Multiply: $(x + 2)(x + 5)$.
questions.solution: Multiply each term of the first by each term of the second: $x \cdot x = x^{2}$, $x \cdot 5 = 5x$, $2 \cdot x = 2x$, $2 \cdot 5 = 10$. Combine the $x$ terms: $5x + 2x = 7x$. The product is $x^{2} + 7x + 10$.

questions.skill: Multiply two binomials
questions.stem: When $(x + 3)(x + 4)$ is multiplied out as $x^{2} + bx + c$, what is $b$?

questions.skill: Multiply two binomials
questions.stem: Multiply: $(y + 6)(y + 1)$.
questions.solution: $y \cdot y = y^{2}$, $y \cdot 1 = y$, $6 \cdot y = 6y$, $6 \cdot 1 = 6$. Combine: $y + 6y = 7y$. The product is $y^{2} + 7y + 6$.

questions.skill: Square a binomial or multiply conjugates
questions.stem: Multiply: $(x + 4)(x - 4)$.
questions.solution: $x \cdot x = x^{2}$; $x \cdot (-4) = -4x$; $4 \cdot x = 4x$; $4 \cdot (-4) = -16$. The $x$ terms cancel: $-4x + 4x = 0$. The product is $x^{2} - 16$.

questions.skill: Area model for a product
questions.stem: A rectangle has width $x + 1$ and length $x + 4$. It is cut into four smaller rectangles with areas $x^{2}$, $4x$, $x$ and $c$. What is $c$?
questions.solution: The small rectangle with sides 1 and 4 has area $1 \times 4 = 4$. So $c = 4$.

questions.skill: Area model for a product
questions.stem: An area model for $(x + 3)(x + 2)$ has four parts with areas $x^{2}$, $2x$, $3x$ and $6$. What is the total area?
questions.solution: Add the four areas: $x^{2} + 2x + 3x + 6$. Combine the two $x$ parts: $2x + 3x = 5x$. The total area is $x^{2} + 5x + 6$.

questions.skill: Rewrite an expression in an equivalent form
questions.stem: When $x^{2} + 3x + 5x$ is written with like terms combined, it is $x^{2} + bx$. What is $b$?
questions.solution: The terms $3x$ and $5x$ are like terms, so $3x + 5x = 8x$. The expression is $x^{2} + 8x$, so $b = 8$.

questions.skill: Rewrite an expression in an equivalent form
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $4(x + 1) - 4$?
questions.solution: Distribute the 4: $4(x + 1) = 4x + 4$. Then subtract 4: $4x + 4 - 4 = 4x$.

questions.skill: Rewrite an expression in an equivalent form
questions.stem: The expression $5(x + 2) - 3x$ is equivalent to $2x + k$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: Distribute the 5: $5x + 10 - 3x$. Combine the $x$ terms: $5x - 3x = 2x$. So the expression is $2x + 10$ and $k = 10$.

questions.skill: Subtract polynomials, distributing the negative
questions.solution: Subtracting changes the sign of every term in the second polynomial: $5x^2 + 3x - 4 - 2x^2 + x - 6$. Combine like terms: $3x^2 + 4x - 10$.

questions.skill: Multiply two binomials
questions.stem: Multiply: $(x + 4)(x - 2)$.
questions.solution: Multiply each term by each term: $x \cdot x + x(-2) + 4 \cdot x + 4(-2) = x^2 - 2x + 4x - 8 = x^2 + 2x - 8$.

questions.skill: Use an area model for a product
questions.stem: A rectangle has width $x + 2$ and length $x + 6$. Cutting it into four smaller rectangles gives areas $x^2$, $6x$, $2x$ and 12. The total area is $x^2 + bx + c$. What is $b$?
questions.solution: The four parts add to $x^2 + 6x + 2x + 12 = x^2 + 8x + 12$. So $b = 8$.

solve.work: (x + 2)(x + 6) = x^2 + 6x + 2x + 12 = x^2 + 8x + 12, matching the four pieces. b = 8.

questions.skill: Multiply powers with the same base
questions.stem: Find the value of $n$ that makes this statement true for every $a$: $a^{n} \cdot a^{7} = a^{12}$.
questions.solution: The exponents add when the bases are the same, so $n + 7 = 12$. Then $n = 12 - 7 = 5$. Check: $a^{5} \cdot a^{7} = a^{12}$.

solve.work: a^n * a^7 = a^(n+7) = a^12 for every a, so n + 7 = 12, n = 5. (a = 0 also checks: 0 = 0.)

questions.skill: Multiply powers with the same base
questions.solution: Multiply the coefficients: $-2 \times 5 = -10$. Add the exponents of $x$: $3 + 4 = 7$. The product is $-10x^{7}$.

solve.work: Coefficients: (-2)(5) = -10. Powers: x^3 * x^4 = x^7. Product -10x^7.

questions.skill: Divide powers with the same base
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $\frac{12a^{7}}{3a^{2}}$, for $a \neq 0$?
questions.solution: Divide the coefficients: $12 \div 3 = 4$. Subtract the exponents: $7 - 2 = 5$. The result is $4a^{5}$.

questions.skill: Divide powers with the same base
questions.stem: Priya writes $\frac{3^{8}}{3^{5}}$ as a whole number. What number does she write?
questions.solution: Subtract the exponents: $\frac{3^{8}}{3^{5}} = 3^{8-5} = 3^{3}$. Then $3^{3} = 3 \times 3 \times 3 = 27$.

questions.skill: Raise a power to a power
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $(a^{-2})^{3}$, for $a \neq 0$?
questions.solution: Multiply the exponents: $(-2) \times 3 = -6$, so the expression is $a^{-6}$. A negative exponent means a reciprocal, so $a^{-6} = \frac{1}{a^{6}}$.

questions.skill: Raise a power to a power
questions.stem: For what value of $m$ is $(y^{m})^{4}$ equal to $y^{20}$ for every nonzero $y$?
questions.solution: Multiply the exponents: $(y^{m})^{4} = y^{4m}$. This must equal $y^{20}$, so $4m = 20$ and $m = 5$.

solve.work: (y^m)^4 = y^(4m) = y^20 for every nonzero y, so 4m = 20, m = 5.

questions.skill: Raise a product or quotient to a power
questions.solution: Raise each factor to the 4th power. $(-2)^{4} = 16$, because an even power of a negative number is positive. $(a^{3})^{4} = a^{12}$ and $(b^{2})^{4} = b^{8}$. The result is $16a^{12}b^{8}$.

solve.work: (-2)^4 = 16; (a^3)^4 = a^12; (b^2)^4 = b^8. Result 16a^12b^8 (even power makes it positive).

questions.skill: Raise a product or quotient to a power
questions.stem: Write the value of $\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{3}$ as a fraction.
questions.solution: A power of a quotient is the quotient of the powers: $\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{3} = \frac{2^{3}}{3^{3}} = \frac{8}{27}$.

questions.skill: Zero and negative exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $\frac{3}{x^{4}}$, for $x \neq 0$?
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{x^{4}} = x^{-4}$, so $\frac{3}{x^{4}} = 3 \cdot x^{-4} = 3x^{-4}$. The 3 is not part of the power: in $(3x)^{-4}$ the 3 would be raised to the power too.

questions.skill: Zero and negative exponents
questions.stem: What is the value of $\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{-3}$?
questions.solution: A negative exponent flips the fraction: $\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{-3} = \left(\frac{2}{1}\right)^{3} = 2^{3} = 8$.

questions.skill: Combine several exponent properties
questions.stem: Which statement is true for every nonzero $x$?

solve.work: x^8/x^2 = x^6 (not x^4); (x^2)^4 = x^8 (not x^6); (x^-2)^-3 = x^6 TRUE; x^2*x^4 = x^6 (not x^8). Only the third is true.

questions.skill: Combine several exponent properties
questions.stem: What is the value of $\frac{(3^{2})^{3}}{3^{4}}$?

questions.skill: Compare polynomial and integer operations
questions.stem: Polynomials and integers are alike in some ways and different in others. Which statement about dividing one polynomial by another is correct?
choices: The quotient is always a polynomial, just as the quotient of two integers is always an integer
The quotient is always a polynomial, even though the quotient of two integers is not always an integer
The quotient is not always a polynomial, just as the quotient of two integers is not always an integer
The quotient is never a polynomial, but the quotient of two integers is always an integer
questions.answer: The quotient is not always a polynomial, just as the quotient of two integers is not always an integer
questions.solution: Integers are closed under adding, subtracting and multiplying, but not dividing: $1 \div 2$ is not an integer. Polynomials behave the same way: $1 \div x$ is not a polynomial. So division does not always give a polynomial.

solve.answer: The quotient is not always a polynomial, just as the quotient of two integers is not always an integer
solve.work: Neither polynomials nor integers are closed under division: e.g. 1/x is not a polynomial and 1/2 is not an integer. So the first option.

questions.skill: Compare polynomial and integer operations
questions.stem: Let $x = 10$. Then $(x+2)(x+3)$ matches the product $12 \times 13$. Multiplying the polynomials gives $x^{2} + 5x + 6$. What is the value of $x^{2} + 5x + 6$ when $x = 10$?
questions.solution: With $x = 10$: $x^{2} + 5x + 6 = 100 + 50 + 6 = 156$. This agrees with $12 \times 13 = 156$, which shows that multiplying polynomials follows the same pattern as multiplying whole numbers.

questions.skill: Compare polynomial and integer operations
questions.stem: Which operation on two polynomials can give a result that is not a polynomial?
choices: Addition
Subtraction
Multiplication
Division
questions.answer: Division
questions.solution: The sum, difference and product of two polynomials are always polynomials. A quotient is not always one: $1 \div x$ is not a polynomial.

solve.answer: Division
solve.work: Addition, subtraction and multiplication of polynomials always give polynomials; division can give e.g. x/x^2 = 1/x, not a polynomial.

questions.skill: Add polynomials
Add polynomials
questions.stem: The sum $(4x^{2} + 3x - 8) + (x^{2} - 9x + 5)$ is written as $ax^{2} + bx + c$. What is $a + b + c$?

questions.skill: Subtract polynomials
questions.solution: Distribute the minus sign to every term of the second polynomial: $4x^{2} - 7x + 2 - 6x^{2} - 3x + 5$. Combine like terms: $4x^{2} - 6x^{2} = -2x^{2}$; $-7x - 3x = -10x$; $2 + 5 = 7$. The result is $-2x^{2} - 10x + 7$.

questions.skill: Subtract polynomials
questions.stem: Subtract $(3x^{2} + 2x - 9)$ from $(8x^{2} - x + 4)$. The result is $ax^{2} + bx + c$. What is $c$?
questions.solution: Subtracting from means: $(8x^{2} - x + 4) - (3x^{2} + 2x - 9) = 5x^{2} - 3x + 13$. The constant is $4 - (-9) = 13$, so $c = 13$.

questions.skill: Multiply a monomial by a polynomial
questions.solution: Multiply $-2x$ by each term: $-2x \cdot 3x^{2} = -6x^{3}$; $-2x \cdot (-4x) = 8x^{2}$; $-2x \cdot 5 = -10x$. The result is $-6x^{3} + 8x^{2} - 10x$.

questions.skill: Multiply a monomial by a polynomial
questions.stem: When $3x(2x^{2} + x - 4)$ is expanded, what is the coefficient of the $x$ term?
questions.solution: Multiply $3x$ by each term: $3x \cdot 2x^{2} = 6x^{3}$; $3x \cdot x = 3x^{2}$; $3x \cdot (-4) = -12x$. The $x$ term is $-12x$, so its coefficient is $-12$.

questions.skill: Multiply two binomials
questions.stem: Multiply: $(2x - 3)(x + 5)$.
questions.solution: $2x \cdot x = 2x^{2}$; $2x \cdot 5 = 10x$; $-3 \cdot x = -3x$; $-3 \cdot 5 = -15$. Combine: $10x - 3x = 7x$. The product is $2x^{2} + 7x - 15$.

questions.skill: Multiply two binomials
questions.stem: What is the coefficient of $x$ in the product $(3x - 2)(2x - 5)$?
questions.solution: The $x$ terms come from $3x \cdot (-5) = -15x$ and $-2 \cdot 2x = -4x$. Together they make $-19x$, so the coefficient is $-19$. (The full product is $6x^{2} - 19x + 10$.)

questions.skill: Square a binomial or multiply conjugates
questions.solution: $(x + 5)^{2} = (x + 5)(x + 5)$. Then $x \cdot x = x^{2}$, $x \cdot 5 + 5 \cdot x = 10x$ and $5 \cdot 5 = 25$. The result is $x^{2} + 10x + 25$. The middle term is easy to forget.

questions.skill: Square a binomial or multiply conjugates
questions.stem: When $(3x - 2)^{2}$ is expanded as $ax^{2} + bx + c$, what is $b$?

questions.skill: Multiply a binomial by a trinomial, or three factors
questions.solution: Multiply every term of the trinomial by $x$: $x^{3} - 3x^{2} + x$. Then by 2: $2x^{2} - 6x + 2$. Add and combine like terms: $x^{3} + (-3x^{2} + 2x^{2}) + (x - 6x) + 2 = x^{3} - x^{2} - 5x + 2$.

questions.skill: Area model for a product
questions.stem: An area model for $(2x + 3)(x + 4)$ has four parts. Which list gives the four areas?
questions.solution: Multiply each side of the first factor by each side of the second: $2x \cdot x = 2x^{2}$; $2x \cdot 4 = 8x$; $3 \cdot x = 3x$; $3 \cdot 4 = 12$. The areas are $2x^{2}$, $8x$, $3x$ and $12$.

questions.skill: Area model for a product
questions.stem: A rectangle is $2x + 1$ units long and $x + 3$ units wide. An area model gives its area as $2x^{2} + 7x + 3$ square units. How many square units is the area when $x = 4$?
questions.solution: Put $x = 4$ into the area: $2(16) + 7(4) + 3 = 32 + 28 + 3 = 63$. Check: the sides are $9$ and $7$, and $9 \times 7 = 63$.

questions.skill: Rewrite an expression in an equivalent form
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $3(x + 2) + 2x$?
questions.solution: Distribute the 3: $3x + 6 + 2x$. Combine the $x$ terms: $3x + 2x = 5x$. The expression is $5x + 6$.

questions.skill: Rewrite an expression in an equivalent form
questions.stem: The expressions $(x + 4)^{2}$ and $x^{2} + 16$ are not equivalent, but they give the same result for one of the values of $x$ below. Which value is it?
questions.solution: Try each value. At $x = 0$ both give 16. At $x = -4$ they give 0 and 32. At $x = 1$ they give 25 and 17. At $x = 2$ they give 36 and 20. The expressions differ in general because $(x + 4)^{2} = x^{2} + 8x + 16$, which has an extra $8x$ that is zero only at $x = 0$.

solve.work: (x + 4)^2 = x^2 + 8x + 16; equal to x^2 + 16 only when 8x = 0, x = 0. Check: x=1: 25 vs 17; x=2: 36 vs 20; x=-4: 0 vs 32.

questions.skill: Divide powers with negative exponents
questions.stem: Simplify $\frac{x^5 y^{-2}}{x^2 y^{-6}}$, where $x$ and $y$ are not zero.
questions.solution: When you divide powers with the same base, subtract the exponents. For $x$: $5 - 2 = 3$. For $y$: $-2 - (-6) = -2 + 6 = 4$. The result is $x^3 y^4$.

questions.skill: Find a coefficient after multiplying binomials
questions.stem: When $(2x - 1)(x + 4)$ is written in the form $ax^2 + bx + c$, what is $b$?
questions.solution: $(2x - 1)(x + 4) = 2x^2 + 8x - x - 4 = 2x^2 + 7x - 4$. The middle terms $8x$ and $-x$ combine to $7x$, so $b = 7$.

questions.skill: Raise a product to a power
questions.stem: Simplify $(3x^2 y)^3$.
questions.solution: Cube every factor: $3^3 = 27$, $(x^2)^3 = x^6$ (multiply exponents) and $y^3$. The result is $27x^6y^3$.

questions.skill: Multiply powers with the same base
questions.stem: Simplify $(2a^{-2}b^{3})(6a^{5}b^{-1})$, where $a$ and $b$ are not zero.
questions.solution: Multiply the coefficients: $2 \times 6 = 12$. For $a$, add the exponents: $-2 + 5 = 3$. For $b$, add the exponents: $3 + (-1) = 2$. The product is $12a^{3}b^{2}$.

questions.skill: Multiply powers with the same base
questions.solution: Add the exponents on the left: $n + (-2) + 4 = n + 2$. This must equal 9, so $n = 9 - 2 = 7$. Check: $5^{7} \cdot 5^{-2} \cdot 5^{4} = 5^{9}$.

questions.skill: Divide powers with the same base
questions.stem: What is the value of $\frac{2^{3} \cdot 2^{-5}}{2^{-6}}$?
questions.solution: In the top, add the exponents: $3 + (-5) = -2$, so the top is $2^{-2}$. Now divide by $2^{-6}$ by subtracting: $-2 - (-6) = 4$. The value is $2^{4} = 16$.

questions.skill: Divide powers with the same base
questions.stem: Simplify $\frac{18p^{4}q^{3}}{6p^{9}q}$ so that every exponent is positive. Assume $p$ and $q$ are not zero.
questions.solution: Divide the coefficients: $18 \div 6 = 3$. For $p$: $4 - 9 = -5$, so $p^{-5} = \frac{1}{p^{5}}$. For $q$: $3 - 1 = 2$. The result is $\frac{3q^{2}}{p^{5}}$.

questions.skill: Raise a power to a power
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $\left(\left(x^{2}\right)^{3}\right)^{2}$, for $x \neq 0$?
questions.solution: Work from the inside. $(x^{2})^{3} = x^{2 \times 3} = x^{6}$. Then $(x^{6})^{2} = x^{6 \times 2} = x^{12}$. Altogether the exponents multiply: $2 \times 3 \times 2 = 12$.

questions.skill: Raise a power to a power
questions.stem: A number is written as $\left(3^{-2}\right)^{-2}$. What is its value?
questions.solution: Multiply the exponents: $(-2) \times (-2) = 4$. So the number is $3^{4} = 3 \times 3 \times 3 \times 3 = 81$.

questions.skill: Raise a product or quotient to a power
questions.stem: Simplify $\left(\frac{2x^{2}}{y^{3}}\right)^{-2}$, where $x$ and $y$ are not zero.
questions.solution: The exponent $-2$ flips the fraction and squares it: $\left(\frac{2x^{2}}{y^{3}}\right)^{-2} = \left(\frac{y^{3}}{2x^{2}}\right)^{2} = \frac{y^{6}}{4x^{4}}$. The 2 is squared to 4, and $(x^{2})^{2} = x^{4}$.

questions.skill: Raise a product or quotient to a power
questions.stem: Find $k$ so that $(2x^{k})^{3}$ equals $8x^{15}$ for every $x$.
questions.solution: Cube each factor: $(2x^{k})^{3} = 2^{3}x^{3k} = 8x^{3k}$. The 8 already matches. Then $3k = 15$, so $k = 5$.

questions.skill: Zero and negative exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $\frac{x^{-2}y^{3}}{z^{-4}}$ with only positive exponents? Assume $x$, $y$ and $z$ are not zero.
questions.solution: A factor with a negative exponent moves across the fraction bar and its exponent becomes positive. $x^{-2}$ in the top goes to the bottom as $x^{2}$. $z^{-4}$ in the bottom goes to the top as $z^{4}$. The result is $\frac{y^{3}z^{4}}{x^{2}}$.

solve.work: x^-2 moves to the denominator as x^2; z^-4 in the denominator moves to the numerator as z^4. Result y^3 z^4 / x^2.

questions.skill: Zero and negative exponents
questions.stem: Find the sum $2^{-2} + 2^{-1} + 2^{0}$. Give the sum as a fraction.

questions.skill: Combine several exponent properties
questions.stem: Simplify $\frac{(2a^{2}b)^{3}}{4a^{5}b^{-2}}$, where $a$ and $b$ are not zero.
choices: $2ab$
questions.solution: Cube the top: $(2a^{2}b)^{3} = 8a^{6}b^{3}$. Divide the coefficients: $8 \div 4 = 2$. Subtract the exponents: $a^{6-5} = a$ and $b^{3-(-2)} = b^{5}$. The result is $2ab^{5}$.

questions.skill: Combine several exponent properties
questions.stem: What is the value of $\frac{2^{-3} \cdot 4^{2}}{2^{-1}}$?

questions.skill: Combine several exponent properties
questions.stem: Find $n$ so that $\frac{x^{n} \cdot x^{-3}}{x^{2}} = x^{4}$ for every nonzero $x$.
questions.solution: The exponent on the left is $n + (-3) - 2 = n - 5$. Set it equal to 4: $n - 5 = 4$, so $n = 9$.
