questions.skill: Compare polynomial and integer operations
questions.stem: Two polynomials each have degree 3. Which statement about their sum must be true?
choices: The sum has degree exactly 3
The sum has degree at most 3
The sum has degree exactly 6
The sum has degree at least 3
questions.answer: The sum has degree at most 3
questions.solution: Adding never creates a higher power, so the degree cannot be more than 3. It can be less: $(x^{3} + 2) + (-x^{3} + 5) = 7$ has no $x$ at all. So the degree is at most 3, but not always exactly 3.

solve.answer: The sum has degree at most 3
solve.work: Adding cannot create a term above x^3, but the x^3 terms can cancel (x^3 + 1) + (-x^3 + x) = x + 1, degree 1. So degree at most 3; not exactly 3, not 6, not at least 3.

questions.skill: Compare polynomial and integer operations
questions.stem: The sum $347 + 285$ can be written, with $x = 10$, as $(3x^{2} + 4x + 7) + (2x^{2} + 8x + 5)$. When the polynomials are added, the sum is $5x^{2} + bx + c$. What is $b + c$?

questions.skill: Add polynomials
questions.solution: Only terms with exactly the same letters and powers combine. $3a^{2}b + a^{2}b = 4a^{2}b$. The terms $-2ab$ and $6ab^{2}$ have no partner, so they stay as they are. The constants give $5 + (-7) = -2$. The sum is $4a^{2}b - 2ab + 6ab^{2} - 2$.

solve.work: a^2b: 3 + 1 = 4; ab: -2 (no partner); ab^2: +6 (no partner, unlike ab); constants 5 - 7 = -2. Result 4a^2b - 2ab + 6ab^2 - 2.

questions.skill: Add polynomials
questions.stem: The sum of $(5x^{2} + kx - 3)$ and $(2x^{2} - 4x + 9)$ is $7x^{2} + 3x + 6$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: Adding the $x$ terms gives $kx + (-4x) = (k - 4)x$. This must equal $3x$, so $k - 4 = 3$ and $k = 7$. The other terms check: $5x^{2} + 2x^{2} = 7x^{2}$ and $-3 + 9 = 6$.

solve.work: x terms: kx - 4x = 3x, so k - 4 = 3, k = 7. (x^2: 7 ok; constants: 6 ok.)

questions.skill: Subtract polynomials
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $(2a^{2}b - 3ab + 4) - (5a^{2}b - 7ab - 1)$?
questions.solution: Distribute the minus: $2a^{2}b - 3ab + 4 - 5a^{2}b + 7ab + 1$. Combine like terms: $2a^{2}b - 5a^{2}b = -3a^{2}b$; $-3ab + 7ab = 4ab$; $4 + 1 = 5$. The result is $-3a^{2}b + 4ab + 5$.

questions.skill: Subtract polynomials
questions.stem: When $(7x^{2} + 5x + k)$ is subtracted from $(10x^{2} + 2x - 3)$, the result is $3x^{2} - 3x + 6$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: The constant terms give $-3 - k = 6$, so $k = -3 - 6 = -9$. Check the rest: $10x^{2} - 7x^{2} = 3x^{2}$ and $2x - 5x = -3x$. With $k = -9$ the constant is $-3 - (-9) = 6$.

questions.skill: Multiply a monomial by a polynomial
questions.solution: Expand each part: $2x(x^{2} - 3) = 2x^{3} - 6x$ and $x(x^{2} + 4x) = x^{3} + 4x^{2}$. Subtract: $2x^{3} - 6x - x^{3} - 4x^{2}$. Combine like terms to get $x^{3} - 4x^{2} - 6x$.

questions.skill: Multiply two binomials
questions.stem: Multiply: $(4x - 3)(2x - 7)$.

questions.skill: Multiply two binomials
questions.stem: The product $(x + a)(x - 4)$ equals $x^{2} + 3x - 28$ for every $x$. What is $a$?
questions.solution: Multiplying out gives $x^{2} + (a - 4)x - 4a$. Matching the $x$ term: $a - 4 = 3$, so $a = 7$. Check the constant: $-4 \times 7 = -28$.

questions.skill: Square a binomial or multiply conjugates
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $(3a - 2b)(3a + 2b)$?
questions.solution: $3a \cdot 3a = 9a^{2}$; $3a \cdot 2b = 6ab$; $-2b \cdot 3a = -6ab$; $-2b \cdot 2b = -4b^{2}$. The $ab$ terms cancel, leaving $9a^{2} - 4b^{2}$.

questions.skill: Square a binomial or multiply conjugates
questions.stem: When $(x + 3)^{2} - (x - 3)^{2}$ is simplified, the result is $kx$. What is $k$?

questions.skill: Multiply a binomial by a trinomial, or three factors
questions.stem: The product $(2x - 1)(x^{2} + 3x - 5)$ is written as $2x^{3} + ax^{2} + bx + c$. What is $b$?
questions.solution: The $x$ terms come from $2x \cdot (-5) = -10x$ and $-1 \cdot 3x = -3x$. Together they make $-13x$, so $b = -13$. (The full product is $2x^{3} + 5x^{2} - 13x + 5$, so $a = 5$ and $c = 5$.)

questions.skill: Multiply a binomial by a trinomial, or three factors
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $(x + 1)(x + 2)(x + 3)$?
questions.solution: First multiply two of them: $(x + 1)(x + 2) = x^{2} + 3x + 2$. Then multiply by $(x + 3)$: $x^{3} + 3x^{2} + 3x^{2} + 9x + 2x + 6 = x^{3} + 6x^{2} + 11x + 6$.

questions.skill: Multiply a binomial by a trinomial, or three factors
questions.stem: A box has length $x + 4$ inches, width $x + 2$ inches and height $x$ inches. Its volume is $x^{3} + bx^{2} + cx$ cubic inches. What is $b + c$?
questions.solution: Volume is length times width times height. $(x + 4)(x + 2) = x^{2} + 6x + 8$. Multiply by $x$: $x^{3} + 6x^{2} + 8x$. So $b = 6$, $c = 8$ and $b + c = 14$.

questions.skill: Area model for a product
questions.stem: A rectangle has sides $x + 6$ and $x - 2$. Its area model has parts $x^{2}$, $-2x$, $6x$ and $-12$. Which expression is the area?
questions.solution: Add the four parts: $x^{2} - 2x + 6x - 12$. Combine the $x$ parts: $-2x + 6x = 4x$. The area is $x^{2} + 4x - 12$.

questions.skill: Area model for a product
questions.stem: A rectangle's area model has the four parts $6x^{2}$, $-4x$, $-9x$ and $6$. One side of the rectangle is $2x - 3$. The other side is $3x + k$. What is $k$?
questions.solution: The part $-4x$ comes from $2x$ times $k$. So $2k = -4$ and $k = -2$. Check the others: $2x \cdot 3x = 6x^{2}$, $-3 \cdot 3x = -9x$ and $(-3)(-2) = 6$.

solve.work: (2x - 3)(3x + k) = 6x^2 + 2kx - 9x - 3k. Parts match: 2kx = -4x gives k = -2; -3k = 6 gives k = -2. Consistent: k = -2.

questions.skill: Rewrite an expression in an equivalent form
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $(x + 3)^{2} - (x + 3)(x - 3)$?
questions.solution: $(x + 3)^{2} = x^{2} + 6x + 9$ and $(x + 3)(x - 3) = x^{2} - 9$. Subtract, distributing the minus sign: $x^{2} + 6x + 9 - x^{2} + 9 = 6x + 18$.

questions.skill: Recognize an arithmetic sequence
questions.stem: Which list of numbers is an arithmetic sequence?
questions.solution: An arithmetic sequence adds the same number each time. 5, 9, 13, 17 adds 4 every time. 2, 6, 18, 54 and 3, 6, 12, 24 multiply by the same number, and 1, 2, 4, 7 adds 1, then 2, then 3.

solve.work: 5,9,13,17: differences 4,4,4 -> arithmetic. 1,2,4,7: differences 1,2,3 no. 3,6,12,24 and 2,6,18,54 are geometric with non-constant differences.

questions.skill: Continue a geometric pattern
questions.stem: A pattern begins 4, 12, 36, 108. Each number is the same multiple of the number before it. What is the next number in the pattern?
questions.solution: Each number is 3 times the one before it: $4 \times 3 = 12$, $12 \times 3 = 36$, $36 \times 3 = 108$. The next is $108 \times 3 = 324$.

questions.skill: Match a situation to exponential growth
questions.stem: Which situation is best described by exponential growth?
choices: A plumber charges 40 dollars plus 15 dollars per hour
The number of views of a video doubles every day
A runner covers 3 kilometers every 15 minutes
A tree grows 4 centimeters every year
questions.answer: The number of views of a video doubles every day
questions.solution: Exponential growth multiplies by the same factor each step. Doubling every day is multiplying by 2. The other three situations add the same amount each time, so they are linear.

solve.answer: The number of views of a video doubles every day
solve.work: Doubling every day is a constant multiplier -> exponential. The other three add a constant amount per unit -> linear.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a table
questions.stem: The values of $y$ at $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$ are 5, 8, 11, 14. What happens to $y$ each time $x$ increases by 1?
choices: It increases by 3
It is multiplied by 3
It increases by 1
It increases by 5
questions.answer: It increases by 3
questions.solution: $8 - 5 = 3$, $11 - 8 = 3$ and $14 - 11 = 3$. The same amount, 3, is added each time, so $y$ increases by 3 each time $x$ goes up by 1. This is a linear pattern.

solve.answer: It increases by 3
solve.work: 8-5=3, 11-8=3, 14-11=3: y increases by 3 each time x increases by 1. Not multiplied by 3 (5*3=15, not 8).

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a table
questions.stem: Each list gives the values of $y$ at $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$. Which list shows a linear relationship?
questions.solution: A linear relationship adds the same amount each time. In 2, 5, 8, 11 each value is 3 more than the one before. The list 2, 4, 8, 16 doubles each time, 2, 3, 5, 8 adds 1, 2, 3, and 2, 4, 6, 9 adds 2, 2, 3.

solve.work: 2,3,5,8: differences 1,2,3 (not constant). 2,5,8,11: differences 3,3,3 -> linear. 2,4,6,9: differences 2,2,3 (not constant). 2,4,8,16: ratio 2 (exponential). Only 2,5,8,11 is linear.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a table
questions.stem: The values of $y$ are 1, 3, 9, 27 when $x$ is 0, 1, 2, 3. How should this relationship be described?
choices: Linear, because $y$ increases by 2 each time
Linear, because $y$ keeps increasing
Exponential, because $y$ increases by 3 each time
Exponential, because $y$ is multiplied by 3 each time
questions.answer: Exponential, because $y$ is multiplied by 3 each time
questions.solution: $3 \div 1 = 3$, $9 \div 3 = 3$ and $27 \div 9 = 3$, so $y$ is multiplied by 3 each time. The differences are 2, 6, 18, which are not equal. A constant multiplier means the relationship is exponential.

solve.answer: Exponential, because $y$ is multiplied by 3 each time
solve.work: 1*3=3, 3*3=9, 9*3=27: constant ratio 3, so exponential because y is multiplied by 3 each time. Differences 2,6,18 are not constant, so not linear.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a table
questions.stem: The values of $y$ at $x = 1, 2, 3, 4$ are 100, 90, 80, 70. By how much does $y$ change each time $x$ goes up by 1? (Use a negative number for a decrease.)
questions.solution: $90 - 100 = -10$, $80 - 90 = -10$ and $70 - 80 = -10$. The value of $y$ changes by $-10$ each time.

solve.work: 90-100=-10, 80-90=-10, 70-80=-10. y changes by -10 each time x goes up by 1.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a situation or equation
questions.stem: Which situation is linear?
choices: The number of bacteria in a dish doubles every hour
A car loses 10% of its value every year
A candle burns down 3 centimeters every hour
The views of a video triple every day
questions.answer: A candle burns down 3 centimeters every hour
questions.solution: A linear situation changes by the same amount each time. The candle loses 3 centimeters each hour. The other three change by multiplying (doubling, losing 10% of the current value, tripling), so they are exponential.

solve.answer: A candle burns down 3 centimeters every hour
solve.work: Candle: subtracts a constant 3 cm per hour -> linear. Bacteria doubling, losing 10% per year, tripling views: all constant ratios -> exponential. Answer: the candle.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a situation or equation
questions.stem: Which equation is an exponential relationship?
questions.solution: In an exponential relationship the variable $x$ is in the exponent. $y = 5^x$ multiplies by 5 each time $x$ goes up by 1. $y = 5x$ and $y = x + 5$ are linear, and $y = x^5$ has $x$ as the base, not the exponent.

solve.work: y=x+5 and y=5x are linear; y=x^5 is a power (polynomial) function; y=5^x has the variable in the exponent with constant base 5 -> exponential.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a situation or equation
questions.stem: Maya earns 12 dollars for each hour she works, so her pay for $h$ hours is $P = 12h$ dollars. How should this relationship be described?
choices: Exponential, with a growth factor of 12
Linear, with a rate of 12 dollars per hour
Linear, with a starting amount of 12 dollars
Exponential, with a rate of 12 dollars per hour
questions.answer: Linear, with a rate of 12 dollars per hour
questions.solution: Each extra hour adds the same 12 dollars, so the relationship is linear and 12 is the rate, in dollars per hour. With 0 hours she earns 0 dollars, so there is no starting amount.

solve.answer: Linear, with a rate of 12 dollars per hour
solve.work: P=12h: each extra hour adds 12 dollars, a constant rate of change -> linear with rate 12 dollars per hour. Starting amount (h=0) is 0, not 12. Not exponential.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a situation or equation
questions.stem: Which statement describes exponential growth?
choices: The amount is multiplied by the same number greater than 1 in each step
The amount increases by the same number in each step
The amount is multiplied by a number between 0 and 1 in each step
The amount stays the same in each step
questions.answer: The amount is multiplied by the same number greater than 1 in each step
questions.solution: Exponential growth multiplies by the same number each step, and that number is greater than 1 so the amount gets bigger. Adding the same number each step is linear growth, and multiplying by a number between 0 and 1 is exponential decay.

solve.answer: The amount is multiplied by the same number greater than 1 in each step
solve.work: Exponential growth: multiply by the same factor b>1 each step. "Stays the same" is constant; "increases by same number" is linear; factor between 0 and 1 is exponential decay.

questions.skill: Recognize a pattern that is neither linear nor exponential
questions.stem: Which equation is neither linear nor exponential?
questions.solution: $y = 3x - 1$ is linear, and $y = 3^x$ and $y = 2(0.5)^x$ have $x$ in the exponent, so they are exponential. In $y = x^2 + 1$ the variable is squared, which is neither.

solve.work: y=3^x exponential growth; y=2(0.5)^x exponential decay; y=3x-1 linear; y=x^2+1 quadratic -> neither linear nor exponential.

questions.skill: Recognize a pattern that is neither linear nor exponential
questions.stem: The values of $y$ at $x = 1, 2, 3, 4$ are 1, 4, 9, 16. Which statement is true?
choices: Linear, because $y$ goes up by 3 at the start
Exponential, because $y$ is multiplied by 4 at the start
Linear, because $y$ keeps increasing
Neither, because the differences and the ratios both change
questions.answer: Neither, because the differences and the ratios both change
questions.solution: The differences are $4 - 1 = 3$, $9 - 4 = 5$, $16 - 9 = 7$, which are not equal, so it is not linear. The ratios are $4$, $2.25$, $1.78$, which are not equal, so it is not exponential.

solve.answer: Neither, because the differences and the ratios both change
solve.work: 1,4,9,16: differences 3,5,7 (not equal); ratios 4, 2.25, 1.78 (not equal). So neither linear nor exponential (it is y=x^2).

questions.skill: Recognize a pattern that is neither linear nor exponential
questions.stem: After its first two terms, each term of the pattern 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 is the sum of the two terms before it. Which statement is true?
choices: It is arithmetic with common difference 1
It is neither arithmetic nor geometric
It is geometric with common ratio 1.5
It is both arithmetic and geometric
questions.answer: It is neither arithmetic nor geometric
questions.solution: The differences are 1, 2, 3, 5, which are not equal, so it is not arithmetic. The ratios are $1.5$, $1.67$, $1.6$, $1.625$, which are not equal, so it is not geometric.

solve.answer: It is neither arithmetic nor geometric
solve.work: 2,3,5,8,13: differences 1,2,3,5 not constant -> not arithmetic; ratios 1.5, 1.67, 1.6, 1.625 not constant -> not geometric. So neither.

questions.skill: Arithmetic sequences: difference, terms and formulas
questions.stem: What is the common difference of the arithmetic sequence 7, 12, 17, 22, ...?
questions.solution: Subtract a term from the next one: $12 - 7 = 5$. Check: $17 - 12 = 5$ and $22 - 17 = 5$.

questions.skill: Arithmetic sequences: difference, terms and formulas
questions.stem: The first term of an arithmetic sequence is 10 and the common difference is 4. What is the 4th term?
questions.solution: The terms are 10, 14, 18, 22. The 4th term is $10 + 3 \times 4 = 22$.

questions.skill: Arithmetic sequences: difference, terms and formulas
questions.stem: An arithmetic sequence starts at 20 and has common difference $-3$. Which list shows its first four terms?
questions.solution: Add $-3$ each time: $20$, $20 - 3 = 17$, $17 - 3 = 14$, $14 - 3 = 11$. The list 20, 23, 26, 29 adds 3 instead, 23, 20, 17, 14 starts at the wrong term, and the last list multiplies instead of adding.

questions.skill: Arithmetic sequences: difference, terms and formulas
questions.stem: In a sequence, each term is the same amount less than the term before it: 50, 44, 38, 32, ... What is the next term?
questions.solution: Each term is $50 - 44 = 6$ less than the one before. The next term is $32 - 6 = 26$.

questions.skill: Geometric sequences: ratio, terms and formulas
questions.stem: What is the common ratio of the geometric sequence 5, 15, 45, 135, ...?
questions.solution: Divide a term by the one before it: $15 \div 5 = 3$. Check: $45 \div 15 = 3$ and $135 \div 45 = 3$.

questions.skill: Geometric sequences: ratio, terms and formulas
questions.stem: A geometric sequence has first term 2 and common ratio 5. What is its third term?
questions.solution: The terms are 2, $2 \times 5 = 10$, $10 \times 5 = 50$. The third term is 50.

questions.skill: Geometric sequences: ratio, terms and formulas
questions.stem: What is the common ratio of the geometric sequence 80, 40, 20, 10, ...?
questions.solution: Divide a term by the one before it: $40 \div 80 = 0.5$. Check: $20 \div 40 = 0.5$ and $10 \div 20 = 0.5$. The value 2 is the ratio read backwards, and $-40$ is the change from the first term to the second, not a ratio.

questions.skill: Geometric sequences: ratio, terms and formulas
questions.stem: Each term of the pattern 1, 5, 25, 125 is the same multiple of the term before it. Which number comes next?
questions.solution: Each term is 5 times the one before, so the next term is $125 \times 5 = 625$. Adding 5 would give 130, adding 25 would give 150 and doubling would give 250; none of these follows the pattern.

solve.work: Each term is 5 times the previous: 1,5,25,125, next 125*5=625.

questions.skill: Predict a value from a table
questions.stem: A bike shop charges 7 dollars for 1 hour, 12 dollars for 2 hours and 17 dollars for 3 hours, and the pattern continues. How many dollars does it charge for 4 hours?
questions.solution: The charge goes up by $12 - 7 = 5$ dollars for each extra hour. For 4 hours it is $17 + 5 = 22$ dollars.

questions.skill: Predict a value from a table
questions.stem: A video has 3 views on day 0, 6 views on day 1, 12 views on day 2 and 24 views on day 3. The pattern continues. How many views are there on day 4?
questions.solution: The views double each day: $3 \times 2 = 6$, $6 \times 2 = 12$, $12 \times 2 = 24$. On day 4 there are $24 \times 2 = 48$ views.

questions.skill: Predict a value from a table
questions.stem: The values of $y$ at $x = 1, 2, 3, 4$ are 90, 81, 72, 63, and the pattern continues. What is $y$ at $x = 5$?
questions.solution: The values go down by 9 each time ($90 - 81 = 9$). At $x = 5$ the value is $63 - 9 = 54$.

questions.skill: Predict a value from a table
questions.stem: In a linear relationship, $y = 4$ when $x = 0$ and $y = 7$ when $x = 1$. What is $y$ when $x = 2$?
questions.solution: The value of $y$ goes up by $7 - 4 = 3$ each time $x$ goes up by 1. When $x = 2$, $y = 7 + 3 = 10$.

solve.work: Linear: rate = 7-4 = 3 per unit of x. At x=2: 7+3=10.

questions.skill: Predict a value from points on a graph
questions.stem: A straight line passes through the points $(0, 3)$, $(1, 5)$ and $(2, 7)$. What is the $y$-coordinate of the point on the line with $x = 4$?
questions.solution: Each time $x$ goes up by 1, $y$ goes up by 2. Starting at $y = 3$ when $x = 0$, at $x = 4$ the value is $3 + 4 \times 2 = 11$.

questions.skill: Predict a value from points on a graph
questions.stem: The points $(0, 1)$, $(1, 3)$ and $(2, 9)$ lie on the graph of an exponential relationship. What is the $y$-coordinate of the point on the graph with $x = 3$?
questions.solution: Each $y$-value is 3 times the one before ($3 \div 1 = 3$, $9 \div 3 = 3$). At $x = 3$, $y = 9 \times 3 = 27$.

solve.work: 1,3,9: multiplied by 3 each step (y=3^x). At x=3: 9*3=27.

questions.skill: Predict a value from points on a graph
questions.stem: The graph of a pattern contains the points $(0, 3)$, $(1, 6)$ and $(2, 12)$, and each $y$-value is the same multiple of the one before it. Which point is also on the graph?
questions.solution: Each $y$-value is 2 times the one before, so at $x = 3$ the value is $12 \times 2 = 24$. The point $(3, 18)$ adds 6 and $(3, 15)$ adds 3, which would make the pattern linear, and $(4, 24)$ has the wrong $x$-value.

questions.skill: Compare linear and exponential growth
questions.stem: Pattern A starts at 5 and adds 5 each time. Pattern B starts at 5 and doubles each time. How much larger is the 4th term of B than the 4th term of A?
questions.solution: Pattern A is 5, 10, 15, 20, so its 4th term is 20. Pattern B is 5, 10, 20, 40, so its 4th term is 40. The difference is $40 - 20 = 20$.

questions.skill: Compare linear and exponential growth
questions.stem: Two quantities start at the same size and both keep growing. One adds the same amount each step. The other multiplies by 2 each step. Which statement is true?
choices: The one that adds each step is always larger
The two quantities always stay equal
The one multiplied by 2 each step eventually becomes larger
The one multiplied by 2 each step never becomes larger
questions.answer: The one multiplied by 2 each step eventually becomes larger
questions.solution: Repeated multiplying makes the increases bigger and bigger, while repeated adding makes the same size increase every time. So the quantity that doubles eventually passes the one that adds, however large the added amount is.

solve.answer: The one multiplied by 2 each step eventually becomes larger
solve.work: Start a>0. Additive: a+nd. Doubling: a*2^n. Exponential growth eventually overtakes any constant addition (e.g. a=1,d=10: by n=7, 128 > 71). So the doubling one eventually becomes larger.

questions.skill: Compare linear and exponential growth
questions.stem: When $x = 5$, which statement comparing $2x$ and $2^x$ is correct?
choices: $2x$ is greater: 10 compared with 7
$2^x$ is greater: 32 compared with 10
They are equal: both are 10
$2^x$ is greater: 25 compared with 10
questions.answer: $2^x$ is greater: 32 compared with 10
questions.solution: $2x = 2 \times 5 = 10$ and $2^x = 2^5 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 = 32$. So $2^x$ is greater. The mistakes are reading $2^5$ as $2 + 5$, as $2 \times 5$, or as $5^2$.

solve.answer: $2^x$ is greater: 32 compared with 10

questions.skill: Compare linear and exponential growth
questions.stem: Two savings plans each start with 2 dollars. Plan L adds 3 dollars each week. Plan E triples its amount each week. After 2 weeks, how do the plans compare?
choices: Plan E has 10 dollars more than Plan L
Plan E has 4 dollars more than Plan L
Plan L has 2 dollars more than Plan E
Plan E has 28 dollars more than Plan L
questions.answer: Plan E has 10 dollars more than Plan L
questions.solution: Plan L: $2 \to 5 \to 8$, so 8 dollars. Plan E: $2 \to 6 \to 18$, so 18 dollars. Plan E has $18 - 8 = 10$ dollars more.

solve.answer: Plan E has 10 dollars more than Plan L
solve.work: Plan L: 2 -> 5 -> 8 dollars after 2 weeks. Plan E: 2 -> 6 -> 18 dollars. 18-8=10, Plan E has 10 dollars more.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a table
questions.stem: A table gives $y$ for $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$: the values of $y$ are 3, 6, 12, 24. Which statement describes the pattern?
choices: Exponential: $y$ is multiplied by 2 each time $x$ increases by 1
Linear: $y$ increases by 3 each time $x$ increases by 1
Linear: $y$ increases by 6 each time $x$ increases by 1
Exponential: $y$ is multiplied by 3 each time $x$ increases by 1
questions.answer: Exponential: $y$ is multiplied by 2 each time $x$ increases by 1
questions.solution: The differences are 3, 6, 12, which are not equal, so the pattern is not linear. The ratios are $6 \div 3 = 2$, $12 \div 6 = 2$ and $24 \div 12 = 2$, so $y$ is multiplied by 2 each time.

solve.answer: Exponential: $y$ is multiplied by 2 each time $x$ increases by 1
solve.work: 3,6,12,24: differences 3,6,12 not constant; ratios 2,2,2 -> exponential, multiplied by 2.

questions.skill: Predict a value in an exponential decay pattern
questions.stem: A table gives $P$ for $t = 0, 1, 2, 3$: the values of $P$ are 640, 320, 160, 80. The pattern continues in the same way. What is $P$ when $t = 6$?
questions.solution: Each value is half the one before it. So $P = 640 \times \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^t$. At $t = 6$: $640 \div 64 = 10$. (Continuing the list: 80, 40, 20, 10.)

questions.skill: Predict a value in a linear pattern from a table
questions.stem: A table gives $y$ for $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$: the values of $y$ are 10, 14, 18, 22. The pattern continues in the same way. What is $y$ when $x = 6$?
questions.solution: The values go up by 4 each time, so $y = 10 + 4x$. When $x = 6$: $y = 10 + 24 = 34$.

solve.work: Adds 4 each step: y = 10 + 4x. At x = 6: 10 + 24 = 34.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a table
questions.stem: The values of $y$ at $x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4$ are 160, 80, 40, 20, 10. How should this relationship be described?
choices: Exponential, because $y$ is multiplied by 2 each time
Linear, because $y$ keeps decreasing
Linear, because $y$ decreases by 80 each time
Exponential, because $y$ is multiplied by $\frac{1}{2}$ each time
questions.answer: Exponential, because $y$ is multiplied by $\frac{1}{2}$ each time
questions.solution: $80 \div 160 = \frac{1}{2}$, $40 \div 80 = \frac{1}{2}$, and so on, so $y$ is multiplied by $\frac{1}{2}$ each time. The decreases are 80, 40, 20, 10, which are not equal, so it is not linear.

solve.answer: Exponential, because $y$ is multiplied by $\frac{1}{2}$ each time
solve.work: 80/160=1/2, 40/80=1/2, 20/40=1/2, 10/20=1/2: constant ratio 1/2 -> exponential decay, multiplied by 1/2. Differences -80,-40,-20,-10 are not constant, so not linear; not multiplied by 2.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a table
questions.stem: The relationship between $x$ and $y$ is linear. When $x$ is 0, 5, 10 and 15, $y$ is 2, 12, 22 and 32. By how much does $y$ change each time $x$ increases by 1?
questions.solution: When $x$ goes up by 5, $y$ goes up by $12 - 2 = 10$. So for each increase of 1 in $x$, $y$ goes up by $10 \div 5 = 2$.

solve.work: y rises by 10 for each increase of 5 in x (12-2, 22-12, 32-22). Rate = 10/5 = 2 per unit of x.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a table
questions.stem: A savings account holds 100, 110, 121 and 133.1 dollars after 0, 1, 2 and 3 years. Which statement describes the pattern?
choices: Linear, because each amount is 10 more than the one before
Linear, because each amount is 11 more than the one before
Exponential, because each amount is 1.1 times the one before
Exponential, because each amount is 10 times the one before
questions.answer: Exponential, because each amount is 1.1 times the one before
questions.solution: The increases are 10, 11, 12.1, which are not equal, so it is not linear. The ratios $110 \div 100$, $121 \div 110$ and $133.1 \div 121$ are all $1.1$, so each amount is 1.1 times the one before.

solve.answer: Exponential, because each amount is 1.1 times the one before
solve.work: 110/100=1.1, 121/110=1.1, 133.1/121=1.1: constant ratio -> exponential. Differences 10, 11, 12.1 not constant.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a table
questions.stem: The values of $y$ at $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$ are 81, 27, 9, 3. Each value is the same multiple of the one before it. What is that multiple?
questions.solution: Divide each value by the one before it: $27 \div 81 = \frac{1}{3}$, $9 \div 27 = \frac{1}{3}$ and $3 \div 9 = \frac{1}{3}$.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a situation or equation
questions.stem: Which situation shows exponential decay?
choices: A candle burns down 2 centimeters every hour
A car loses 15% of its value each year
A tank drains 5 gallons every minute
A phone battery drops 4 percentage points every hour
questions.answer: A car loses 15% of its value each year
questions.solution: Exponential decay multiplies by the same number between 0 and 1 each time. Losing 15% of the value each year multiplies the value by 0.85. The other three lose the same fixed amount each time, so they are linear.

solve.answer: A car loses 15% of its value each year
solve.work: Losing 15% each year means multiplying by 0.85 each year -> exponential decay. The battery (4 points/hour), tank (5 gal/min) and candle (2 cm/hour) decrease by constant amounts -> linear.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a situation or equation
questions.stem: Which equation represents a linear relationship?
questions.solution: $y = 2(x + 4)$ simplifies to $y = 2x + 8$, which is linear. $y = 2(4)^x$ and $y = 4^{2x}$ (which equals $16^x$) are exponential, and $y = (x + 4)^2$ has a squared variable.

solve.work: y=2(x+4)=2x+8 is linear. y=2(4)^x and y=4^{2x}=16^x are exponential; y=(x+4)^2 is quadratic.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a situation or equation
questions.stem: A fish population grows by 12% each year. By what number is the population multiplied from one year to the next?
questions.solution: Growing by 12% means keeping 100% of the population and adding 12% more, so the new population is $100\% + 12\% = 112\%$, which is $1.12$ times the old one.

solve.work: Growing by 12% means new = old + 0.12*old = 1.12*old. Factor 1.12.

questions.skill: Recognize a pattern that is neither linear nor exponential
questions.stem: Which relationship is neither linear nor exponential?
choices: The perimeter of a square as its side length changes
The cost of buying pencils at 30 cents each as the number of pencils changes
The area of a square as its side length changes
The amount in an account that doubles each year as the number of years changes
questions.answer: The area of a square as its side length changes
questions.solution: The area is $s^2$, which is neither linear nor exponential. The perimeter $4s$ and the pencil cost are linear (a fixed amount added each time), and an amount that doubles each year is exponential.

solve.answer: The area of a square as its side length changes
solve.work: Area of square A=s^2: quadratic -> neither. Doubling account: exponential. Pencils at 30 cents: linear. Perimeter P=4s: linear.

questions.skill: Recognize a pattern that is neither linear nor exponential
questions.stem: A ball is thrown straight up. Its height rises, reaches a top, then falls back to the ground. Which statement is true about modeling the whole flight?
choices: Neither a linear nor an exponential function fits, because the height rises and then falls
A linear function fits, because the ball moves at a steady speed
An exponential function fits, because the height keeps multiplying
One linear function fits if its rate of change is positive and then negative
questions.answer: Neither a linear nor an exponential function fits, because the height rises and then falls
questions.solution: A linear function always goes one way (up if the rate is positive, down if it is negative) and so does an exponential function. The height of the ball goes up and then down, so neither kind of function can model the whole flight.

solve.answer: Neither a linear nor an exponential function fits, because the height rises and then falls
solve.work: A linear function is always increasing or always decreasing (or constant), with one fixed rate; an exponential function is also monotonic. Height rising then falling cannot be either. One linear function cannot have a rate that changes sign. So neither fits.

questions.skill: Recognize a pattern that is neither linear nor exponential
questions.stem: The numbers of dots in figures 1, 2, 3 and 4 are 1, 3, 6 and 10. Which statement is true?
choices: Linear, because the number of dots keeps increasing
Neither: the increases 2, 3, 4 are not equal and the ratios are not equal
Linear, because it goes up by 2 each time
Exponential, because it is multiplied by 3 at the start
questions.answer: Neither: the increases 2, 3, 4 are not equal and the ratios are not equal
questions.solution: The increases are $3 - 1 = 2$, $6 - 3 = 3$, $10 - 6 = 4$, so it is not linear. The ratios are $3$, $2$, $1.67$, so it is not exponential.

solve.answer: Neither: the increases 2, 3, 4 are not equal and the ratios are not equal
solve.work: 1,3,6,10: increases 2,3,4 not equal -> not linear; ratios 3, 2, 1.67 not equal -> not exponential. Neither.

questions.skill: Recognize a pattern that is neither linear nor exponential
questions.stem: Here are four sequences. A: 4, 8, 12, 16. B: 4, 8, 16, 32. C: 4, 8, 14, 22. D: 4, 8, 13, 19. How many of them are neither arithmetic nor geometric?
questions.solution: A adds 4 each time, so it is arithmetic. B multiplies by 2 each time, so it is geometric. C has differences 4, 6, 8 and D has differences 4, 5, 6, and neither has a constant ratio. So 2 sequences, C and D, are neither.

solve.work: A: diffs 4,4,4 arithmetic. B: ratio 2 geometric. C: diffs 4,6,8; ratios 2, 1.75, 1.57 -> neither. D: diffs 4,5,6; ratios 2, 1.625, 1.46 -> neither. Two are neither.

questions.skill: Arithmetic sequences: difference, terms and formulas
questions.stem: What is the 20th term of the arithmetic sequence 5, 8, 11, 14, ...?
questions.solution: The common difference is 3. The 20th term is the first term plus 19 differences: $5 + 19 \times 3 = 5 + 57 = 62$.

questions.skill: Arithmetic sequences: difference, terms and formulas
questions.stem: Which formula gives the $n$th term of the arithmetic sequence 7, 11, 15, 19, ...?
questions.solution: The first term is 7 and the common difference is 4, so $a_n = 7 + 4(n - 1)$. Check: $n = 1$ gives 7 and $n = 2$ gives 11. The formula $7 + 4n$ gives 11 for $n = 1$, and the last formula is geometric.

solve.work: a1=7, d=4: a_n = 7 + 4(n-1). Check n=1: 7, n=2: 11. 7+4n gives 11 at n=1 (wrong); 4+7(n-1) gives 4 at n=1 (wrong); 7(4)^{n-1} is geometric.

questions.skill: Arithmetic sequences: difference, terms and formulas
questions.stem: An arithmetic sequence has first term 100 and common difference $-7$. What is the 6th term?
questions.solution: The 6th term is the first term plus 5 differences: $100 + 5 \times (-7) = 100 - 35 = 65$.

questions.skill: Arithmetic sequences: difference, terms and formulas
questions.stem: A theater has 12 seats in the first row. Each row has 3 more seats than the row in front of it. How many seats are in row 10?
questions.solution: The numbers of seats form an arithmetic sequence with first term 12 and difference 3. Row 10 has $12 + 9 \times 3 = 12 + 27 = 39$ seats.

questions.skill: Geometric sequences: ratio, terms and formulas
questions.stem: What is the 6th term of the geometric sequence 3, 6, 12, 24, ...?
questions.solution: The common ratio is 2. The 6th term is the first term times the ratio 5 times: $3 \times 2^5 = 3 \times 32 = 96$.

questions.skill: Geometric sequences: ratio, terms and formulas
questions.stem: Which formula gives the $n$th term of the geometric sequence 5, 10, 20, 40, ...?
questions.solution: The first term is 5 and the common ratio is 2, so $a_n = 5(2)^{n-1}$. Check: $n = 1$ gives 5 and $n = 3$ gives 20. The formula $5 + 5(n - 1)$ is arithmetic, $5(2)^n$ gives 10 for $n = 1$, and $2(5)^{n-1}$ swaps the first term and the ratio.

solve.work: a1=5, r=2: a_n = 5(2)^{n-1}. Check n=1: 5, n=2: 10. 5(2)^n gives 10 at n=1 (wrong); 2(5)^{n-1} gives 2 (wrong); 5+5(n-1) is arithmetic.

questions.skill: Geometric sequences: ratio, terms and formulas
questions.stem: A geometric sequence has first term 64 and common ratio $\frac{1}{2}$. What is the 5th term?
questions.solution: Halve four times: 64, 32, 16, 8, 4. The 5th term is $64 \times \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^4 = 4$.

questions.skill: Geometric sequences: ratio, terms and formulas
questions.stem: A ball is dropped and bounces. The first bounce reaches 200 centimeters. Each later bounce reaches 60% as high as the bounce before it. How high is the third bounce, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The heights form a geometric sequence with ratio $0.6$: first bounce 200, second bounce $200 \times 0.6 = 120$, third bounce $120 \times 0.6 = 72$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Predict a value from a table
questions.stem: A taxi charges 5.50 dollars for 1 mile, 8 dollars for 2 miles and 10.50 dollars for 3 miles, and the pattern continues. How many dollars does it charge for 8 miles?
questions.solution: The charge goes up by $8 - 5.50 = 2.50$ dollars for each extra mile. For 8 miles it is $5.50 + 7 \times 2.50 = 5.50 + 17.50 = 23$ dollars.

questions.skill: Predict a value from a table
questions.stem: A new account has 5 followers on day 0, 10 on day 1, 20 on day 2 and 40 on day 3. The pattern continues. How many followers does it have on day 7?
questions.solution: The number of followers doubles each day, so on day 7 it is $5 \times 2^7 = 5 \times 128 = 640$.

questions.skill: Predict a value from a table
questions.stem: A linear relationship has $y = 4, 11, 18, 25$ when $x = 0, 2, 4, 6$. What is $y$ when $x = 5$?
questions.solution: When $x$ goes up by 2, $y$ goes up by 7, so $y$ goes up by $3.5$ for each increase of 1 in $x$. At $x = 5$, $y = 18 + 3.5 = 21.5$. This is also halfway between 18 and 25.

solve.work: y rises 7 for every 2 in x: slope 3.5, y = 4 + 3.5x. At x=5: 4 + 17.5 = 21.5.

questions.skill: Predict a value from a table
questions.stem: A machine is worth 8100 dollars when new, 5400 dollars after 1 year, 3600 dollars after 2 years and 2400 dollars after 3 years. If the pattern continues, how many dollars is it worth after 4 years?
questions.solution: Each value is $\frac{2}{3}$ of the one before: $8100 \times \frac{2}{3} = 5400$, $5400 \times \frac{2}{3} = 3600$, $3600 \times \frac{2}{3} = 2400$. After 4 years it is $2400 \times \frac{2}{3} = 1600$ dollars.

questions.skill: Predict a value from points on a graph
questions.stem: A straight line passes through the points $(2, 7)$ and $(5, 16)$. What is the $y$-coordinate of the point on the line with $x = 10$?
questions.solution: From $x = 2$ to $x = 5$, $y$ goes up by 9, so $y$ goes up by 3 for each increase of 1 in $x$. From $x = 5$ to $x = 10$, $y$ goes up by $5 \times 3 = 15$, so $y = 16 + 15 = 31$.

questions.skill: Predict a value from points on a graph
questions.stem: The graph of an exponential relationship passes through $(1, 6)$ and $(2, 18)$. What is the $y$-coordinate of the point on the graph with $x = 4$?
questions.solution: Each $y$-value is $18 \div 6 = 3$ times the one before. From $x = 1$ to $x = 4$ is 3 steps, so $y = 6 \times 3^3 = 6 \times 27 = 162$.

solve.work: Ratio 18/6 = 3 per unit x. x=3: 54, x=4: 162.

questions.skill: Predict a value from points on a graph
questions.stem: A straight line passes through the points $(0, 20)$ and $(4, 12)$. Which point is also on the line?
questions.solution: From $x = 0$ to $x = 4$, $y$ goes down by 8, so it goes down by 2 for each increase of 1 in $x$. The line is $y = 20 - 2x$. At $x = 6$, $y = 20 - 12 = 8$. At $x = 5$, $y = 10$, and at $x = 7$, $y = 6$.

questions.skill: Predict a value from points on a graph
questions.stem: A graph passes through the points $(0, 100)$, $(1, 80)$, $(2, 64)$ and $(3, 51.2)$. Which statement is true?
choices: Linear, because $y$ goes down by 20 each time
Exponential growth, because the growth factor is 0.8
Exponential decay, because each $y$-value is 0.8 times the one before
Exponential decay, because each $y$-value is 0.2 times the one before
questions.answer: Exponential decay, because each $y$-value is 0.8 times the one before
questions.solution: $80 \div 100 = 0.8$, $64 \div 80 = 0.8$ and $51.2 \div 64 = 0.8$. Each $y$-value is 0.8 times the one before, which is exponential decay. The decreases (20, 16, 12.8) are not equal, so it is not linear.

solve.answer: Exponential decay, because each $y$-value is 0.8 times the one before
solve.work: 80/100 = 0.8, 64/80 = 0.8, 51.2/64 = 0.8: constant ratio 0.8 < 1 -> exponential decay, each value 0.8 times the one before. Differences -20, -16, -12.8 not constant.

questions.skill: Compare linear and exponential growth
questions.stem: Two plans are measured at $t = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4$. Plan A has the values 8, 12, 16, 20, 24 and Plan B has the values 2, 4, 8, 16, 32. For what value of $t$ does Plan B first have a greater value than Plan A?
questions.solution: At $t = 3$, Plan A is 20 and Plan B is 16. At $t = 4$, Plan A is 24 and Plan B is 32. Plan B is first greater at $t = 4$.

solve.work: t=0: 8 vs 2; t=1: 12 vs 4; t=2: 16 vs 8; t=3: 20 vs 16; t=4: 24 vs 32. B first greater at t=4.

questions.skill: Compare linear and exponential growth
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 4x + 100$ and $g(x) = 2^x$. Which statement is true?
choices: $g(x) < f(x)$ for every value of $x$
$g(x) > f(x)$ for every value of $x$
questions.solution: $g(5) = 32$ and $f(5) = 120$, so $g(5) < f(5)$. $g(20) = 1{,}048{,}576$ and $f(20) = 180$, so $g(20) > f(20)$. The exponential function starts lower but grows faster and passes the linear one.

questions.skill: Compare linear and exponential growth
questions.stem: Account A starts with 200 dollars and adds 25 dollars each year. Account B starts with 200 dollars and is multiplied by 1.1 each year. After 2 years, how many more dollars does Account A hold than Account B?
questions.solution: Account A: $200 + 2 \times 25 = 250$ dollars. Account B: $200 \times 1.1 \times 1.1 = 242$ dollars. Account A holds $250 - 242 = 8$ dollars more.

questions.skill: Recognize a table that is neither linear nor exponential
questions.stem: Four tables each give $y$ for $x = 1, 2, 3, 4$. Which table is neither linear nor exponential?
questions.solution: For 2, 5, 10, 17 the differences are 3, 5, 7 (not equal) and the ratios are 2.5, 2, 1.7 (not equal), so it is neither. 2, 5, 8, 11 adds 3 each time, 2, 6, 18, 54 multiplies by 3, and 32, 16, 8, 4 multiplies by one half.

solve.work: 32,16,8,4: ratio 1/2 exponential. 2,5,10,17: differences 3,5,7 (not constant), ratios 2.5, 2, 1.7 (not constant) -> neither (quadratic, x^2+1). 2,6,18,54: ratio 3 exponential. 2,5,8,11: difference 3 linear.

questions.skill: Compare a linear and an exponential plan
questions.stem: Plan A has value $A = 100 + 20t$ and Plan B has value $B = 20(2)^t$ after $t$ whole years. For the first whole number of years $t$ where Plan B is greater than Plan A, what is $t$?
questions.solution: Compare year by year. $t = 0$: A is 100, B is 20. $t = 1$: 120 and 40. $t = 2$: 140 and 80. $t = 3$: 160 and 160, which are equal, not greater. $t = 4$: A is 180 and B is 320, so Plan B is greater for the first time at $t = 4$.

solve.work: t=0: A 100, B 20. t=1: 120 vs 40. t=2: 140 vs 80. t=3: 160 vs 160 (equal, not greater). t=4: 180 vs 320 -> B greater. t = 4.

questions.skill: Find a later term of an arithmetic sequence from two terms
questions.stem: In an arithmetic sequence, the 3rd term is 11 and the 7th term is 31. What is the 10th term?
questions.solution: From the 3rd to the 7th term there are 4 steps, and the terms rise by $31 - 11 = 20$, so each step adds $20 \div 4 = 5$. The 10th term is 3 steps after the 7th: $31 + 3 \times 5 = 46$.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a table
questions.stem: A table gives $y$ for $x = 1, 2, 4, 6$: the values are 5, 8, 14, 20. Which statement is true?
choices: Neither, because the changes in $y$ (3, 6, 6) are not equal
Exponential, because $y$ keeps increasing
Linear, because $y$ goes up by 6 each time $x$ goes up by 1
Linear, because $y$ goes up by 3 for every increase of 1 in $x$
questions.answer: Linear, because $y$ goes up by 3 for every increase of 1 in $x$
questions.solution: The $x$-values do not go up by 1 each time. From $x = 1$ to 2, $y$ goes up by 3 (a rate of 3 per unit). From $x = 2$ to 4, $y$ goes up by 6, which is 3 per unit. From $x = 4$ to 6, $y$ goes up by 6, which is 3 per unit. The rate is constant, so the relationship is linear.

solve.answer: Linear, because $y$ goes up by 3 for every increase of 1 in $x$
solve.work: x steps are uneven: 1->2 (Dx=1, Dy=3), 2->4 (Dx=2, Dy=6), 4->6 (Dx=2, Dy=6). Rate Dy/Dx = 3 each time -> linear, y = 3x + 2. Option A ignores the uneven x-steps.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a table
questions.stem: A table gives $y$ for $x = 0, 2, 4, 6$: the values are 3, 12, 48, 192. The relationship is exponential, and $y$ is multiplied by the same positive number each time $x$ goes up by 1. What is that number?
questions.solution: When $x$ goes up by 2, $y$ is multiplied by $12 \div 3 = 4$. Going up by 2 means multiplying by the factor twice, so factor $\times$ factor $= 4$. The positive number is 2.

solve.work: Each step of 2 in x multiplies y by 4 (12/3, 48/12, 192/48). Per unit x: b^2 = 4, b positive -> b = 2. y = 3*2^x.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a table
questions.stem: Each list gives the values of $y$ at $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$. Which list shows exponential decay?
questions.solution: In 100, 90, 81, 72.9 each value is 0.9 times the one before, which is exponential decay. The lists 100, 90, 80, 70 and 100, 91, 82, 73 decrease by a constant amount (linear), and in 100, 90, 81, 70 the last step does not follow the pattern.

solve.work: 100,90,81,72.9: ratios 0.9, 0.9, 0.9 -> exponential decay. 100,90,81,70: 70/81 is not 0.9. 100,91,82,73 and 100,90,80,70 are linear (constant differences).

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a situation or equation
questions.stem: Which situation is modeled by an exponential function?
choices: The number of cases in an outbreak is 20% greater each day than the day before
A subscription costs 9 dollars the first month and 2 dollars more each month than the month before
A rope is shortened by 3 feet each time a piece is cut off
A pool is filled at 40 gallons per minute
questions.answer: The number of cases in an outbreak is 20% greater each day than the day before
questions.solution: Each day the number of cases is multiplied by 1.2, which is exponential. The subscription adds 2 dollars each month, the rope loses 3 feet each time, and the pool gains 40 gallons each minute; these all change by a fixed amount, so they are linear.

solve.answer: The number of cases in an outbreak is 20% greater each day than the day before
solve.work: Cases 20% greater each day: multiply by 1.2 daily -> exponential. Subscription +2 each month, rope -3 feet each cut, pool 40 gal/min: constant differences -> linear.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a situation or equation
questions.stem: A town has 2000 people. Its population grows by 5% each year. How many more people does the town gain in the second year than in the first year?
questions.solution: After year 1: $2000 \times 1.05 = 2100$, a gain of 100. After year 2: $2100 \times 1.05 = 2205$, a gain of 105. The town gains $105 - 100 = 5$ more people in the second year.

solve.work: Year 1 gain: 5% of 2000 = 100, population 2100. Year 2 gain: 5% of 2100 = 105. 105 - 100 = 5 more.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a situation or equation
questions.stem: The number of bacteria in a dish triples every 2 hours. There are 10 bacteria at the start. How many bacteria are there after 6 hours?
questions.solution: 6 hours is three periods of 2 hours, so the number is multiplied by 3 three times: $10 \times 3^3 = 10 \times 27 = 270$.

questions.skill: Tell linear from exponential in a situation or equation
questions.stem: A tank holds 512 liters of water. Every hour, 25% of the water in the tank is drained out. How many liters are left after 3 hours?
questions.solution: Each hour 75% of the water is left, so the amount is multiplied by 0.75. After 3 hours: $512 \times 0.75^3 = 512 \times \frac{27}{64} = 216$ liters.

questions.skill: Recognize a pattern that is neither linear nor exponential
questions.stem: The values of $f(x)$ at $x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4$ are 1, 2, 4, 8, 15. Which statement is true?
choices: Exponential, because $f(x)$ is multiplied by 2 each time
Linear, because $f(x)$ keeps increasing
Exponential, because the first three ratios are all 2
Neither linear nor exponential, because the ratios and the differences are not all equal
questions.answer: Neither linear nor exponential, because the ratios and the differences are not all equal
questions.solution: The ratios are 2, 2, 2 and then $15 \div 8 = 1.875$, so they are not all equal. The differences are 1, 2, 4, 7, which are not equal either. So the table is neither linear nor exponential.

solve.answer: Neither linear nor exponential, because the ratios and the differences are not all equal
solve.work: 1,2,4,8,15: ratios 2,2,2,1.875 (not all equal), differences 1,2,4,7 (not all equal) -> neither linear nor exponential.

questions.skill: Recognize a pattern that is neither linear nor exponential
questions.stem: A pattern starts at 4. The second term is 1 more than the first, the third is 2 more than the second, the fourth is 3 more than the third, and so on, adding one more each time. So the pattern begins 4, 5, 7, 10, 14. What is the 8th term?
questions.solution: Continue the pattern: 14, then $14 + 5 = 19$, $19 + 6 = 25$, $25 + 7 = 32$. The 8th term is 32.

questions.skill: Recognize a pattern that is neither linear nor exponential
questions.stem: Which function is NOT an exponential function?
choices: $y = 3 \cdot 3^x$
$y = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^x$
questions.solution: $y = 2^{x+1}$ equals $2 \cdot 2^x$, $y = 3 \cdot 3^x$ and $y = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^x$ all have a constant base with $x$ in the exponent, so they are exponential. In $y = x^3$ the variable is the base, so it is neither linear nor exponential.

solve.work: (1/2)^x, 3*3^x and 2^{x+1}=2*2^x all have the variable in the exponent with a constant positive base -> exponential. y=x^3 is a power (cubic) function -> not exponential.

questions.skill: Arithmetic sequences: difference, terms and formulas
questions.stem: In an arithmetic sequence, the 4th term is 17 and the 9th term is 42. What is the first term?
questions.solution: From the 4th to the 9th term there are 5 steps and the terms go up by $42 - 17 = 25$, so the common difference is 5. The first term is 3 steps before the 4th: $17 - 3 \times 5 = 2$.

solve.work: From term 4 to term 9 is 5 steps: 5d = 42-17 = 25, d = 5. a1 = 17 - 3*5 = 2.

questions.skill: Arithmetic sequences: difference, terms and formulas
questions.stem: How many terms are in the arithmetic sequence 6, 13, 20, ..., 160?
questions.solution: The common difference is 7. From 6 to 160 the terms go up by 154, which is $154 \div 7 = 22$ steps. With 22 steps there are $22 + 1 = 23$ terms.

questions.skill: Arithmetic sequences: difference, terms and formulas
questions.stem: The numbers 3, $k$, $m$, 27 are four consecutive terms of an arithmetic sequence. What is $k + m$?
questions.solution: From 3 to 27 there are 3 steps, so the common difference is $(27 - 3) \div 3 = 8$. Then $k = 11$ and $m = 19$, and $k + m = 30$.

questions.skill: Arithmetic sequences: difference, terms and formulas
questions.stem: A sequence is defined by $a_1 = 9$ and $a_{n+1} = a_n - 4$. Which formula gives $a_n$?
questions.solution: Each term is 4 less than the one before, so it is arithmetic with first term 9 and common difference $-4$: $a_n = 9 - 4(n - 1)$. Check: $n = 1$ gives 9 and $n = 2$ gives 5. The formula $9 - 4n$ gives 5 for $n = 1$.

solve.work: Arithmetic with a1=9, d=-4: a_n = 9 - 4(n-1). Check: 9, 5, 1. 9-4n gives 5 at n=1 (wrong); -4+9(n-1) gives -4 (wrong); 9(-4)^{n-1} is geometric.

questions.skill: Geometric sequences: ratio, terms and formulas
questions.stem: In a geometric sequence, the 2nd term is 6 and the 5th term is 162. What is the common ratio?
questions.solution: From the 2nd to the 5th term there are 3 steps, so the ratio cubed is $162 \div 6 = 27$. Since $3^3 = 27$, the common ratio is 3.

questions.skill: Geometric sequences: ratio, terms and formulas
questions.stem: In a geometric sequence, the 3rd term is 12 and the 4th term is 18. What is the 6th term?
questions.solution: The common ratio is $18 \div 12 = 1.5$. The 5th term is $18 \times 1.5 = 27$ and the 6th term is $27 \times 1.5 = 40.5$.

questions.skill: Geometric sequences: ratio, terms and formulas
questions.stem: The numbers 4, $k$, $m$, 108 are four consecutive terms of a geometric sequence whose terms are all positive. What is $k + m$?
questions.solution: From 4 to 108 there are 3 steps, so the ratio cubed is $108 \div 4 = 27$ and the ratio is 3. Then $k = 4 \times 3 = 12$ and $m = 12 \times 3 = 36$, so $k + m = 48$.

questions.skill: Geometric sequences: ratio, terms and formulas
questions.stem: Which sequence is geometric with common ratio $-\frac{1}{2}$?
questions.solution: Multiply by $-\frac{1}{2}$ each time: $48 \times \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = -24$, then $12$, then $-6$. The list 48, 24, 12, 6 has ratio $\frac{1}{2}$, the list $-6$, 12, $-24$, 48 has ratio $-2$, and the last list is arithmetic.

questions.skill: Predict a value from a table
questions.stem: For an exponential relationship with positive values, $y = 5$ when $x = 0$ and $y = 80$ when $x = 4$. What is $y$ when $x = 2$?
questions.solution: From $x = 0$ to $x = 4$, $y$ is multiplied by $80 \div 5 = 16$, which is 4 steps of the same factor. Since $2^4 = 16$, the factor is 2. At $x = 2$, $y = 5 \times 2^2 = 20$.

questions.skill: Predict a value from a table
questions.stem: A linear relationship has $y = 4, 10, 16, 22$ when $x = 0, 3, 6, 9$. What is $y$ when $x = 20$?
questions.solution: When $x$ goes up by 3, $y$ goes up by 6, so $y$ goes up by 2 for each increase of 1 in $x$. At $x = 20$, $y = 4 + 20 \times 2 = 44$.

solve.work: y rises 6 per 3 in x: slope 2, y = 2x + 4. At x=20: 44.

questions.skill: Predict a value from a table
questions.stem: A table gives $y = 2000, 1600, 1280, 1024$ at $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$, and each value is the same multiple of the one before it. Which expression gives $y$ when $x = 5$?
questions.solution: The multiple is $1600 \div 2000 = 0.8$, and $1280 \div 1600 = 0.8$. Starting from 2000 and multiplying by 0.8 five times gives $2000(0.8)^5$. The expression $2000 - 400(5)$ would be a linear pattern.

questions.skill: Predict a value from points on a graph
questions.stem: The graph of an exponential relationship passes through $(1, 12)$ and $(2, 36)$. What is the $y$-coordinate of the point where the graph crosses the $y$-axis?
questions.solution: Each $y$-value is $36 \div 12 = 3$ times the one before. The $y$-axis is where $x = 0$, one step before $x = 1$, so divide by 3: $12 \div 3 = 4$.

questions.skill: Predict a value from points on a graph
questions.stem: A straight line passes through the points $(-2, 11)$ and $(4, -7)$. What is the $y$-coordinate of the point on the line with $x = 1$?
questions.solution: From $x = -2$ to $x = 4$ (6 steps), $y$ changes by $-7 - 11 = -18$, so the rate is $-3$ per step. From $x = 4$ back to $x = 1$ is 3 steps down, so $y = -7 + 3 \times 3 = 2$.

questions.skill: Predict a value from points on a graph
questions.stem: The graph of an exponential relationship passes through $(0, 9)$ and $(1, 6)$. Which point is also on the graph?
questions.solution: Each $y$-value is $6 \div 9 = \frac{2}{3}$ times the one before. At $x = 2$, $y = 6 \times \frac{2}{3} = 4$. The point $(2, 3)$ would come from subtracting 3 each time (a line).

solve.work: Ratio 6/9 = 2/3: y = 9(2/3)^x. x=2: 9*4/9 = 4; x=3: 8/3. So (2,4). (2,3) is the linear continuation; (2,12) and (3,4) are not on it.

questions.skill: Predict a value from points on a graph
questions.stem: A straight line passes through the points $(3, 10)$ and $(7, 22)$. At what $x$-value does the line reach $y = 40$?
questions.solution: From $x = 3$ to $x = 7$, $y$ goes up by 12, so $y$ goes up by 3 for each increase of 1 in $x$. From $y = 22$ to $y = 40$ is 18 more, which takes $18 \div 3 = 6$ steps. So $x = 7 + 6 = 13$.

questions.skill: Compare linear and exponential growth
questions.stem: For how many whole numbers $x$ with $x \ge 1$ is $2^x$ less than $5x$?
questions.solution: Check each value: $x = 1$: $2 < 5$. $x = 2$: $4 < 10$. $x = 3$: $8 < 15$. $x = 4$: $16 < 20$. $x = 5$: $32 > 25$, and from then on $2^x$ stays greater (for example $x = 6$: $64 > 30$). So there are 4 such numbers.

solve.work: x=1: 2<5; x=2: 4<10; x=3: 8<15; x=4: 16<20 (all yes). x=5: 32>25; x=6: 64>30, and 2^x keeps doubling while 5x adds 5, so no more. Count = 4.

questions.skill: Compare linear and exponential growth
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 4x + 4$ and $g(x) = 4(2)^x$. Which statement about whole-number values of $x$ is true?
choices: They are equal at $x = 0$ and $x = 1$, and $f(x) > g(x)$ for every whole number $x \ge 2$
They are equal for every whole number $x$
$g(x) > f(x)$ for every whole number $x \ge 0$
They are equal at $x = 0$ and $x = 1$, and $g(x) > f(x)$ for every whole number $x \ge 2$
questions.answer: They are equal at $x = 0$ and $x = 1$, and $g(x) > f(x)$ for every whole number $x \ge 2$
questions.solution: $x = 0$: both are 4. $x = 1$: both are 8. $x = 2$: $f = 12$, $g = 16$. $x = 3$: $f = 16$, $g = 32$. $x = 4$: $f = 20$, $g = 64$. The exponential function pulls ahead from $x = 2$ on.

solve.answer: They are equal at $x = 0$ and $x = 1$, and $g(x) > f(x)$ for every whole number $x \ge 2$
solve.work: f(0)=4, g(0)=4; f(1)=8, g(1)=8: equal at 0 and 1. f(2)=12, g(2)=16; f(3)=16, g(3)=32; g doubles while f adds 4, so g>f for all x>=2.

questions.skill: Compare linear and exponential growth
questions.stem: Town A has 5000 people and gains 250 people each year. Town B has 4000 people and grows by 10% each year. After 3 years, how many more people live in Town A than in Town B?

questions.skill: Compare linear and exponential growth
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 1000x$ and $g(x) = 1.1^x$. At $x = 1$, $f(1)$ is much greater than $g(1)$. Which statement is true for very large values of $x$?
choices: $g(x)$ eventually becomes greater, because $g$ is multiplied by 1.1 each step but $f$ only adds 1000
$f(x)$ stays greater than $g(x)$, because 1000 is much larger than 1.1
$g(x)$ never catches up with $f(x)$, because 1.1 is close to 1
$f(x)$ and $g(x)$ become equal at some point and then stay equal
questions.answer: $g(x)$ eventually becomes greater, because $g$ is multiplied by 1.1 each step but $f$ only adds 1000
questions.solution: Each step adds the same 1000 to $f$, but each step multiplies $g$ by 1.1, so the amount $g$ gains each step keeps growing. Eventually the gain of $g$ per step is more than 1000 and $g$ catches up with and passes $f$.

solve.answer: $g(x)$ eventually becomes greater, because $g$ is multiplied by 1.1 each step but $f$ only adds 1000
solve.work: Any exponential with base > 1 eventually exceeds any linear function: g multiplies by 1.1 per unit of x, f adds 1000. E.g. 1.1^200 is about 1.9e8 > 200000. So g eventually becomes greater (and stays greater).

questions.skill: Compare linear and exponential growth
questions.stem: Plan A pays 1 cent on day 1, 2 cents on day 2, 4 cents on day 3, and keeps doubling each day. Plan B pays 20 cents on day 1, 40 cents on day 2, 60 cents on day 3, and keeps adding 20 cents each day. On what day does Plan A's payment first exceed Plan B's payment?
questions.solution: On day $n$, Plan A pays $2^{n-1}$ cents and Plan B pays $20n$ cents. Day 8: 128 compared with 160. Day 9: 256 compared with 180. Plan A first pays more on day 9.

solve.work: A on day n: 2^(n-1) cents; B: 20n cents. Day 7: 64 vs 140; day 8: 128 vs 160; day 9: 256 vs 180. A first exceeds B on day 9.

questions.skill: Choose a reasonable domain in context
questions.stem: A bakery sells muffins for 2 dollars each, so the cost of $n$ muffins is $C(n) = 2n$ dollars. Which set is the most reasonable domain of $C$?
choices: All real numbers
The even numbers 0, 2, 4, 6, and so on
All real numbers greater than 2
Whole numbers: 0, 1, 2, 3, and so on
questions.answer: Whole numbers: 0, 1, 2, 3, and so on
questions.solution: The domain is the set of possible inputs. You cannot buy part of a muffin or a negative number of muffins, so the inputs are the whole numbers. The even numbers 0, 2, 4, 6 are the possible costs (outputs), not the inputs.

solve.answer: Whole numbers: 0, 1, 2, 3, and so on
solve.work: You buy a whole number of muffins, including possibly 0: domain {0,1,2,...}. Not all reals, not only evens, not reals > 2.

questions.skill: Tell growth from decay
questions.stem: Which statement describes $f(x) = 5(0.8)^x$?
choices: Exponential decay
Exponential growth
Linear increase
Linear decrease
questions.answer: Exponential decay
questions.solution: The variable is in the exponent, so the function is exponential. The base 0.8 is less than 1, so each step multiplies the value by 0.8 and it gets smaller: decay.

solve.answer: Exponential decay
solve.work: Form a(b)^x with a = 5 > 0 and 0 < b = 0.8 < 1 -> exponential decay.

questions.stem: A function is given by $h(t) = 20 - 3t$. What is $h(4)$?
questions.solution: Replace $t$ with 4: $h(4) = 20 - 3 \times 4 = 20 - 12 = 8$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a function written in function notation
questions.stem: If $f(x) = x + 8$, which statement is true?
questions.solution: $f(5) = 5 + 8 = 13$. The statement $f(5) = 40$ multiplies instead of adding, $f(13) = 5$ swaps the input and the output, and $f(5) = 3$ subtracts.

questions.skill: Evaluate and interpret a function in context
questions.stem: A colony has $N(t) = 100(2)^t$ bacteria after $t$ hours. How many bacteria are there after 3 hours?
questions.solution: $N(3) = 100 \times 2^3 = 100 \times 8 = 800$ bacteria.

questions.skill: Evaluate and interpret a function in context
questions.stem: $C(n)$ is the cost, in dollars, of $n$ movie tickets. What does $C(4) = 36$ tell you?
choices: 36 tickets cost 4 dollars
Each ticket costs 36 dollars
Each ticket costs 4 dollars
4 tickets cost 36 dollars
questions.answer: 4 tickets cost 36 dollars
questions.solution: The input is the number of tickets and the output is the cost. $C(4) = 36$ means that 4 tickets cost 36 dollars (so each ticket costs 9 dollars).

solve.answer: 4 tickets cost 36 dollars
solve.work: C(n) is the cost of n tickets; C(4) = 36 means 4 tickets cost 36 dollars (9 each).

questions.skill: Evaluate and interpret a function in context
questions.stem: Tia has saved $S(w) = 50 + 15w$ dollars after $w$ weeks. How many dollars had she saved at the very start, when $w = 0$?
questions.solution: $S(0) = 50 + 15 \times 0 = 50$ dollars.

questions.skill: Evaluate and interpret a function in context
questions.stem: The height of a plant, in centimeters, is $H(w) = 12 + 3w$ after $w$ weeks. Which question does $H(4)$ answer?
choices: After how many weeks is the plant 4 centimeters tall?
How many centimeters does the plant grow each week?
How tall is the plant after 4 weeks?
How tall was the plant at the start?
questions.answer: How tall is the plant after 4 weeks?
questions.solution: The input $w$ is the number of weeks and the output is the height. $H(4)$ is the height when $w = 4$, which is the height after 4 weeks.

solve.answer: How tall is the plant after 4 weeks?
solve.work: H(4) is the height when w = 4, i.e. after 4 weeks: 12 + 12 = 24 cm. It answers "How tall is the plant after 4 weeks?"

questions.skill: Find the domain of a function
questions.stem: A store lets each customer buy 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 notebooks. A function gives the cost of $n$ notebooks. Which set is the domain of this function?
choices: All real numbers
The set of possible costs
All real numbers between 1 and 5
questions.solution: The domain is the set of possible inputs. The inputs are the numbers of notebooks a customer may buy: 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5. The costs are the outputs, which make up the range.

solve.work: The inputs are the allowed numbers of notebooks: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Domain = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. Not every real number between 1 and 5 (no fractional notebooks); costs are the range.

questions.skill: Find the domain of a function
questions.stem: The function $f(x) = 3x + 1$ can be used with any real number $x$. What is its domain?
choices: $x \ge 1$
All real numbers
$x \ge 0$
questions.answer: All real numbers
questions.solution: Any real number can be multiplied by 3 and then have 1 added, so every real number is an allowed input. The domain is all real numbers.

solve.answer: All real numbers
solve.work: Any real x may be used, so the domain is all real numbers.

questions.skill: Find the domain of a function
questions.stem: A function has these input-output pairs: $(2, 7)$, $(4, 11)$, $(6, 15)$ and $(8, 19)$. What is the sum of the numbers in its domain?
questions.solution: The domain is the set of inputs, the first numbers of the pairs: 2, 4, 6 and 8. Their sum is $2 + 4 + 6 + 8 = 20$.

questions.skill: Find the domain of a function
questions.stem: The function $T(h) = 12h$ gives the pay, in dollars, for working $h$ hours, where $h$ can be any number from 0 to 8. Which number is NOT in the domain?
questions.solution: The domain is the numbers from 0 to 8, including 0 and 8. The numbers 0, 3.5 and 8 are all in it. The number $-2$ is less than 0, so it is not.

solve.work: Domain is 0 <= h <= 8. 3.5, 0 and 8 are in it; -2 is not.

questions.skill: Find the range of a function
questions.stem: A function has these input-output pairs: $(1, 4)$, $(2, 7)$ and $(3, 10)$. What is the range of the function?
choices: All real numbers
questions.solution: The range is the set of outputs, the second numbers of the pairs: 4, 7 and 10. The set $\{1, 2, 3\}$ is the domain.

questions.skill: Find the range of a function
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 2x + 1$ with domain $\{0, 1, 2, 3\}$. What is the largest number in the range?
questions.solution: The outputs are $f(0) = 1$, $f(1) = 3$, $f(2) = 5$ and $f(3) = 7$. The largest is 7.

questions.skill: Find the range of a function
questions.stem: The function $f(x) = 2x$ is defined for all real numbers $x$. What is its range?
choices: All real numbers
$y \ge 0$
All whole numbers
questions.answer: All real numbers
questions.solution: Any real number $y$ is an output, because $x = y \div 2$ gives $f(x) = y$ (negative outputs come from negative inputs). So the range is all real numbers.

solve.answer: All real numbers
solve.work: For any real y, x = y/2 gives f(x) = y. Range is all real numbers.

questions.skill: Decide whether a function is discrete or continuous
questions.stem: Which quantity is discrete?
choices: The number of cars in a parking lot
The weight of a bag of apples
The time it takes to run a race
The temperature of a room
questions.answer: The number of cars in a parking lot
questions.solution: A discrete quantity is counted in separate values, such as whole numbers. Cars can be counted: 0, 1, 2, and so on. Weight, time and temperature can take any value in a range, so they are continuous.

solve.answer: The number of cars in a parking lot
solve.work: Cars are counted in whole numbers -> discrete. Time, weight and temperature are measured and can take any value in an interval -> continuous.

questions.skill: Decide whether a function is discrete or continuous
questions.stem: Which quantity is continuous?
choices: The number of tickets sold
The amount of juice in a glass as it is poured
The number of students absent
The number of goals scored
questions.answer: The amount of juice in a glass as it is poured
questions.solution: A continuous quantity can take any value in a range, including parts of a unit. The amount of juice can be 100.5 milliliters or 100.52 milliliters. Tickets, students and goals are counted in whole numbers, so they are discrete.

solve.answer: The amount of juice in a glass as it is poured
solve.work: Amount of juice being poured can take any value -> continuous. Students absent, goals, tickets are counts -> discrete.

questions.skill: Decide whether a function is discrete or continuous
questions.stem: A function gives the cost of $n$ pencils, where $n$ is 0, 1, 2, 3, and so on. Is the function discrete or continuous, and why?
choices: Continuous, because $n$ can be any number
Continuous, because the cost goes up steadily
Continuous, because the cost can be any amount of money
Discrete, because $n$ can only be a whole number
questions.answer: Discrete, because $n$ can only be a whole number
questions.solution: You cannot buy 2.5 pencils, so the inputs are only whole numbers. A function whose inputs are separate values like this is discrete.

solve.answer: Discrete, because $n$ can only be a whole number
solve.work: Inputs n are 0, 1, 2, 3, ... (whole numbers only), so the graph is separate points -> discrete.

questions.skill: Decide whether a function is discrete or continuous
questions.stem: What does the graph of a discrete function look like?
choices: A solid line with no breaks
A smooth curve with no breaks
A set of separate points
A shaded region
questions.answer: A set of separate points
questions.solution: A discrete function is defined only at separate input values, so its graph is separate points. A solid line or a smooth curve with no breaks is the graph of a continuous function.

solve.answer: A set of separate points
solve.work: A discrete function is defined only at separate input values, so its graph is a set of separate (unconnected) points.

questions.skill: Tell growth from decay and find the factor or rate
questions.stem: Which function shows exponential growth?
questions.solution: Exponential growth has $x$ in the exponent and a base greater than 1. In $3(1.5)^x$ the base is 1.5. The bases 0.5 and 0.9 give decay, and $1.5x$ is linear, not exponential.

solve.work: Exponential growth needs a(b)^x with a > 0, b > 1. 3(1.5)^x: b = 1.5 > 1 -> growth. 0.5(0.9)^x and 3(0.5)^x are decay; 1.5x is linear.

questions.skill: Tell growth from decay and find the factor or rate
questions.stem: In the function $f(x) = 6(3)^x$, what is the growth factor?
questions.solution: An exponential function $f(x) = a \cdot b^x$ has initial value $a$ and growth factor $b$. Here $a = 6$ and $b = 3$, so the growth factor is 3.

solve.work: f(x) = 6(3)^x: base 3 is the growth factor.

questions.skill: Tell growth from decay and find the factor or rate
questions.stem: What is the initial value (the value when $x = 0$) of $f(x) = 40(0.5)^x$?
questions.solution: $f(0) = 40 \times 0.5^0 = 40 \times 1 = 40$. In $f(x) = a \cdot b^x$ the initial value is $a$.

questions.skill: Tell growth from decay and find the factor or rate
questions.stem: The value of a car is multiplied by 0.85 every year. What kind of change is this?
choices: Exponential growth
Exponential decay
Linear decay
Linear growth
questions.answer: Exponential decay
questions.solution: The value is multiplied by the same number each year, so the change is exponential. The number 0.85 is less than 1, so the value gets smaller: exponential decay.

solve.answer: Exponential decay
solve.work: Multiplying by a constant factor 0.85 (between 0 and 1) each year -> exponential decay.

questions.skill: Find and use an average rate of change
questions.stem: A plant is 12 centimeters tall at week 2 and 30 centimeters tall at week 5. What is its average rate of change, in centimeters per week?
questions.solution: Average rate of change = change in height $\div$ change in time $= (30 - 12) \div (5 - 2) = 18 \div 3 = 6$.

questions.skill: Find and use an average rate of change
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 4x + 3$. What is the average rate of change of $f$ from $x = 1$ to $x = 5$?
questions.solution: $f(1) = 7$ and $f(5) = 23$. The average rate of change is $(23 - 7) \div (5 - 1) = 16 \div 4 = 4$.

questions.skill: Find and use an average rate of change
questions.stem: A tank holds 90 liters at minute 0 and 60 liters at minute 5. What is the average rate of change of the amount of water, in liters per minute?
questions.solution: The change is $60 - 90 = -30$ liters over 5 minutes, so the average rate of change is $-30 \div 5 = -6$ liters per minute.

questions.skill: Find and use an average rate of change
questions.stem: Which expression gives the average rate of change of a function $f$ from $x = a$ to $x = b$?
choices: $\frac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}$
$\frac{f(b) - f(a)}{a - b}$
$\frac{f(b) + f(a)}{b + a}$
$\frac{b - a}{f(b) - f(a)}$
questions.answer: $\frac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}$
questions.solution: The average rate of change is the change in output divided by the change in input: $\frac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}$. The other expressions flip the sign of the denominator, add instead of subtract, or turn the fraction upside down.

solve.answer: $\frac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}$
solve.work: Average rate of change = change in output / change in input = (f(b) - f(a))/(b - a).

questions.skill: Compare two functions
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 3x + 2$ and $g(x) = 5x + 1$. Which function has the greater rate of change?
choices: $f$, because 2 is greater than 1
They have the same rate of change
$g$, because 5 is greater than 3
$f$, because 3 is greater than 1
questions.answer: $g$, because 5 is greater than 3
questions.solution: In $y = mx + b$ the rate of change is $m$. For $f$ it is 3 and for $g$ it is 5, so $g$ changes faster. The numbers 2 and 1 are the starting values, not the rates.

solve.answer: $g$, because 5 is greater than 3
solve.work: Rates (slopes): f has 3, g has 5. g has the greater rate of change because 5 > 3. The constants 2 and 1 are intercepts.

questions.skill: Compare two functions
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 2x + 6$ and $g(x) = 3x$. How much greater is $f(2)$ than $g(2)$?
questions.solution: $f(2) = 2 \times 2 + 6 = 10$ and $g(2) = 3 \times 2 = 6$. The difference is $10 - 6 = 4$.

questions.skill: Compare two functions
questions.stem: Function $f$ has $f(0) = 2$, $f(1) = 4$, $f(2) = 6$ and $f(3) = 8$. Function $g$ is $g(x) = 3x + 1$. Which function has the greater rate of change?
choices: $g$, with a rate of 3 compared with 2
$f$, with a rate of 2 compared with 1
They have the same rate of change, 2
$f$, because $f(0) = 2$ is greater than $g(0) = 1$
questions.answer: $g$, with a rate of 3 compared with 2
questions.solution: The values of $f$ go up by 2 each time $x$ goes up by 1, so its rate is 2. For $g(x) = 3x + 1$ the rate is 3. So $g$ has the greater rate of change.

solve.answer: $g$, with a rate of 3 compared with 2
solve.work: f rises 2 per unit (2,4,6,8): rate 2. g(x) = 3x + 1: rate 3. g has the greater rate, 3 vs 2.

questions.skill: Find an average rate of change
questions.stem: For a function $f$, $f(2) = 7$ and $f(6) = 19$. What is the average rate of change of $f$ from $x = 2$ to $x = 6$?
questions.solution: Average rate of change is the change in output divided by the change in input: $\frac{19 - 7}{6 - 2} = \frac{12}{4} = 3$.

questions.skill: Decide whether a function in context is discrete or continuous
questions.stem: A car travels at a steady 60 miles per hour, so after $t$ hours it has gone $d(t) = 60t$ miles, where $t$ can be any time from 0 to 5 hours. Which statement is true?
choices: The graph is discrete because distance is measured in miles
The graph is continuous because $t$ can be any value from 0 to 5
The graph is discrete because 60 is a whole number
The graph is continuous only because it passes through the origin
questions.answer: The graph is continuous because $t$ can be any value from 0 to 5
questions.solution: A function is continuous when its inputs can be any value in an interval. Time can be any value from 0 to 5 hours, including parts of an hour, so the graph is continuous. The units and the number 60 do not decide this.

solve.answer: The graph is continuous because $t$ can be any value from 0 to 5
solve.work: Time can take any value in [0, 5], so the graph is an unbroken segment: continuous for that reason. The other options give wrong reasons.

questions.skill: Evaluate a function written in function notation
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 3x - 8$. For what value of $x$ is $f(x) = 19$?
questions.solution: Solve $3x - 8 = 19$. Add 8: $3x = 27$. Divide by 3: $x = 9$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a function written in function notation

questions.skill: Evaluate a function written in function notation
questions.stem: If $f(x) = 5 - 2x$, which expression is equal to $f(a + 1)$?
questions.solution: Replace $x$ with $a + 1$: $f(a + 1) = 5 - 2(a + 1) = 5 - 2a - 2 = 3 - 2a$. The expression $6 - 2a$ forgets to multiply the 1 by $-2$, and $4 - 2a$ subtracts 1 instead of 2.

questions.skill: Evaluate and interpret a function in context
questions.stem: The number of bacteria in a dish is $B(t) = 500(2)^t$, where $t$ is in hours. What does $B(0) = 500$ tell you?
choices: There were 500 bacteria after 1 hour
There were 500 bacteria at the start
The number of bacteria doubles every 500 hours
There were no bacteria after 500 hours
questions.answer: There were 500 bacteria at the start
questions.solution: The input $t = 0$ is the start (zero hours have passed). The output $B(0) = 500$ is the number of bacteria then, so there were 500 bacteria at the start.

solve.answer: There were 500 bacteria at the start
solve.work: t = 0 is the start; B(0) = 500 means 500 bacteria at the start.

questions.skill: Evaluate and interpret a function in context
questions.stem: Renting a bike costs $C(h) = 8 + 3h$ dollars for $h$ hours. For how many hours was the bike rented if the cost was 29 dollars?
questions.solution: Solve $8 + 3h = 29$. Subtract 8: $3h = 21$. Divide by 3: $h = 7$ hours.

questions.skill: Evaluate and interpret a function in context
questions.stem: $P(t)$ is a town's population $t$ years after the year 2020. If $P(4) = 3500$, which statement is true?
choices: In 2020 the population was 3500
The population grew by 3500 people in 4 years
In 2024 the population was 3500
In 2023 the population was 3500
questions.answer: In 2024 the population was 3500
questions.solution: The input $t = 4$ means 4 years after 2020, which is 2024. The output $P(4) = 3500$ is the population then, so in 2024 the population was 3500.

solve.answer: In 2024 the population was 3500
solve.work: t = 4 means 4 years after 2020, i.e. 2024. P(4) = 3500: the population in 2024 was 3500.

questions.skill: Find the domain of a function
questions.stem: A tank holds 50 gallons. Water drains out so that the amount left after $t$ minutes is $A(t) = 50 - 5t$, until the tank is empty. Which is the domain of $A$?
choices: $0 \le t \le 10$
$0 \le t \le 50$
$t \ge 0$
$0 \le t \le 5$
questions.answer: $0 \le t \le 10$
questions.solution: The tank is empty when $50 - 5t = 0$, which is $t = 10$. The times that make sense run from the start, $t = 0$, to the time the tank is empty, $t = 10$.

solve.answer: $0 \le t \le 10$

questions.stem: A customer can buy at most 8 T-shirts, which cost 12 dollars each. A function gives the cost of $n$ T-shirts. Which set is its domain?
choices: Whole numbers from 0 through 96
All real numbers from 0 to 8
All real numbers from 0 to 96
Whole numbers from 0 through 8
questions.answer: Whole numbers from 0 through 8

questions.solution: The ball reaches the bottom when $8t = 120$, so $t = 120 \div 8 = 15$ seconds. That is the greatest allowed input.

questions.skill: Decide whether a function is discrete or continuous

questions.skill: Decide whether a function is discrete or continuous
