choices: The function is discrete, because it is defined only at whole numbers of hours
The function is continuous, because every exponential function is continuous
The function is continuous, because time is always continuous
The function is continuous, because a colony grows all the time
questions.answer: The function is discrete, because it is defined only at whole numbers of hours
questions.solution: This function has inputs only at $h = 0, 1, 2, \dots$, so its graph is separate points. A function defined only at whole-number inputs is discrete, even though it comes from an exponential rule.

questions.skill: Decide whether a function is discrete or continuous
questions.stem: How many of these four quantities are continuous? (1) the number of pages in a book, (2) the length of a rope as it is stretched, (3) the number of students in a school, (4) the speed of a car.
questions.solution: Pages and students are counted in whole numbers, so they are discrete. Length and speed can take any value in a range, so they are continuous. There are 2 continuous quantities.

questions.skill: Decide whether a function is discrete or continuous

$x$ can only be 0 or 10
$x$ can be any real number from 0 to 10
questions.answer: $x$ can be any real number from 0 to 10

solve.answer: $x$ can be any real number from 0 to 10
solve.work: A solid segment from x = 0 to x = 10 includes every x in between: domain 0 <= x <= 10 (all reals). 5 to 25 is the range.

questions.skill: Tell growth from decay and find the factor or rate
questions.stem: A bicycle loses 20% of its value each year. By what number is its value multiplied from one year to the next?
questions.solution: Losing 20% means 80% of the value is kept, and 80% is $0.8$. So the value is multiplied by 0.8 each year.

questions.skill: Tell growth from decay and find the factor or rate
questions.stem: Which function describes a quantity that decays by 25% each period?
questions.solution: Decaying by 25% leaves 75% of the amount, so the factor is $0.75$: $f(x) = 100(0.75)^x$. A factor of 0.25 would lose 75% each period, 1.25 is growth, and $100 - 0.25x$ is linear.

solve.work: Decay of 25% leaves 75% each period: factor 0.75. f(x) = 100(0.75)^x. 1.25 is growth; 0.25 is decay of 75%; 100 - 0.25x is linear.

questions.skill: Tell growth from decay and find the factor or rate
questions.stem: For $f(x) = 200(1.05)^x$, what is the percent growth rate per period? Give the number of percent.
questions.solution: The growth factor is $1.05 = 1 + 0.05$, so the quantity grows by $0.05 = 5\%$ each period.

questions.skill: Find and use an average rate of change
questions.stem: Let $g(x) = 3^x$. What is the average rate of change of $g$ from $x = 0$ to $x = 2$?
questions.solution: $g(0) = 1$ and $g(2) = 9$. The average rate of change is $(9 - 1) \div (2 - 0) = 8 \div 2 = 4$.

questions.skill: Find and use an average rate of change
questions.stem: A function has $f(0) = 4$, $f(2) = 10$, $f(5) = 19$ and $f(9) = 31$. What is the average rate of change of $f$ from $x = 2$ to $x = 9$?
questions.solution: The change in output is $31 - 10 = 21$ and the change in input is $9 - 2 = 7$. The average rate of change is $21 \div 7 = 3$.

questions.skill: Find and use an average rate of change
questions.stem: A town had $15{,}600$ residents in 2012 and $14{,}000$ residents in 2020. What was the average rate of change of its population, in people per year?
questions.solution: The change is $14000 - 15600 = -1600$ people over $2020 - 2012 = 8$ years, so the average rate of change is $-1600 \div 8 = -200$ people per year.

questions.skill: Find and use an average rate of change
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 80(0.5)^x$. What is the average rate of change of $f$ from $x = 1$ to $x = 3$?
questions.solution: $f(1) = 40$ and $f(3) = 10$. The average rate of change is $(10 - 40) \div (3 - 1) = -30 \div 2 = -15$.

questions.skill: Compare two functions

$f$ has the greater rate of change, and $g$ has the greater $y$-intercept
$f$ has both the greater rate of change and the greater $y$-intercept
$g$ has the greater rate of change, and $f$ has the greater $y$-intercept
questions.answer: $f$ has the greater rate of change, and $g$ has the greater $y$-intercept
questions.solution: The rate of $f$ is 6 and the rate of $g$ is 5 (its values go up by 5 each time), so $f$ changes faster. The $y$-intercept of $f$ is $-4$ and of $g$ is $g(0) = 3$, so $g$ has the greater $y$-intercept.

solve.answer: $f$ has the greater rate of change, and $g$ has the greater $y$-intercept
solve.work: f: rate 6, y-intercept -4. g: rate 5 (3, 8, 13), y-intercept 3. f has the greater rate; g has the greater y-intercept.

questions.skill: Compare two functions
questions.stem: Plan A costs $C = 12 + 4m$ dollars for $m$ miles. Plan B costs $D = 6m$ dollars. For how many miles do the two plans cost the same?
questions.solution: Set $12 + 4m = 6m$. Subtract $4m$: $12 = 2m$, so $m = 6$. Check: both plans cost 36 dollars for 6 miles.

questions.skill: Compare two functions
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 100(0.9)^x$ and $g(x) = 100(0.7)^x$. Which statement is true?
choices: $f$ decays faster, because 0.9 is greater than 0.7

questions.answer: $g$ decays faster, because it loses 30% each step while $f$ loses 10%
questions.solution: The factor 0.9 keeps 90% of the value (a loss of 10% per step) and the factor 0.7 keeps 70% (a loss of 30% per step). The smaller factor means faster decay, so $g$ decays faster.

solve.answer: $g$ decays faster, because it loses 30% each step while $f$ loses 10%
solve.work: f keeps 90% (loses 10%) per step; g keeps 70% (loses 30%). g decays faster.

questions.skill: Compare two functions
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 7x + 2$. Function $g$ is linear with $g(0) = 30$ and $g(5) = 10$. How much greater is the rate of change of $f$ than the rate of change of $g$?
questions.solution: The rate of $f$ is 7. The rate of $g$ is $(10 - 30) \div 5 = -4$. The difference is $7 - (-4) = 11$.

solve.answer: Decay of 15% per step

questions.skill: Find the range of an exponential function
questions.stem: Let $g(x) = 2(3)^x$ for all real numbers $x$. What is the range of $g$?
choices: All real numbers
$y \ge 2$
$y \ge 0$
questions.solution: A positive number raised to any power is positive, and $2(3)^x$ gets as close to 0 as you like for very negative $x$ without ever reaching it. So every output is greater than 0, and every positive number is an output: $y > 0$.

solve.work: 3^x > 0 for all real x and takes every positive value, so 2(3)^x takes every value > 0, never 0. Range y > 0. (y >= 2 is wrong: e.g. g(-1) = 2/3.)

questions.skill: Compare the rates of change of two functions
questions.stem: Function $f$ is $f(x) = 5x - 2$. Function $g$ is linear with $g(0) = 1$, $g(2) = 9$ and $g(4) = 17$. Which function has the greater rate of change, and what are the two rates?
choices: $g$ has the greater rate: 8 compared with 5
$g$ has the greater rate: 16 compared with 5
$f$ has the greater rate: 5 compared with 4
The rates are equal: both are 4
questions.answer: $f$ has the greater rate: 5 compared with 4
questions.solution: The rate of change of $f$ is its slope, 5. For $g$, the output rises from 1 to 9 while the input rises by 2, so the rate is $\frac{9 - 1}{2} = 4$ (the same from 2 to 4: $\frac{17 - 9}{2} = 4$). Since $5 > 4$, $f$ has the greater rate.

solve.answer: $f$ has the greater rate: 5 compared with 4

questions.skill: Average rate of change of an exponential function
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 3(2)^x$. What is the average rate of change of $f$ from $x = 1$ to $x = 3$?
questions.solution: $f(1) = 3(2) = 6$ and $f(3) = 3(8) = 24$. The average rate of change is $\frac{24 - 6}{3 - 1} = \frac{18}{2} = 9$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a function written in function notation
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 2x + 3$. If $f(a) = 17$, what is $f(a + 2)$?
questions.solution: Adding 2 to the input adds $2 \times 2 = 4$ to the output, because the rate of $f$ is 2. So $f(a + 2) = 17 + 4 = 21$. (Or solve $2a + 3 = 17$ to get $a = 7$, then $f(9) = 21$.)

questions.solution: Halve 200 repeatedly: 100 after 1 hour, 50 after 2, 25 after 3 and 12.5 after 4. So $M(4) = 12.5$ and the answer is 4 hours.

questions.skill: Evaluate and interpret a function in context

questions.answer: For how many extra days does the rental cost 47 dollars?
questions.solution: Solving $C(n) = 47$ means the output (the cost) is 47 and the unknown is the input $n$ (the extra days). So it answers: for how many extra days does the rental cost 47 dollars? (Here $15 + 4n = 47$ gives $n = 8$.)

solve.answer: For how many extra days does the rental cost 47 dollars?
solve.work: Solving C(n) = 47 finds the input n giving output 47: the number of extra days for which the cost is 47 dollars (n = 8).

questions.skill: Decide whether a function is discrete or continuous

The whole numbers $x$ with $1 < x < 5$

questions.skill: Find and use an average rate of change

questions.solution: Each interval has length 2. The average rates are $(4 - 1) \div 2 = 1.5$, $(8 - 2) \div 2 = 3$, $(16 - 4) \div 2 = 6$ and $(32 - 8) \div 2 = 12$. The greatest is from $x = 3$ to $x = 5$. The rate of an exponential growth function keeps increasing.

solve.answer: From $x = 3$ to $x = 5$

questions.skill: Find and use an average rate of change

questions.skill: Find and use an average rate of change
questions.stem: For which kind of function is the average rate of change the same on every interval of $x$-values?

Linear functions
Both linear and exponential functions
Neither linear nor exponential functions
questions.answer: Linear functions
questions.solution: A linear function changes by the same amount for every equal step in $x$, so its average rate of change is its slope on every interval. An exponential function changes by more or less on each step, so its average rate of change depends on the interval.

solve.answer: Linear functions
solve.work: Only a linear function has a constant rate of change on every interval; an exponential function's average rate of change varies with the interval.

questions.skill: Find and use an average rate of change

questions.solution: The change in temperature is $50 - 70 = -20$ degrees over $15 - 5 = 10$ minutes, so the average rate of change is $-20 \div 10 = -2$ degrees per minute.

questions.solution: The rate of $f$ is $8 - 5 = 3$, so $f(3) = 5 + 3 \times 3 = 14$. Also $g(3) = 2 \times 3^3 = 54$. The difference is $54 - 14 = 40$.

questions.skill: Compare two functions
questions.stem: Function $f$ is $f(x) = 4(2)^x$. Function $g$ is $g(x) = 6x + 1$. Function $h$ is exponential with $h(0) = 5$ and $h(1) = 15$. What is the greatest of $f(3)$, $g(3)$ and $h(3)$?
questions.solution: $f(3) = 4 \times 8 = 32$ and $g(3) = 6 \times 3 + 1 = 19$. For $h$ the factor is $15 \div 5 = 3$, so $h(3) = 5 \times 3^3 = 135$. The greatest is 135.

questions.skill: Compare two functions
questions.stem: Let $f(x) = 10 + 2x$ and $g(x) = 10(1.2)^x$. Which statement is true?
choices: They are equal at $x = 0$ and at $x = 1$, and $g$ is greater at $x = 2$
They are equal at $x = 0$, and $g$ is greater at $x = 1$
$f$ is greater than $g$ at $x = 2$
$g$ is less than $f$ for every $x > 0$
questions.answer: They are equal at $x = 0$ and at $x = 1$, and $g$ is greater at $x = 2$

solve.answer: They are equal at $x = 0$ and at $x = 1$, and $g$ is greater at $x = 2$
solve.work: f(0) = 10 = g(0); f(1) = 12, g(1) = 12 (equal); f(2) = 14, g(2) = 10*1.44 = 14.4 > 14. So equal at 0 and 1 and g greater at 2. Option "g greater at x=1" is false (equal); "f greater at 2" false; "g less for every x>0" false.

questions.skill: Compare two functions
questions.stem: How much greater is the average rate of change of $g(x) = 2^x$ than that of $f(x) = 6x + 4$ from $x = 2$ to $x = 6$?
questions.solution: For $g$: $(64 - 4) \div 4 = 15$. For $f$, a linear function, the rate is 6 on every interval. The difference is $15 - 6 = 9$.

questions.skill: Compare two functions
questions.stem: Both $f(x) = 100(0.8)^x$ and $g(x) = 100 - 8x$ start at 100 and decrease. Which statement is true?
choices: $f$ loses 20 each step, while $g$ loses 8% of its value each step
$f$ and $g$ both lose 8 each step
$f$ loses 20% of its current value each step, while $g$ loses 8 each step
$f$ loses 0.8 each step, while $g$ loses 8 each step
questions.answer: $f$ loses 20% of its current value each step, while $g$ loses 8 each step
questions.solution: $f$ is exponential decay with factor 0.8, so each step it keeps 80% and loses 20% of its current value. $g$ is linear with rate $-8$, so each step it loses exactly 8.

solve.answer: $f$ loses 20% of its current value each step, while $g$ loses 8 each step
solve.work: f multiplies by 0.8 each step: loses 20% of its current value. g subtracts 8 each step. Other options misdescribe one or both.

questions.skill: Write a linear function from a situation

questions.solution: The joining fee is paid once (25), and 10 dollars is added for each month, so $f(m) = 25 + 10m$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a recursive rule for an arithmetic sequence

questions.solution: The second term is $12 + 7 = 19$. The third term is $19 + 7 = 26$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a recursive rule for an arithmetic sequence

questions.solution: Subtract 3 each time: $a_2 = 17$, $a_3 = 14$, $a_4 = 11$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a recursive rule for an arithmetic sequence

Exponential, because $y$ is multiplied by 2 each time

questions.solution: The elevation starts at 1200 and rises 150 per kilometer: $E(k) = 150k + 1200$.

questions.solution: In 3 hours the height fell by 6 centimeters, so the candle burns down 2 centimeters per hour. Going back 2 hours from the first measurement adds $2 \times 2 = 4$ centimeters: $30 + 4 = 34$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Evaluate a recursive rule for an arithmetic sequence
questions.stem: A sequence has $a_1 = 100$ and $a_n = a_{n-1} - 15$ for $n \ge 2$. Which term is the first one that is less than 20?
questions.solution: The terms are 100, 85, 70, 55, 40, 25, 10. The term 25 is still more than 20, and $a_7 = 10$ is the first one below 20.

questions.skill: Evaluate a recursive rule for an arithmetic sequence
questions.stem: A sequence has $a_1 = 50$ and $a_n = a_{n-1} - 8$ for $n \ge 2$. What is the first negative term of the sequence?
questions.solution: The terms are 50, 42, 34, 26, 18, 10, 2, -6. The first negative term is $a_8 = 50 - 8 \cdot 7 = -6$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a recursive rule for an arithmetic sequence
questions.stem: A sequence has $a_1 = 5$ and $a_n = a_{n-1} + 6$ for $n \ge 2$. One term of the sequence is 71. Which term number is it?
questions.solution: From 5 to 71 the sequence rises $71 - 5 = 66$, which is $66 \div 6 = 11$ steps after the first term. So 71 is term number $11 + 1 = 12$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a recursive rule for an arithmetic sequence
questions.stem: In a sequence with the rule $a_n = a_{n-1} + d$, the first term is 5 and the fourth term is 20. What is $d$?
questions.solution: There are 3 steps from the first term to the fourth term and the total change is $20 - 5 = 15$. So $d = 15 \div 3 = 5$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a recursive rule for a geometric sequence
questions.stem: A sequence starts with 2, and each term is 3 times the term before it. What is the first term that is greater than 1000?
questions.solution: The terms are 2, 6, 18, 54, 162, 486, 1458. The first one greater than 1000 is 1458.

questions.skill: Evaluate a recursive rule for a geometric sequence
questions.stem: Each term of a geometric sequence is the same multiple of the term before it. The second term is 12 and the third term is 36. What is the fifth term?
questions.solution: The multiplier is $36 \div 12 = 3$. The fourth term is $36 \cdot 3 = 108$ and the fifth is $108 \cdot 3 = 324$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a recursive rule for a geometric sequence
questions.stem: A sequence has $a_1 = 192$ and $a_n = \frac{1}{2}a_{n-1}$ for $n \ge 2$. What is $a_7$?
questions.solution: Halving 6 times gives 96, 48, 24, 12, 6, 3. So $a_7 = 3$.

questions.skill: Evaluate a recursive rule for a geometric sequence
questions.stem: In a sequence, each term is the same positive multiple of the term before it. If the first term is 3 and the third term is 48, what is that multiple?
questions.solution: Multiplying twice by the same number $r$ turns 3 into 48, so $r^2 = 48 \div 3 = 16$. Since $r$ is positive, $r = 4$. Check: $3 \to 12 \to 48$.

questions.skill: Write a recursive rule for a sequence
questions.stem: Which recursive rule produces the sequence 5, 8, 14, 26, 50, ...?
questions.solution: Try doubling and then subtracting 2: $2 \cdot 5 - 2 = 8$, $2 \cdot 8 - 2 = 14$, $2 \cdot 14 - 2 = 26$, $2 \cdot 26 - 2 = 50$. The other rules fail on the second or third term.

solve.work: Test 2a-2: 5 -> 8 -> 14 -> 26 -> 50. Matches. 2a gives 10; 2a+2 gives 12; a+3 gives 8 then 11.

questions.skill: Write a recursive rule for a sequence
questions.stem: A pool holds 500 gallons of water on day 0. Each day it loses 4% of the water it held the day before. Which recursive rule gives the amount $V_n$, in gallons, on day $n$?
questions.solution: Losing 4% leaves 96% of the water, so each day's amount is $0.96$ times the day before: $V_n = 0.96V_{n-1}$.

questions.skill: Write a linear function from a situation
questions.stem: Water drains from a tank at a constant rate. After 3 minutes the tank holds 90 liters, and after 5 minutes it holds 70 liters. Which function gives the liters $V$ in the tank after $t$ minutes?
questions.solution: The tank loses $90 - 70 = 20$ liters in 2 minutes, which is 10 liters per minute. Going back 3 minutes from $t = 3$ gives $90 + 30 = 120$ liters at the start. So $V(t) = 120 - 10t$.

questions.skill: Write a linear function from a situation
questions.stem: A tub drains at a constant rate. After 5 minutes it holds 300 gallons, and after 8 minutes it holds 264 gallons. After how many minutes from the start will it be empty?
questions.solution: The tub loses $300 - 264 = 36$ gallons in 3 minutes, which is 12 gallons per minute. At the start it held $300 + 12 \cdot 5 = 360$ gallons. It is empty after $360 \div 12 = 30$ minutes.

questions.skill: Write a linear function from a situation
questions.stem: A printer prints 45 pages per minute. Which function gives the number of pages $P$ printed after $s$ seconds?
questions.solution: There are 60 seconds in a minute, so the printer prints $45 \div 60 = 0.75$ pages each second: $P(s) = 0.75s$.

solve.work: 45 pages per 60 s = 0.75 pages per second. P(s) = 0.75s.

questions.skill: Write and use an exponential function from a situation
questions.stem: A culture starts with 50 cells and doubles every 3 hours. Which function gives the number of cells $N$ after $t$ hours?
choices: $N(t) = 50 \cdot 2^t$
$N(t) = 50 \cdot 3^t$
questions.solution: The culture doubles once for every 3 hours, so the number of doublings is $t \div 3$. That gives $N(t) = 50 \cdot 2^{t/3}$. (Check: at $t = 3$ the value is $100$.)

solve.work: Doubling every 3 hours means t/3 doublings: N(t) = 50*2^(t/3).

questions.skill: Write and use an exponential function from a situation
questions.stem: The function $f(x) = a \cdot b^x$ with $b > 0$ passes through the points $(0, 6)$ and $(2, 54)$. What is $b$?

questions.skill: Write and use an exponential function from a situation
questions.stem: The function $f(x) = a \cdot b^x$ with $b > 0$ passes through the points $(1, 12)$ and $(3, 108)$. What is $a$?
questions.solution: Going from $x = 1$ to $x = 3$ multiplies the value by $108 \div 12 = 9$, which is $b^2$. So $b = 3$. Then $f(1) = 3a = 12$ gives $a = 4$.

questions.skill: Write and use an exponential function from a situation
questions.stem: An account starts with 2000 dollars and earns 3% interest every 6 months. Which function gives the balance $B$, in dollars, after $y$ years?
questions.solution: There are 2 six-month periods in each year, so after $y$ years there are $2y$ periods. Each period multiplies the balance by 1.03: $B(y) = 2000 \cdot 1.03^{2y}$.

solve.work: Two 6-month periods per year, factor 1.03 each: B(y) = 2000*1.03^(2y).

questions.skill: Write a line in slope-intercept form
questions.stem: Which equation is $3x - 4y = 12$ written in slope-intercept form?
questions.solution: Subtract $3x$: $-4y = -3x + 12$. Divide every term by $-4$: $y = \frac{3}{4}x - 3$.

questions.skill: Write a line in slope-intercept form
questions.stem: A line passes through the points $(4, 1)$ and $(10, 4)$. What is its y-intercept?

questions.skill: Write a line in slope-intercept form
questions.stem: A line has slope $-\frac{2}{3}$ and passes through the point $(6, 1)$. What is its y-intercept?
questions.solution: Put the point into $y = mx + b$: $1 = -\frac{2}{3} \cdot 6 + b = -4 + b$. So $b = 5$.

questions.skill: Write a line in slope-intercept form
questions.stem: A line passes through $(0, -1)$ and has the same slope as the line through $(1, 2)$ and $(3, 8)$. Which is its equation?
questions.solution: The slope of the line through $(1, 2)$ and $(3, 8)$ is $\frac{8 - 2}{3 - 1} = 3$. The new line has slope 3 and y-intercept $-1$, so $y = 3x - 1$.

questions.skill: Choose a linear or exponential model
questions.stem: A table gives $y = 5, 20, 80, 320$ for $x = 0, 2, 4, 6$. Which function fits all four pairs?
choices: $y = 5 \cdot 4^x$
$y = 5 \cdot 2^x$
$y = 20 \cdot 2^x$
questions.answer: $y = 5 \cdot 2^x$
questions.solution: At $x = 0$, $y = 5$, so $a = 5$. When $x$ increases by 2, $y$ is multiplied by 4, so $b^2 = 4$ and $b = 2$. Check: $5 \cdot 2^2 = 20$, $5 \cdot 2^4 = 80$, $5 \cdot 2^6 = 320$.

solve.answer: $y = 5 \cdot 2^x$
solve.work: x up by 2 multiplies y by 4, so b^2 = 4, b = 2, a = 5. y = 5*2^x: 5, 20, 80, 320. 7.5x+5 gives 35 at x=4; 5*4^x gives 80 at x=2; 20*2^x gives 20 at x=0.

questions.skill: Choose a linear or exponential model
questions.stem: Job A pays 100 dollars on day 1 and 20 dollars more each day than the day before. Job B pays 5 dollars on day 1 and doubles its pay each day. On which day does Job B first pay more than Job A?
questions.solution: Job A pays $100 + 20(n - 1)$ and Job B pays $5 \cdot 2^{n-1}$ on day $n$. Day 6: A pays 200 and B pays 160. Day 7: A pays 220 and B pays 320. So day 7.

questions.skill: Choose a linear or exponential model
questions.stem: What is the least positive whole number $x$ for which $2^x$ is greater than $10x$?

questions.skill: Choose a linear or exponential model
questions.stem: Plan A starts with 100 dollars and adds 20 dollars each month. Plan B starts with 100 dollars and grows by 20% each month. How many more dollars does Plan B have than Plan A after 3 months?
questions.solution: Plan A has $100 + 20 \cdot 3 = 160$ dollars. Plan B has $100 \cdot 1.2^3 = 172.8$ dollars. The difference is $172.8 - 160 = 12.8$.

questions.skill: Interpret the parts of a linear or exponential function
questions.stem: A population grows by 20% each year. By what percent has it grown in total after 2 years?
questions.solution: After 2 years the population is multiplied by $1.2^2 = 1.44$. That is a total increase of 44%, not 40%.

questions.skill: Interpret the parts of a linear or exponential function
questions.stem: The function $f(x) = a \cdot b^x$ has $f(0) = 8$ and $f(1) = 12$. Which statement is true about $f$?
choices: $f$ increases by 4 each time $x$ increases by 1
$f$ increases by 50% each time $x$ increases by 1
$f$ increases by 12% each time $x$ increases by 1
$f$ doubles each time $x$ increases by 1
questions.answer: $f$ increases by 50% each time $x$ increases by 1
questions.solution: $f(0) = a = 8$ and $f(1) = 8b = 12$, so $b = 1.5$. A factor of 1.5 is an increase of 50% each step. (Going from 8 to 12 is a rise of 4 only the first time.)

solve.answer: $f$ increases by 50% each time $x$ increases by 1
solve.work: a = 8, b = 12/8 = 1.5: increases by 50% per unit of x.

questions.skill: Write and use an explicit rule for a sequence
questions.stem: The explicit rule for a sequence is $a_n = 5 \cdot 2^{n-1}$. Which term number $n$ has the value 320?

questions.skill: Write and use an explicit rule for a sequence
questions.stem: A sequence has the recursive rule $a_1 = 6$ and $a_n = a_{n-1} + 4$. Which explicit rule gives the same sequence?
questions.solution: The terms are 6, 10, 14, ..., so the rule is $4n + b$. At $n = 1$, $4 + b = 6$ gives $b = 2$: $a_n = 4n + 2$.

questions.skill: Write and use an explicit rule for a sequence
questions.stem: The first level of a parking garage has 140 spaces, and each higher level has 6 fewer spaces than the level below it. How many spaces are on level 15?
questions.solution: Level 15 is 14 levels above level 1, so it has $140 - 6 \cdot 14 = 140 - 84 = 56$ spaces.

questions.skill: Solve a one-step-plus-one linear equation
questions.stem: Solve for $x$: $3x + 5 = 20$.
questions.solution: Subtract 5 from both sides: $3x = 15$. Divide both sides by 3: $x = 5$.

questions.skill: Solve a formula for one quantity
questions.stem: The formula $d = rt$ relates distance $d$, rate $r$ and time $t$. Solve the formula for $t$.
choices: $t = dr$
$t = \frac{r}{d}$
$t = \frac{d}{r}$
$t = d - r$
questions.answer: $t = \frac{d}{r}$
questions.solution: To get $t$ alone, divide both sides of $d = rt$ by $r$: $t = \frac{d}{r}$.

solve.answer: $t = \frac{d}{r}$
solve.work: Divide both sides of d = rt by r: t = d/r.

questions.skill: Justify a step in solving an equation
questions.stem: In solving $4x - 7 = 21$, a student writes the next line as $4x = 28$. Which property justifies this step?
choices: Addition property of equality
Multiplication property of equality
Distributive property
Commutative property of addition
questions.answer: Addition property of equality
questions.solution: The student added 7 to both sides: $4x - 7 + 7 = 21 + 7$. Adding the same number to both sides of an equation keeps it true, which is the addition property of equality.

solve.answer: Addition property of equality
solve.work: From 4x - 7 = 21 to 4x = 28, 7 is added to both sides: addition property of equality.

questions.skill: Justify the steps in solving an equation
questions.stem: In solving $x + 9 = 15$, a student writes $x = 6$ as the next line. What was done to both sides of the equation?
choices: 9 was added to both sides
Both sides were divided by 9
9 was subtracted from both sides
Both sides were multiplied by 9
questions.answer: 9 was subtracted from both sides
questions.solution: Subtracting 9 from both sides leaves $x = 15 - 9 = 6$.

solve.answer: 9 was subtracted from both sides
solve.work: x + 9 = 15 -> x = 6 is obtained by subtracting 9 from both sides (15 - 9 = 6).

questions.skill: Justify the steps in solving an equation
questions.stem: In solving $\frac{x}{4} = 7$, a student writes $x = 28$ as the next line. Which property justifies this step?
choices: Multiplication property of equality
Addition property of equality
Subtraction property of equality
Distributive property
questions.answer: Multiplication property of equality
questions.solution: Multiplying both sides by 4 undoes the division by 4: $x = 7 \cdot 4 = 28$. That is the multiplication property of equality.

solve.answer: Multiplication property of equality
solve.work: x/4 = 7 -> x = 28: both sides multiplied by 4, the multiplication property of equality.

questions.skill: Justify the steps in solving an equation
questions.stem: A student rewrites $3(x + 2) = 15$ as $3x + 6 = 15$. Which property justifies this step?
choices: Addition property of equality
Distributive property
Commutative property of addition
Division property of equality
questions.answer: Distributive property
questions.solution: Multiplying 3 by each term inside the parentheses, $3 \cdot x + 3 \cdot 2$, uses the distributive property.

solve.answer: Distributive property
solve.work: 3(x+2) -> 3x + 6 distributes 3 over the sum: distributive property.

questions.skill: Justify the steps in solving an equation
questions.stem: To solve $x - 7 = 12$, a student adds the same number to both sides. What number is added?
questions.solution: Adding 7 to both sides undoes the subtraction: $x - 7 + 7 = 12 + 7$, so $x = 19$. The number added is 7.

solve.work: x - 7 = 12; add 7 to both sides to isolate x: x = 19. Number added is 7.

questions.skill: Solve a linear equation in one variable
questions.stem: Solve for $x$: $\frac{x}{5} - 3 = 4$.
questions.solution: Add 3: $\frac{x}{5} = 7$. Multiply both sides by 5: $x = 35$.

questions.skill: Solve a linear equation in one variable
questions.stem: Solve for $x$: $2x + 9 = 1$.
questions.solution: Subtract 9: $2x = -8$. Divide by 2: $x = -4$.

questions.skill: Solve a linear equation in one variable
questions.stem: Which value of $x$ makes $4x - 5 = 11$ true?
questions.solution: Add 5 to both sides: $4x = 16$. Divide by 4: $x = 4$. Check: $4 \cdot 4 - 5 = 11$.

questions.skill: Solve a linear equation in one variable
questions.stem: Which equation has the solution $x = -2$?
questions.solution: Put $x = -2$ into $3x + 4$: $3(-2) + 4 = -2$, which matches. The other three equations have the solution $x = 2$.

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality in one variable
questions.stem: Solve the inequality $x + 5 > 12$.
questions.solution: Subtract 5 from both sides: $x > 7$.

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality in one variable
questions.stem: Solve the inequality $4x \le 20$.
choices: $x \le 5$
$x \ge 5$
questions.answer: $x \le 5$
questions.solution: Divide both sides by 4 (a positive number, so the sign stays): $x \le 5$.

solve.answer: $x \le 5$

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality in one variable
questions.stem: What is the least whole number that is a solution of $3x > 20$?
questions.solution: $x > \frac{20}{3}$, which is about 6.67. The least whole number greater than 6.67 is 7. (Check: $3 \cdot 7 = 21 > 20$ but $3 \cdot 6 = 18$ is not.)

questions.skill: Solve a formula for a quantity
questions.stem: Solve the formula $P = 4s$ for $s$.
choices: $s = \frac{P}{4}$
$s = \frac{4}{P}$
questions.answer: $s = \frac{P}{4}$
questions.solution: Divide both sides by 4: $s = \frac{P}{4}$.

solve.answer: $s = \frac{P}{4}$

questions.skill: Solve a formula for a quantity
questions.stem: The perimeter of a rectangle is $P = 2l + 2w$. A rectangle has perimeter 30 and width 5. What is its length?
questions.solution: Put in the values: $30 = 2l + 10$. Subtract 10: $20 = 2l$. So $l = 10$.

questions.skill: Solve a formula for a quantity
questions.stem: Solve the formula $A = \frac{1}{2}bh$ for $b$.
choices: $b = \frac{2A}{h}$
$b = \frac{A}{2h}$
$b = 2Ah$
$b = \frac{h}{2A}$
questions.answer: $b = \frac{2A}{h}$
questions.solution: Multiply both sides by 2: $2A = bh$. Divide both sides by $h$: $b = \frac{2A}{h}$.

solve.answer: $b = \frac{2A}{h}$

questions.skill: Solve a formula for a quantity
questions.stem: The area of a triangle is $A = \frac{1}{2}bh$. A triangle has area 36 and base 9. What is its height?
questions.solution: Put in the values: $36 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 9 \cdot h$, so $72 = 9h$ and $h = 8$.

questions.skill: Solve a formula for a quantity
questions.stem: The mean of two test scores is $A = \frac{x + y}{2}$. A student's mean is 84 and the first score $x$ is 79. What is the second score $y$?
questions.solution: Multiply both sides by 2: $x + y = 168$. Then $y = 168 - 79 = 89$.

questions.skill: Write an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: A video starts with 5 views, and the number of views triples every hour. Which equation can be solved to find the number of hours $t$ until there are 405 views?
questions.solution: The count starts at 5 and is multiplied by 3 each hour, so after $t$ hours it is $5 \cdot 3^t$. Set this equal to 405.

solve.work: Start 5, factor 3 per hour: views = 5 * 3^t. Set equal to 405: 5 * 3^t = 405 (t = 4).

questions.skill: Write an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: A message is passed on so that the number of people who have it doubles every round: after $t$ rounds, $2^t$ people have it. After how many rounds will 64 people have it?

questions.skill: Write an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: A 400-milligram dose of medicine halves every hour. Which equation can be solved to find the number of hours $t$ until 25 milligrams remain?
questions.solution: The amount starts at 400 and is multiplied by $\frac{1}{2}$ each hour, so after $t$ hours it is $400 \cdot (\frac{1}{2})^t$.

questions.skill: Solve an exponential equation with a table or by reasoning
questions.stem: Which value of $x$ makes $3^x = 81$ true?

questions.skill: Solve an exponential equation with a table or by reasoning
questions.stem: A table shows $f(x) = 3 \cdot 2^x$: for $x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5$ the values of $f(x)$ are 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, 96. For which value of $x$ is $f(x) = 48$?
questions.solution: Reading the table, 48 is the value when $x = 4$.

questions.skill: Solve an exponential equation with a table or by reasoning
questions.stem: Solve for $x$: $5 \cdot 2^x = 40$.
questions.solution: Divide by 5: $2^x = 8$. Since $2^3 = 8$, $x = 3$.

questions.skill: Interpret the solution of an equation or inequality
questions.stem: A taxi ride costs 3 dollars plus 2 dollars per mile. Maria has 15 dollars. The inequality $3 + 2m \le 15$ gives the number of miles $m$ she can ride. What is the greatest number of miles she can ride?
questions.solution: Subtract 3: $2m \le 12$. Divide by 2: $m \le 6$. The greatest is 6 miles.

questions.skill: Interpret the solution of an equation or inequality
questions.stem: The solution of an inequality in $x$, the number of whole pencils that can be bought, is $x \le 12.5$. Which statement is the best interpretation?
choices: At most 13 pencils can be bought
Exactly 12.5 pencils can be bought
At least 12 pencils must be bought
At most 12 pencils can be bought
questions.answer: At most 12 pencils can be bought
questions.solution: Whole pencils cannot be split, so $x$ can be at most the greatest whole number not above 12.5, which is 12.

solve.answer: At most 12 pencils can be bought
solve.work: x is a whole number of pencils and x <= 12.5, so x can be at most 12. 13 exceeds 12.5.

questions.skill: Interpret the solution of an equation or inequality
questions.stem: A student saves 5 dollars each week and wants 35 dollars. The equation $5w = 35$ gives the number of weeks $w$. After how many weeks will she have exactly 35 dollars?
questions.solution: Divide both sides by 5: $w = 7$. She will have 35 dollars after 7 weeks.

solve.issues: Very easy for Math 1 (a one-step grade-6 equation), though it does ask for interpreting a solution in context.

questions.skill: Interpret the solution of an equation or inequality
questions.stem: The equation $7.5h + 12 = 57$ models total pay in dollars for $h$ hours of work, including a 12 dollar bonus. Its solution is $h = 6$. What does the solution tell us?
choices: Working 57 hours earns a total of 6 dollars
The hourly pay is 6 dollars
Working 6 hours earns a total of 57 dollars
The bonus is 6 dollars
questions.answer: Working 6 hours earns a total of 57 dollars
questions.solution: The equation asks for the hours that give a total of 57 dollars. The solution $h = 6$ means 6 hours of work gives 57 dollars.

solve.answer: Working 6 hours earns a total of 57 dollars
solve.work: h = 6 hours gives total pay 7.5(6) + 12 = 57 dollars. So working 6 hours earns 57 dollars in total.

questions.skill: Write and solve a linear equation or inequality from a situation
questions.stem: Sam has 15 stickers and buys packs of 6 stickers. He wants 51 stickers in all. Which equation can be solved to find the number of packs $p$?
questions.solution: He starts with 15 and adds 6 stickers for each pack: $15 + 6p = 51$.

questions.skill: Write and solve a linear equation or inequality from a situation
questions.stem: A tutor charges 5 dollars to sign up and then 20 dollars per hour. A family paid 65 dollars in all. For how many hours was the tutor hired?
questions.solution: The equation is $5 + 20h = 65$. Subtract 5: $20h = 60$. So $h = 3$ hours.

questions.skill: Write and solve a linear equation or inequality from a situation
questions.stem: Which inequality states "3 less than twice a number is at most 9"?
questions.solution: "Twice a number" is $2n$, "3 less than" that is $2n - 3$, and "at most 9" means $\le 9$.

solve.work: Twice a number: 2n; 3 less than that: 2n - 3; at most 9: <= 9. So 2n - 3 <= 9.

questions.skill: Write and solve a linear equation or inequality from a situation
questions.stem: Adult tickets cost 8 dollars and child tickets cost 5 dollars. A theater sold 12 adult tickets and some child tickets for a total of 126 dollars. How many child tickets were sold?
questions.solution: Adult tickets bring in $12 \cdot 8 = 96$ dollars. The child tickets bring in $126 - 96 = 30$ dollars, so $30 \div 5 = 6$ child tickets.

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality, reversing the sign
questions.stem: Solve the inequality $-2x + 3 < 11$.
questions.solution: Subtract 3 from both sides: $-2x < 8$. Dividing both sides by $-2$ reverses the inequality sign: $x > -4$.

solve.work: -2x + 3 < 11 -> -2x < 8 -> divide by -2 and flip: x > -4. Check x = 0: 3 < 11 true.

questions.skill: Solve a formula for a quantity, given a value
questions.stem: The formula $F = \frac{9}{5}C + 32$ changes a temperature in degrees Celsius $C$ to degrees Fahrenheit $F$. A temperature is 68 degrees Fahrenheit. What is it in degrees Celsius?
questions.solution: Put $F = 68$ in the formula: $68 = \frac{9}{5}C + 32$. Subtract 32: $36 = \frac{9}{5}C$. Multiply by $\frac{5}{9}$: $C = 36 \times \frac{5}{9} = 20$.

questions.skill: Solve a simple exponential equation in context
questions.stem: A culture starts with 3 bacteria and triples every hour, so after $t$ hours it has $3 \cdot 3^t$ bacteria. After how many hours are there 243 bacteria?
questions.solution: Solve $3 \cdot 3^t = 243$. Divide by 3: $3^t = 81$. Since $3^4 = 81$, $t = 4$ hours. (Check: 3, 9, 27, 81, 243.)

questions.skill: Justify the steps in solving an equation
questions.stem: A student rewrites $5x - 2x + 4 = 19$ as $3x + 4 = 19$. What justifies this step?
choices: Division property of equality
Addition property of equality
Multiplication property of equality
Combining like terms
questions.answer: Combining like terms
questions.solution: $5x$ and $-2x$ are like terms, and combining them gives $3x$. Nothing is done to both sides.

solve.answer: Combining like terms
solve.work: 5x - 2x = 3x on the left side only: combining like terms.

questions.skill: Justify the steps in solving an equation
questions.stem: In solving $6x + 5 = 2x + 21$, a student subtracts $2x$ from both sides and then subtracts 5 from both sides, giving $4x = c$. What is $c$?
questions.solution: After subtracting $2x$: $4x + 5 = 21$. After subtracting 5: $4x = 16$. So $c = 16$.

questions.skill: Justify the steps in solving an equation
questions.stem: A student solves $-3x \ge 12$ and writes $x \le -4$. Which statement justifies reversing the inequality sign?
choices: Dividing both sides of an inequality by a positive number reverses the inequality sign
Subtracting a number from both sides of an inequality reverses the inequality sign
The sign always reverses when the answer is negative
Dividing both sides of an inequality by a negative number reverses the inequality sign
questions.answer: Dividing both sides of an inequality by a negative number reverses the inequality sign
questions.solution: The student divided both sides by $-3$. Dividing (or multiplying) by a negative number flips the direction of the inequality: $x \le -4$.

solve.answer: Dividing both sides of an inequality by a negative number reverses the inequality sign
solve.work: -3x >= 12, divide by -3: x <= -4. The reversal is because both sides were divided by a negative number.

questions.skill: Justify the steps in solving an equation
questions.stem: A student solves $2(x - 3) = 10$ and writes $2x - 3 = 10$ as the first line. Which property was applied incorrectly?
choices: Division property of equality
Addition property of equality
Distributive property
Combining like terms
questions.answer: Distributive property
questions.solution: The 2 must multiply both terms in the parentheses: $2(x - 3) = 2x - 6$. The student multiplied only the first term.

solve.answer: Distributive property
solve.work: 2(x - 3) should be 2x - 6; writing 2x - 3 means the 2 was not distributed to the -3: distributive property misapplied.

questions.skill: Solve a linear equation in one variable
questions.stem: Solve for $x$: $5(x - 2) = 3x + 6$.
questions.solution: Distribute: $5x - 10 = 3x + 6$. Subtract $3x$: $2x - 10 = 6$. Add 10: $2x = 16$. So $x = 8$.

questions.skill: Solve a linear equation in one variable
questions.stem: Solve for $x$: $7 - 3x = 2x - 13$.
questions.solution: Add $3x$ to both sides: $7 = 5x - 13$. Add 13: $20 = 5x$. So $x = 4$.

questions.skill: Solve a linear equation in one variable
questions.stem: Solve for $x$: $\frac{2}{3}x + 4 = 10$.
questions.solution: Subtract 4: $\frac{2}{3}x = 6$. Multiply by $\frac{3}{2}$: $x = 9$.

questions.skill: Solve a linear equation in one variable
questions.stem: Solve for $x$: $6x + 1 = 2x + 8$.
questions.solution: Subtract $2x$: $4x + 1 = 8$. Subtract 1: $4x = 7$. So $x = \frac{7}{4}$.

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality in one variable
questions.stem: Solve the inequality $-3x + 4 \le 19$.
choices: $x \ge 5$
$x \le 5$
questions.solution: Subtract 4: $-3x \le 15$. Divide by $-3$ and reverse the sign: $x \ge -5$.

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality in one variable
questions.stem: Solve the inequality $5 - 2(x + 1) > 9$.
questions.solution: Distribute: $5 - 2x - 2 > 9$, so $3 - 2x > 9$. Subtract 3: $-2x > 6$. Divide by $-2$ and reverse the sign: $x < -3$.

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality in one variable
questions.stem: What is the greatest whole number that satisfies $4x - 7 < 21$?
questions.solution: Add 7: $4x < 28$. Divide by 4: $x < 7$. The greatest whole number less than 7 is 6.

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality in one variable
questions.stem: How many positive whole numbers satisfy $2x + 3 \le 17$?
questions.solution: Subtract 3: $2x \le 14$, so $x \le 7$. The positive whole numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 all work, which is 7 numbers.

solve.work: 2x + 3 <= 17 -> 2x <= 14 -> x <= 7. Positive whole numbers 1 through 7: 7 of them.

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality in one variable
questions.stem: Which number is a solution of $-4x + 2 > 10$?
questions.solution: Subtract 2: $-4x > 8$. Dividing by $-4$ reverses the sign: $x < -2$. Of the choices, only $-3$ is less than $-2$. (Check: $-4(-3) + 2 = 14 > 10$.)

questions.skill: Solve a formula for a quantity
questions.stem: Solve the formula $y = mx + b$ for $x$.
choices: $x = \frac{y}{m} + b$
$x = y - b - m$
$x = \frac{y + b}{m}$
$x = \frac{y - b}{m}$
questions.answer: $x = \frac{y - b}{m}$
questions.solution: Subtract $b$ from both sides: $y - b = mx$. Divide both sides by $m$: $x = \frac{y - b}{m}$.

solve.answer: $x = \frac{y - b}{m}$
solve.work: y = mx + b -> y - b = mx -> x = (y - b)/m.

questions.skill: Solve a formula for a quantity
questions.stem: The simple interest formula is $I = Prt$. A loan of 600 dollars earned 90 dollars in interest over 3 years. What is the yearly rate $r$, written as a decimal?
questions.solution: Solve for $r$: $r = \frac{I}{Pt} = \frac{90}{600 \cdot 3} = \frac{90}{1800} = 0.05$.

questions.skill: Solve a formula for a quantity
questions.stem: Solve the equation $3x + 2y = 12$ for $y$.
questions.solution: Subtract $3x$: $2y = 12 - 3x$. Divide every term by 2: $y = \frac{12 - 3x}{2}$.

solve.work: 3x + 2y = 12 -> 2y = 12 - 3x -> y = (12 - 3x)/2. (6 - 3x is wrong: only 12 was halved.)

questions.skill: Write an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: A town of 12000 people grows 3% each year. Which equation can be solved to find the number of years $t$ until the population is 15000?
questions.solution: A 3% increase multiplies the population by 1.03 each year, so after $t$ years it is $12000 \cdot 1.03^t$.

questions.skill: Write an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: A truck worth 18000 dollars loses 12% of its value each year. Which equation can be solved to find the number of years $t$ until it is worth 9000 dollars?
questions.solution: Losing 12% leaves 88% of the value each year, so the value after $t$ years is $18000 \cdot 0.88^t$.

questions.skill: Solve an exponential equation with a table or by reasoning
questions.stem: The value of an investment is $V = 1000 \cdot 1.1^t$ dollars after $t$ years. A table gives $V$ as 1100, 1210, 1331 and 1464.1 for $t = 1, 2, 3, 4$. In which year $t$ does the value first exceed 1300 dollars?
questions.solution: The values for $t = 1$ and $t = 2$ (1100 and 1210) are below 1300. For $t = 3$, the value is 1331, which is above 1300. So $t = 3$.

solve.work: Table: t=1 1100, t=2 1210 (below 1300), t=3 1331 (above 1300). First exceeds 1300 at t = 3.

questions.skill: Solve an exponential equation with a table or by reasoning
questions.stem: A table of values of $1.5^t$ for $t = 2, 3, 4, 5$ is 2.25, 3.375, 5.0625, 7.59375. Between which two whole numbers is the solution of $1.5^t = 5$?
choices: Between 2 and 3
Between 4 and 5
Between 5 and 6
Between 3 and 4
questions.answer: Between 3 and 4
questions.solution: $1.5^3 = 3.375$ is below 5 and $1.5^4 = 5.0625$ is above 5, so the solution lies between $t = 3$ and $t = 4$.

solve.answer: Between 3 and 4
solve.work: 1.5^3 = 3.375 < 5 and 1.5^4 = 5.0625 > 5, so the solution of 1.5^t = 5 lies between 3 and 4 (about 3.97).

questions.skill: Interpret the solution of an equation or inequality
questions.stem: A student scored 88, 92 and 85 on three tests. What is the lowest score on a fourth test that gives an average of at least 90?
questions.solution: The average of four tests is at least 90 when the total is at least $90 \cdot 4 = 360$. The first three add to $88 + 92 + 85 = 265$, so the fourth score must be at least $360 - 265 = 95$.

questions.skill: Interpret the solution of an equation or inequality
questions.stem: A tank holds $50 - 4t$ liters of water after $t$ minutes. Solving $50 - 4t = 18$ gives $t = 8$. What does this tell us?
choices: The tank holds 18 liters after 8 minutes
The tank holds 8 liters after 18 minutes
The tank is empty after 8 minutes
The tank loses 18 liters in 8 minutes
questions.answer: The tank holds 18 liters after 8 minutes
questions.solution: The equation asks when the amount $50 - 4t$ equals 18 liters. The solution $t = 8$ means that happens after 8 minutes.

solve.answer: The tank holds 18 liters after 8 minutes
solve.work: 50 - 4t = 18 at t = 8 means after 8 minutes the tank holds 18 liters. (It has lost 32 liters, not 18; empty would be 12.5 minutes.)

questions.skill: Interpret the solution of an equation or inequality
questions.stem: A kayak rental costs 15 dollars plus 9 dollars per hour. Mia has 62 dollars. What is the greatest number of whole hours she can rent the kayak?
questions.solution: The inequality is $15 + 9h \le 62$. Subtract 15: $9h \le 47$, so $h \le 5.2$. She can rent for 5 whole hours (cost 60 dollars).

solve.work: 15 + 9h <= 62 -> 9h <= 47 -> h <= 5.22. Greatest whole number of hours 5 (15 + 45 = 60; 6 hours would be 69).

questions.skill: Write and solve a linear equation or inequality from a situation
questions.stem: The length of a rectangle is 3 more than twice its width. The perimeter is 54 centimeters. What is the width, in centimeters?
questions.solution: With width $w$, the length is $2w + 3$. The perimeter gives $2(w + 2w + 3) = 54$, so $3w + 3 = 27$ and $w = 8$.

questions.skill: Write and solve a linear equation or inequality from a situation
questions.stem: Mia has 40 dollars and saves 7 dollars each week. Ana has 100 dollars and spends 8 dollars each week. Which equation can be solved to find the number of weeks $w$ until they have the same amount?
questions.solution: Mia has $40 + 7w$ after $w$ weeks and Ana has $100 - 8w$. Set them equal.

questions.skill: Write and solve a linear equation or inequality from a situation
questions.stem: Three consecutive whole numbers add up to 117. What is the largest of the three?
questions.solution: With the smallest number $n$, the sum is $n + (n + 1) + (n + 2) = 3n + 3 = 117$. So $n = 38$ and the largest is $40$.

questions.skill: Write and solve a linear equation or inequality from a situation
questions.stem: A club has 200 dollars to spend. Each pizza costs 12 dollars and delivery is a flat fee of 20 dollars. Which inequality can be solved to find the number of pizzas $p$ the club can afford?
questions.solution: The total cost is $12p + 20$, and it must be at most 200: $12p + 20 \le 200$.

solve.work: Cost = 12 per pizza times p plus flat 20 delivery: 12p + 20, which must be at most 200: 12p + 20 <= 200.

questions.skill: Write an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: A population starts at 200 and doubles every hour. Which equation can be solved to find the number of hours $t$ until the population is 3200?
questions.solution: The starting amount is 200 and it is multiplied by 2 for each hour, so after $t$ hours the population is $200(2)^t$. Setting that equal to 3200 gives $200(2)^t = 3200$.

solve.work: Population after t hours = 200(2)^t; set equal to 3200: 200(2)^t = 3200 (t = 4).

questions.skill: Interpret the solution of an inequality in context
questions.stem: You have 52 dollars. Park entry costs 14 dollars, and each ride ticket costs 3 dollars. You can only buy whole tickets. What is the greatest number of ride tickets you can buy?
questions.solution: The inequality is $14 + 3r \le 52$, so $3r \le 38$ and $r \le 12.67\ldots$. You can only buy whole tickets, so the greatest number is 12 (12 tickets cost 36 dollars, for a total of 50 dollars).

questions.skill: Solve a formula for time, given values
questions.stem: The formula $A = P + Prt$ gives the total $A$ in dollars after $t$ years when $P$ dollars earn simple interest at yearly rate $r$ (written as a decimal). When $P = 200$ and $r = 0.05$, the total is $A = 230$. How many years is that?
questions.solution: Put in the values: $230 = 200 + 200(0.05)t = 200 + 10t$. Subtract 200: $30 = 10t$. So $t = 3$ years.

questions.skill: Justify the steps in solving an equation
questions.stem: A solution is shown. Line 1: $3(x + 4) = 2x + 20$. Line 2: $3x + 12 = 2x + 20$. Line 3: $x + 12 = 20$. Line 4: $x = 8$. What was done to get from Line 2 to Line 3?
choices: 12 was subtracted from both sides
$2x$ was subtracted from both sides
Both sides were divided by 3
$3x$ was subtracted from both sides
questions.answer: $2x$ was subtracted from both sides
questions.solution: $3x - 2x = x$ on the left and $2x - 2x = 0$ on the right, so $2x$ was subtracted from both sides.

solve.answer: $2x$ was subtracted from both sides
solve.work: Line 2: 3x + 12 = 2x + 20. Subtract 2x from both sides: x + 12 = 20 (Line 3).

questions.skill: Justify the steps in solving an equation
questions.stem: A student solves $2(3x - 4) = 4x + 6$. Line 1: $2(3x - 4) = 4x + 6$. Line 2: $6x - 8 = 4x + 6$. Line 3: $2x - 8 = 6$. Line 4: $2x = -2$. Line 5: $x = -1$. Which line number contains the first mistake?
questions.solution: Lines 1 to 3 are correct. From $2x - 8 = 6$, adding 8 to both sides gives $2x = 14$, not $2x = -2$. So the first mistake is in Line 4.

solve.work: Line 2: 6x - 8 = 4x + 6 correct. Line 3: subtract 4x: 2x - 8 = 6 correct. Line 4: add 8: 2x = 14, but student wrote 2x = -2 (subtracted 8). First mistake is Line 4. (Correct x = 7.)

questions.skill: Justify the steps in solving an equation
questions.stem: Which operation turns $\frac{x}{3} + 2 = 5$ into $x + 6 = 15$?
choices: Multiplying every term on both sides by 3
Adding 3 to both sides
Multiplying only the left side by 3
Dividing both sides by 3
questions.answer: Multiplying every term on both sides by 3
questions.solution: Multiplying each term by 3 gives $x + 6 = 15$. The multiplication property of equality allows multiplying both sides, and the distributive property applies it to each term.

solve.answer: Multiplying every term on both sides by 3
solve.work: Multiply each term by 3: 3(x/3) + 3(2) = 3(5) -> x + 6 = 15. Multiplying only the left side would give x + 6 = 5.

questions.skill: Solve a linear equation in one variable
questions.stem: Solve for $x$: $\frac{x + 3}{2} = \frac{2x - 1}{3}$.
questions.solution: Multiply both sides by 6: $3(x + 3) = 2(2x - 1)$. Distribute: $3x + 9 = 4x - 2$. Subtract $3x$ and add 2: $11 = x$.

questions.skill: Solve a linear equation in one variable

questions.stem: How many solutions does the equation $3(x + 2) = 3x + 6$ have?
choices: No solution
Infinitely many
Exactly one solution
Exactly two solutions
questions.answer: Infinitely many
questions.solution: Distributing gives $3x + 6 = 3x + 6$, which is true for every value of $x$. So there are infinitely many solutions.

solve.answer: Infinitely many
solve.work: 3(x + 2) = 3x + 6 is 3x + 6 = 3x + 6, an identity: true for every x, infinitely many solutions.

questions.solution: Distribute: $8x - 12 - 5x = 2x + 14 + 1$, so $3x - 12 = 2x + 15$. Subtract $2x$ and add 12: $x = 27$.

$x \ge 9$

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality in one variable
questions.stem: What is the greatest whole number that satisfies $7 - 3x > 2x - 18$?
questions.solution: Add $3x$ and 18: $25 > 5x$, so $x < 5$. The greatest whole number less than 5 is 4. (Check: for $x = 4$, $-5 > -10$ is true; for $x = 5$, $-8 > -8$ is false.)

solve.work: 7 - 3x > 2x - 18 -> 25 > 5x -> x < 5. Greatest whole number 4 (check 4: -5 > -10 true; 5: -8 > -8 false).

questions.skill: Solve a linear inequality in one variable
questions.stem: Solve the inequality $-2(3 - x) \ge 4x - 10$.

$x \le \frac{2}{3}$
$x \le 2$
$x \ge \frac{2}{3}$
questions.answer: $x \le 2$
questions.solution: Distribute: $-6 + 2x \ge 4x - 10$. Subtract $4x$ and add 6: $-2x \ge -4$. Divide by $-2$ and reverse the sign: $x \le 2$.

solve.answer: $x \le 2$

questions.skill: Solve a formula for a quantity
questions.stem: The area of a trapezoid is $A = \frac{1}{2}h(b_1 + b_2)$. A trapezoid has area 60, height 8 and one base $b_1 = 5$. What is the other base $b_2$?
questions.solution: Put in the values: $60 = 4(5 + b_2)$. Divide by 4: $15 = 5 + b_2$. So $b_2 = 10$.

questions.skill: Solve a formula for a quantity
questions.stem: Solve the formula $A = \frac{1}{2}h(b_1 + b_2)$ for $b_2$.
questions.solution: Multiply by 2: $2A = h(b_1 + b_2)$. Divide by $h$: $\frac{2A}{h} = b_1 + b_2$. Subtract $b_1$: $b_2 = \frac{2A}{h} - b_1$.

questions.skill: Solve a formula for a quantity
questions.stem: The slope of a line is $m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$. A line has slope 3 and passes through the point $(2, 4)$. A second point on the line has $x_2 = 7$. What is $y_2$?
questions.solution: Put in the values: $3 = \frac{y_2 - 4}{7 - 2}$. Multiply both sides by 5: $15 = y_2 - 4$. So $y_2 = 19$.

questions.skill: Solve a formula for a quantity
questions.stem: Solve the equation $\frac{x}{a} + \frac{y}{b} = 1$ for $y$.
choices: $y = b + \frac{bx}{a}$
$y = \frac{b - x}{a}$
$y = 1 - \frac{x}{a} - b$
$y = b - \frac{bx}{a}$
questions.answer: $y = b - \frac{bx}{a}$
questions.solution: Subtract $\frac{x}{a}$: $\frac{y}{b} = 1 - \frac{x}{a}$. Multiply both sides by $b$: $y = b - \frac{bx}{a}$.

solve.answer: $y = b - \frac{bx}{a}$
solve.work: x/a + y/b = 1 -> y/b = 1 - x/a -> y = b(1 - x/a) = b - bx/a.

questions.stem: A sample of 80 grams halves every 3 years. Which equation can be solved to find the number of years $t$ until 10 grams remain?
questions.solution: In $t$ years there are $t \div 3$ halvings, so the mass is $80 \cdot (\frac{1}{2})^{t/3}$.

solve.work: Halves every 3 years: number of halvings after t years is t/3. 80 * (1/2)^(t/3) = 10 (t = 9).

questions.skill: Write an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: A fungus colony covers 3 square centimeters and doubles in area every 5 days. Which equation can be solved to find the number of days $d$ until it covers 96 square centimeters?
questions.solution: In $d$ days there are $d \div 5$ doublings, so the area is $3 \cdot 2^{d/5}$.

solve.work: Doubles every 5 days: doublings after d days = d/5. 3 * 2^(d/5) = 96 (d = 25).

questions.skill: Write an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: Mold on a slice of bread covers 4 square millimeters and doubles in area every 3 days, so its area after $d$ days is $4 \cdot 2^{d/3}$. After how many days will it cover 256 square millimeters?

questions.skill: Write an exponential equation from a situation
questions.stem: Which situation matches the equation $500 \cdot 0.9^t = 200$?
choices: A value of 500 dollars gains 10% each year; $t$ is the number of years until it is worth 200 dollars
A value of 500 dollars loses 90% each year; $t$ is the number of years until it is worth 200 dollars
A value of 500 dollars loses 10% each year; $t$ is the number of years until it is worth 200 dollars
A value of 200 dollars loses 10% each year; $t$ is the number of years until it is worth 500 dollars
questions.answer: A value of 500 dollars loses 10% each year; $t$ is the number of years until it is worth 200 dollars
questions.solution: The start is 500 and the factor 0.9 keeps 90% of the value, which is a loss of 10% each year. The result 200 is the target.

solve.answer: A value of 500 dollars loses 10% each year; $t$ is the number of years until it is worth 200 dollars
solve.work: 500 is the start, 0.9 = 1 - 0.10 means it loses 10% per period, 200 is the target. Matches: 500 dollars loses 10% each year until worth 200.

questions.skill: Solve an exponential equation with a table or by reasoning
questions.stem: A culture has $B(t) = 50 \cdot 2^t$ bacteria after $t$ hours. What is the least whole number of hours after which there are more than 10000 bacteria?
questions.solution: Divide by 50: we need $2^t > 200$. $2^7 = 128$ is too small and $2^8 = 256$ is enough. So $t = 8$ (12800 bacteria; at 7 hours there are only 6400).

questions.skill: Solve an exponential equation with a table or by reasoning
questions.stem: A car's value is $V(t) = 20000 \cdot 0.8^t$ dollars after $t$ years. What is the least whole number of years after which it is worth less than 10000 dollars?
questions.solution: We need $0.8^t < 0.5$. $0.8^3 = 0.512$ (value 10240) is still too high, and $0.8^4 = 0.4096$ (value 8192) is below 10000. So $t = 4$.
