questions.stem: A baker finds that a line of best fit for the number of cakes ordered, $x$, and the cups of sugar needed, $y$, is $y = 3x + 2$. About how many cups of sugar are needed for 7 cakes?
questions.solution: Substitute $x = 7$: $y = 3 \times 7 + 2 = 21 + 2 = 23$ cups of sugar.

questions.skill: Predicting from a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit passes through $(0, 10)$ and $(1, 14)$. Use the line to predict the value of $y$ when $x = 5$.
questions.solution: Going from $x = 0$ to $x = 1$, $y$ rises by $14 - 10 = 4$. So $y$ rises by 4 for each step of 1 in $x$, and at $x = 5$ it is $10 + 4 \times 5 = 30$.

questions.skill: Predicting from a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit for the number of tickets bought, $x$, and the total cost in dollars, $y$, is $y = 5x + 20$. What cost does the line predict for 3 tickets?
questions.solution: Substitute $x = 3$: $y = 5 \times 3 + 20 = 15 + 20 = 35$.

questions.skill: Slope of a line of best fit
questions.stem: Along a line of best fit, $y$ goes up by 6 every time $x$ goes up by 2. What is the slope of the line?
questions.solution: Slope is the change in $y$ divided by the change in $x$: $6 \div 2 = 3$.

questions.skill: Intercept of a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit for a candle's burning time, $x$ (in hours), and its height, $y$ (in centimeters), is $y = -4x + 30$. How tall does the line predict the candle was before it was lit, when $x = 0$?
questions.solution: At $x = 0$ the term $-4x$ is 0, so $y = 30$ centimeters. This is the $y$-intercept.

questions.skill: Outliers, clusters and gaps
questions.stem: The points on a scatter plot are $(1, 2)$, $(2, 4)$, $(3, 6)$, $(4, 8)$ and $(5, 30)$. Which $y$-value is far from the pattern of the others?
questions.solution: The first four points have $y$ equal to 2 times $x$: 2, 4, 6, 8. At $x = 5$ that pattern gives 10, but the point has $y = 30$, which is far from the pattern. This point is an outlier.

solve.work: Pattern y = 2x gives 10 at x = 5; the point has 30, far off.

questions.skill: Outliers, clusters and gaps
questions.stem: What is a point called when it lies far away from the pattern of all the other points in a scatter plot?
choices: A cluster
A gap
An outlier
A trend
questions.answer: An outlier
questions.solution: A point that stands apart from the overall pattern is an outlier. A cluster is a group of points close together, and a gap is an empty region.

solve.answer: An outlier
solve.work: A point far from the pattern of the others is an outlier.

questions.skill: Interpolation and extrapolation
questions.stem: A line of best fit is made from data with $x$-values from 10 to 30. Using the line to predict $y$ for $x = 20$ is called which of these?
choices: Extrapolation
Correlation
Residual
Interpolation
questions.answer: Interpolation
questions.solution: Predicting inside the range of the data is interpolation. Predicting outside the range is extrapolation.

solve.answer: Interpolation

questions.skill: Critiquing a misleading display
questions.stem: A pie chart labels its slices 40 percent, 35 percent, 30 percent and 25 percent. These labels add up to more than 100 percent. By how many percentage points do they pass 100 percent?
questions.solution: The labels add to $40 + 35 + 30 + 25 = 130$ percent. A whole pie is 100 percent, so the labels are $130 - 100 = 30$ points too many.

questions.skill: Critiquing a misleading display
questions.stem: The labels on the vertical axis of a bar graph are 0, 10, 20, 50 and 100, drawn at equal spacing. Why is this misleading?
choices: Equal spaces on the axis stand for different amounts
The axis has too few labels
The axis should start at 10 instead of 0
The labels should be written in order from largest to smallest
questions.answer: Equal spaces on the axis stand for different amounts
questions.solution: On a fair axis, equal spaces stand for equal amounts. Here the step from 20 to 50 uses the same space as the step from 0 to 10, which distorts the bar heights.

solve.answer: Equal spaces on the axis stand for different amounts
solve.work: Equal gaps stand for 10, 10, 30, 50 units: unequal amounts, misleading.

questions.skill: Critiquing a misleading display
questions.stem: A graph of monthly rainfall has no title and no labels on either axis. What is the main problem with it?
choices: The graph has too many bars for a reader to count them
The bars are not all drawn in the same color, so it looks messy
A reader cannot tell what is measured or in which units
The graph shows rainfall instead of showing temperature
questions.answer: A reader cannot tell what is measured or in which units
questions.solution: Without a title and labels, a reader cannot tell which quantities are shown or what units they have, so the graph cannot be interpreted.

solve.answer: A reader cannot tell what is measured or in which units
solve.work: Without title or axis labels a reader cannot tell what is measured or its units.

questions.skill: Reading non-standard displays
questions.stem: A bubble chart plots each country: the horizontal position is average income, the vertical position is life expectancy, and the size of each bubble shows population. What does a bigger bubble mean?
choices: The country has a larger population
The country has a higher average income
The country has a longer life expectancy
The country has more land
questions.answer: The country has a larger population
questions.solution: Position shows income and life expectancy. The size of the bubble is the third variable, which the chart says is population.

solve.answer: The country has a larger population
solve.work: Bubble size shows population, so a bigger bubble means a larger population.

questions.skill: Reading non-standard displays
questions.stem: A chart must show three numbers for each city on one plot: parks, average commute time and population. Which display can do this?
choices: A pie chart, using one slice for each of the cities
A single bar graph, using the height of each bar
A scatter plot, using only its two axes for the numbers
A bubble chart, using bubble size for the third number
questions.answer: A bubble chart, using bubble size for the third number
questions.solution: A scatter plot shows two numbers by position. A bubble chart adds a third number as the size of each point, so it can show all three.

solve.answer: A bubble chart, using bubble size for the third number
solve.work: Three numbers per city: two axes plus bubble size, a bubble chart.

questions.skill: Choosing and building a scatter plot
questions.stem: A teacher wants to see how the hours 20 students studied relate to their test scores. Which display is best?
choices: A scatter plot, with one axis for hours and one for scores
A pie chart with one slice for each of the 20 students
A bar graph that shows only the names of the students
A table that lists only the scores, in order from low to high
questions.answer: A scatter plot, with one axis for hours and one for scores
questions.solution: To see how two numerical variables are related, each student's pair of values is plotted as one point. That is a scatter plot.

solve.answer: A scatter plot, with one axis for hours and one for scores
solve.work: Two numerical variables per student: a scatter plot with hours and scores on the axes.

questions.skill: Choosing and building a scatter plot
questions.stem: A researcher wants to see whether the number of hours students study helps predict their quiz score. Which variable usually goes on the horizontal axis?
choices: Hours studied
Quiz score
The students' names
Whichever is larger
questions.answer: Hours studied
questions.solution: The variable used to predict, here hours studied, goes on the horizontal axis. The variable being predicted, the quiz score, goes on the vertical axis.

solve.answer: Hours studied
solve.work: The explanatory (predictor) variable, hours studied, goes on the horizontal axis.

questions.skill: Reading non-standard displays
questions.stem: Each point on a scatter plot shows a student's height and arm span, and the color of the point shows the student's grade (6, 7 or 8). How many different variables does each point show?
questions.solution: Each point shows the height, the arm span and the grade, so it shows 3 variables. The grade is carried by the color of the point.

solve.work: Height, arm span and grade: 3 variables.

questions.skill: Comparing the strength of associations
choices: Q shows a stronger linear association than P
P shows a stronger linear association than Q
P and Q show equally strong associations, because both go upward
Q shows a negative association and P a positive one
questions.answer: P shows a stronger linear association than Q
questions.solution: Every point of P lies exactly on the line $y = 2x$, a perfectly strong linear association. Q rises overall but its points are scattered above and below any line, so the association is positive and weaker.

solve.answer: P shows a stronger linear association than Q
solve.work: P lies exactly on y = 2x (perfect linear). Q rises overall (3,2,6,5,8) but zigzags, so its linear association is weaker. Both positive.

questions.skill: Slope of a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit for the age of a car, $x$ (in years), and its value, $y$ (in thousands of dollars), passes through $(2, 18)$ and $(6, 10)$. What is the slope of the line?
questions.solution: Slope $= \frac{10 - 18}{6 - 2} = \frac{-8}{4} = -2$. The value drops by 2 thousand dollars for each extra year of age.

questions.skill: Recognizing a nonlinear form
questions.stem: A scatter plot has the points $(0, 1)$, $(1, 2)$, $(2, 4)$, $(3, 8)$ and $(4, 16)$. Which kind of model fits these points best?
choices: A straight line with positive slope
A straight line with negative slope
No pattern at all
A curve that rises faster and faster
questions.answer: A curve that rises faster and faster
questions.solution: The $y$-values double each time $x$ goes up by 1 (1, 2, 4, 8, 16), so the points rise by larger and larger amounts. They follow an upward curve, not a straight line.

solve.answer: A curve that rises faster and faster
solve.work: y doubles each step (1,2,4,8,16): exponential growth, a curve rising faster and faster.

questions.skill: Reading a point in context
questions.stem: A museum counted its visitors on five days. The scatter plot of (day of the month, visitors) has the points $(2, 11)$, $(5, 17)$, $(7, 15)$, $(9, 22)$ and $(12, 20)$. How many more visitors came on the busiest day than on the quietest day?
questions.solution: The busiest day has the greatest vertical value, 22 visitors. The quietest day has the least, 11 visitors. The difference is $22 - 11 = 11$.

questions.skill: Reading a point in context
questions.stem: In a scatter plot of bike rides, each point is (distance in miles, time in minutes). One ride is plotted at $(6, 42)$. At that ride's pace, how many minutes did each mile take?
questions.solution: The ride covered 6 miles in 42 minutes, so each mile took $42 \div 6 = 7$ minutes.

questions.skill: Reading a point in context
questions.stem: A scatter plot of used cars has age in years on the horizontal axis and price in thousands of dollars on the vertical axis. Car P is plotted at $(3, 15)$ and car Q at $(8, 6)$. Which statement is true?
choices: Car P is older and costs more than car Q
Car P is newer and costs more than car Q
Car P is newer and costs less than car Q
Car P is older and costs less than car Q
questions.answer: Car P is newer and costs more than car Q
questions.solution: Car P has age 3 and car Q has age 8, so P is newer. Car P has price 15 and car Q has price 6, so P costs more.

solve.answer: Car P is newer and costs more than car Q
solve.work: P: age 3, price 15; Q: age 8, price 6. P is newer (3 < 8) and costs more (15 > 6).

questions.skill: Direction of an association
questions.stem: A scatter plot has the points $(1, 3)$, $(2, 5)$, $(3, 4)$, $(4, 7)$, $(5, 6)$ and $(6, 9)$. Which statement describes the direction of the association?
choices: Negative: y goes down at some places, so it tends to decrease as x increases
None: y goes up and down, so there is no overall pattern to the points
None: the points do not all lie on one straight line, so they show no trend
Positive: y tends to increase as x increases, despite a few dips
questions.answer: Positive: y tends to increase as x increases, despite a few dips
questions.solution: The values dip twice (5 to 4, and 7 to 6) but the overall trend from 3 to 9 is upward, so the direction is positive. A few dips and points off a line do not make the association negative or absent.

solve.answer: Positive: y tends to increase as x increases, despite a few dips
solve.work: y: 3, 5, 4, 7, 6, 9. Overall rising from 3 to 9 with small dips: positive.

questions.skill: Form of an association
questions.stem: A scatter plot has the points $(1, 2)$, $(2, 5)$, $(3, 6)$, $(4, 5)$ and $(5, 2)$. Which description fits the form of the pattern?
choices: Nonlinear: the points rise and then fall, forming an arch
Linear with a positive direction, because the first jump is upward
Linear with a negative direction, because the last jump is downward
Exponential growth, because the points start by rising quickly
questions.answer: Nonlinear: the points rise and then fall, forming an arch
questions.solution: The y-values go 2, 5, 6, 5, 2: they rise to a peak at $x = 3$ and then fall back. A pattern that changes direction cannot be a straight line, so it is nonlinear (an arch).

solve.answer: Nonlinear: the points rise and then fall, forming an arch
solve.work: y: 2, 5, 6, 5, 2 rises then falls symmetrically: nonlinear arch.

questions.skill: Form of an association
questions.stem: The value of a delivery van is $20{,}000$, $16{,}000$, $12{,}800$ and $10{,}240$ dollars at ages 0, 1, 2 and 3 years. Which description fits the pattern?
choices: Linear: each value is $4{,}000$ less than the one before
Exponential growth: each value is 1.25 times the one before
Exponential decay: each value is 0.8 times the one before
Exponential decay: each value is 0.2 times the one before
questions.answer: Exponential decay: each value is 0.8 times the one before
questions.solution: The drops are 4000, 3200 and 2560, so the change is not constant and the pattern is not linear. The ratios are $16000 \div 20000 = 0.8$, $12800 \div 16000 = 0.8$ and $10240 \div 12800 = 0.8$, so each value is 0.8 times the one before.

solve.answer: Exponential decay: each value is 0.8 times the one before
solve.work: 16000/20000 = 0.8, 12800/16000 = 0.8, 10240/12800 = 0.8: exponential decay by factor 0.8. Differences 4000, 3200, 2560 are not constant.

questions.skill: Form of an association
questions.stem: A mold sample covers 5, 15 and 45 square centimeters on days 0, 1 and 2. If the exponential pattern continues, how many square centimeters will it cover on day 3?
questions.solution: Each area is 3 times the one before: $5 \times 3 = 15$ and $15 \times 3 = 45$. On day 3 the area is $45 \times 3 = 135$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Strength of an association
questions.stem: In plot 1 the points follow the line $y = 5x$ closely. In plot 2 the points follow the line $y = 2x$ equally closely. A student says plot 1 has the stronger association because its line is steeper. What is wrong with this reasoning?
choices: Nothing is wrong: a steeper line always means a stronger association
Strength depends on how close the points are to the line, not its steepness
A line with a smaller slope always means a stronger association, whatever the points do
Strength depends only on how many points the plot has, not on the line
questions.answer: Strength depends on how close the points are to the line, not its steepness
questions.solution: Both plots have points equally close to their lines, so the two associations are equally strong. Slope tells how fast y changes, not how tightly the points follow the line.

solve.answer: Strength depends on how close the points are to the line, not its steepness
solve.work: Both plots follow their lines equally closely, so equal strength; slope does not measure strength.

questions.skill: Strength of an association
questions.stem: A line of best fit is $y = 2x + 1$. The data points are $(1, 3)$, $(2, 6)$, $(3, 7)$, $(4, 12)$ and $(5, 11)$. For how many points is the vertical distance to the line at most 1 unit?
questions.solution: The line gives 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 at $x = 1$ to 5. The points are off by 0, 1, 0, 3 and 0. Four of the distances (0, 1, 0, 0) are at most 1; only $(4, 12)$ is farther, at 3 units.

solve.work: Line values 3, 5, 7, 9, 11. Distances: 0, 1, 0, 3, 0. At most 1: four points.

questions.skill: Judging an informal line of best fit
questions.stem: The data points are $(1, 3)$, $(2, 5)$, $(3, 6)$, $(4, 9)$ and $(5, 10)$. Which line fits them best?
questions.solution: Compare each line's values at $x = 1$ to 5 with 3, 5, 6, 9, 10. The line $y = 2x + 1$ gives 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, off by only 0, 0, 1, 0, 1. The line $y = x + 3$ gives 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 (off by up to 2). The line $y = 3x$ gives 3, 6, 9, 12, 15 (off by up to 5), and $y = 2x - 3$ gives $-1$, 1, 3, 5, 7 (off by 3 or more at every point).

questions.skill: Judging an informal line of best fit
questions.stem: A line has the equation $y = 2x + 3$. Six data points are $(1, 4)$, $(2, 9)$, $(3, 8)$, $(4, 13)$, $(5, 12)$ and $(6, 14)$. How many more points lie below the line than above it?
questions.solution: The line gives 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 and 15 at $x = 1$ to 6. The points $(2, 9)$ and $(4, 13)$ are above the line (2 points). The points $(1, 4)$, $(3, 8)$, $(5, 12)$ and $(6, 14)$ are below it (4 points). That is $4 - 2 = 2$ more below.

solve.work: Line values 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15. Points 4 (below), 9 (above), 8 (below), 13 (above), 12 (below), 14 (below). Below 4, above 2. Difference 2.

questions.skill: Judging an informal line of best fit
questions.stem: Which statement about an informal line of best fit is true?
choices: It must pass through at least two of the data points on the scatter plot
It must start at the origin of the plot, where both axes are equal to 0
Two people may draw slightly different lines and both be reasonable
It must connect the first point to the last point, with no exceptions
questions.answer: Two people may draw slightly different lines and both be reasonable
questions.solution: An informal line only needs to follow the trend, with points scattered on both sides. Reasonable lines can differ a little, and no data point or the origin has to be on the line.

solve.answer: Two people may draw slightly different lines and both be reasonable
solve.work: An informal line is drawn by eye; two reasonable lines may differ slightly. It need not pass through the origin, the end points, or any data points.

questions.skill: Predicting from a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit for a laptop's age, $x$ (in years), and its resale value, $y$ (in dollars), is $y = -120x + 800$. What value does the line predict for a laptop that is 3.5 years old, in dollars?
questions.solution: Substitute $x = 3.5$: $y = -120 \times 3.5 + 800 = -420 + 800 = 380$ dollars.

questions.skill: Predicting from a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit for the hours a tutor works, $x$, and the pay received, $y$ (in dollars), is $y = 12x + 15$. For how many hours does the line predict a pay of 87 dollars?
questions.solution: Set $12x + 15 = 87$. Subtract 15 to get $12x = 72$, then divide by 12 to get $x = 6$ hours.

questions.skill: Predicting from a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit passes through $(10, 30)$ and $(20, 50)$. Which is the best prediction of $y$ when $x = 15$?
questions.solution: The value $x = 15$ is exactly halfway between 10 and 20, so $y$ is halfway between 30 and 50: $(30 + 50) \div 2 = 40$.

questions.skill: Slope of a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit for the hours a phone has been charging, $x$, and its battery level in percent, $y$, is $y = 12x + 8$. Which is the best interpretation of the slope, 12?
choices: The battery rises about 12 percentage points for each hour of charging
The battery level was 12 percent at the moment when charging began
The battery level is only 8 percent after 12 hours of charging
The phone takes exactly 12 hours to charge from empty to full
questions.answer: The battery rises about 12 percentage points for each hour of charging
questions.solution: The slope is the change in $y$ for each increase of 1 in $x$. Each extra hour of charging adds about 12 percentage points. The 8 is the starting level.

solve.answer: The battery rises about 12 percentage points for each hour of charging
solve.work: Slope 12 = change in battery percent per hour: about 12 percentage points per hour of charging.

questions.skill: Slope of a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit for the number of cookies baked, $x$, and the cups of flour used, $y$, passes through $(12, 3)$ and $(36, 9)$. What is the slope of the line?
questions.solution: Slope is $(9 - 3) \div (36 - 12) = 6 \div 24 = 0.25$. This means 0.25 cup of flour for each cookie.

questions.skill: Intercept of a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit for the hours a bike is rented, $x$, and the total cost in dollars, $y$, is $y = 18x + 30$. Which is the best interpretation of the 30?
choices: The extra cost the line predicts for each additional hour of renting
The number of hours the bike must be rented for the cost to reach 18 dollars
The predicted cost after renting the bike for a full 30 hours
The predicted cost for 0 hours, a starting fee of 30 dollars
questions.answer: The predicted cost for 0 hours, a starting fee of 30 dollars
questions.solution: The $y$-intercept is the predicted $y$ when $x = 0$. Here that is the cost with no hours rented, a starting fee of 30 dollars. The 18 is the cost for each hour.

solve.answer: The predicted cost for 0 hours, a starting fee of 30 dollars
solve.work: 30 is the y-intercept: predicted cost at 0 hours, a starting fee.

questions.skill: Intercept of a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit has a slope of 3 and passes through $(2, 14)$. What is its $y$-intercept?
questions.solution: Going back from $x = 2$ to $x = 0$ takes 2 steps of 3, so $y$ is $2 \times 3 = 6$ lower: $14 - 6 = 8$.

questions.skill: Outliers, clusters and gaps
questions.stem: A scatter plot has 9 points that follow a rising line closely and one more point far above that line at the right end. A line of best fit is drawn through all 10 points. If the far-above point is removed and the line is drawn again, how will the line change?
choices: It will be less steep and will follow the other 9 points more closely
It will be steeper and will follow the other 9 points more closely
It will not change, because one point is only 1 of 10
It will move up by the distance from the removed point to the old line
questions.answer: It will be less steep and will follow the other 9 points more closely
questions.solution: A point far above the line at the right end pulls the right end of the line upward, making it steeper. Removing it lets the line settle back toward the other points, so it becomes less steep.

solve.answer: It will be less steep and will follow the other 9 points more closely
solve.work: A point far above the line at the right end pulls that end up, steepening the fit. Removing it makes the line less steep and closer to the other 9.

questions.skill: Interpolation and extrapolation
questions.stem: A line of best fit for the age of a laptop, $x$ (from 1 to 6 years), and its value in dollars, $y$, is $y = -150x + 900$. A shop uses the line for a 10-year-old laptop. Why is the answer unreasonable?
choices: The line gives a value of 600 dollars, which is too high for an old laptop
The line gives $-600$ dollars, and 10 years is far outside the data
The line cannot be used for any laptop older than 1 year, since the data start there
The line gives a value of 0 dollars at 10 years, so the line itself must be wrong
questions.answer: The line gives $-600$ dollars, and 10 years is far outside the data
questions.solution: At $x = 10$ the line gives $-150 \times 10 + 900 = -600$, a negative price. That is extrapolation, far beyond the 1 to 6 years of data, so the prediction should not be trusted.

solve.answer: The line gives $-600$ dollars, and 10 years is far outside the data
solve.work: y = -150(10) + 900 = -600: a negative value, and 10 is far outside 1-6 (extrapolation).

questions.skill: Critiquing a misleading display
questions.stem: On a bar graph, the vertical axis starts at 45 instead of 0. One bar shows 50 dollars saved and another shows 55 dollars saved. Measured from the start of the axis, the bar for 55 looks how many times as tall as the bar for 50?
questions.solution: The bar for 50 looks $50 - 45 = 5$ units tall and the bar for 55 looks $55 - 45 = 10$ units tall. So the second bar looks $10 \div 5 = 2$ times as tall, though 55 is only 1.1 times 50.

questions.skill: Critiquing a misleading display
questions.stem: To show that a company's profit doubled, a graphic makes a picture of a coin twice as wide and twice as tall. The coin's area becomes how many times as large?
questions.solution: Doubling both the width and the height multiplies the area by $2 \times 2 = 4$. The picture looks 4 times as big, though the profit only doubled.

questions.skill: Critiquing a misleading display
questions.stem: The same monthly sales, rising from 41 to 46, are shown on two line graphs. Graph 1 has a vertical axis from 0 to 50. Graph 2 has a vertical axis from 40 to 47. Which statement is true?
choices: The data differ: graph 1 shows less of the sales than graph 2
The data are the same, but graph 2 makes the rise look larger
Graph 2 shows a bigger increase in sales than graph 1 does
Both graphs make the rise look equally large to a reader
questions.answer: The data are the same, but graph 2 makes the rise look larger
questions.solution: The sales are the same in both graphs. Graph 2 uses a narrow axis range that magnifies the small rise, while graph 1 shows it at a fair scale.

solve.answer: The data are the same, but graph 2 makes the rise look larger
solve.work: Same data; graph 2's narrow axis (40-47) stretches the rise so it looks larger.

questions.skill: Reading non-standard displays
questions.stem: In a bubble chart, each bubble is a city: the horizontal value is the number of parks, the vertical value is the average commute in minutes, and the bubble's label gives the population in thousands. City P is at $(12, 25)$ with a bubble labeled 340. City Q is at $(8, 31)$ with a bubble labeled 215. How many thousand more people live in P than in Q?
questions.solution: The population is shown by the bubble labels, not by the position. City P has 340 thousand and city Q has 215 thousand, so the difference is $340 - 215 = 125$ thousand.

questions.skill: Choosing and building a scatter plot
questions.stem: A student plots data with $x$-values from 0 to 50. The horizontal axis is 10 squares wide, and every square stands for the same whole number of units. What is the smallest number of units each square can stand for if 50 must fit on the axis?
questions.solution: Ten squares must cover at least 50 units, so each square must stand for at least $50 \div 10 = 5$ units.

solve.work: 10 squares x u units must reach 50: 10u >= 50, so u = 5.

questions.skill: Choosing and building a scatter plot
questions.stem: A table gives the daily temperature and the number of ice-cream cones sold: (60 degrees, 20 cones), (70 degrees, 35 cones) and (80 degrees, 50 cones). With temperature on the horizontal axis, which list gives the points to plot?
questions.solution: Each row gives one point, with temperature first (horizontal) and cones second (vertical): $(60, 20)$, $(70, 35)$ and $(80, 50)$. The other lists swap the coordinates or pair values from different rows.

questions.skill: Choosing and building a scatter plot
questions.stem: Which pair of measurements could NOT be shown fairly on a scatter plot as it stands?
choices: Each student's height and arm span
Each student's age and shoe size
Each student's hours of sleep and hours of study
Each student's favorite color and number of pets
questions.answer: Each student's favorite color and number of pets
questions.solution: A scatter plot needs two numerical variables, so that each point has a horizontal and a vertical value. A favorite color is a category, not a number.

solve.answer: Each student's favorite color and number of pets
solve.work: Favorite color is categorical and cannot be placed on a numerical axis; the other pairs are both numerical.

questions.skill: Slope of a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit for a bicycle's age, $x$ (in years), and its price, $y$ (in dollars), is $y = -45x + 400$. According to the line, how many dollars less is the predicted price of a 6-year-old bicycle than the predicted price of a 2-year-old bicycle?
questions.solution: Each extra year changes the predicted price by $-45$ dollars, which is 45 dollars less. The bicycles are 6 - 2 = 4 years apart, so the predicted price is $45 \times 4 = 180$ dollars less. (Check: at 2 years the line gives 310 dollars and at 6 years it gives 130 dollars, and 310 - 130 = 180.)

questions.skill: Reading non-standard displays
questions.stem: Each point in a data display is written (hours of sleep, test score, grade level): (6, 70, 9), (7, 78, 10), (8, 85, 9), (9, 92, 10), (7, 74, 9). Look only at the points for grade 10. How many points higher is the test score of the student who slept the most hours than the test score of the student who slept the fewest hours?
questions.solution: The grade 10 points are (7, 78, 10) and (9, 92, 10). The student who slept the most (9 hours) scored 92 and the student who slept the fewest (7 hours) scored 78. The difference is $92 - 78 = 14$ points.

solve.work: Grade 10 points: (7,78) and (9,92). Most sleep 9 -> 92, fewest 7 -> 78. 92 - 78 = 14.

questions.skill: Interpreting the slope of a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit for hours of practice ($x$) and test score ($y$) is $y = 3x + 40$. Which is the best interpretation of the slope, 3?
choices: Each extra hour of practice goes with about 3 more points, on average
A student who does not practice scores about 3
A student who practices 3 hours scores exactly 40
Each extra point goes with about 3 more hours of practice
questions.answer: Each extra hour of practice goes with about 3 more points, on average
questions.solution: The slope is the change in $y$ for each 1-unit increase in $x$: each extra hour of practice goes with about 3 more points of score, on average. The 40 is the predicted score for 0 hours.

solve.answer: Each extra hour of practice goes with about 3 more points, on average
solve.work: Slope 3 = predicted change in score per extra hour of practice: about 3 more points per hour on average.

questions.skill: Predicting from two points on a line
questions.stem: A line of best fit passes through $(1, 12)$ and $(5, 20)$. Use the line to predict $y$ when $x = 8$.
questions.solution: Slope $= \frac{20 - 12}{5 - 1} = 2$. From $x = 1$ to $x = 8$ is 7 units, so $y$ rises by $2 \times 7 = 14$ from 12: $y = 26$.

questions.skill: Critiquing a misleading display
questions.stem: A news graph shows the test pass rates of two classes as bars. Class A's pass rate is 90 percent and Class B's is 85 percent. The vertical axis starts at 80 percent instead of 0, so Class A's bar looks twice as tall as Class B's. Why is this display misleading?
choices: Bars should never be used to compare two classes
The pass rates should have been shown as decimals
Starting the axis at 80 makes a small difference look much larger than it is
Class B's bar should be taller because its class is smaller
questions.answer: Starting the axis at 80 makes a small difference look much larger than it is
questions.solution: With the axis starting at 80, the bars show heights of 10 and 5, which looks like a 2-to-1 difference. The real pass rates, 90 and 85 percent, differ by only 5 points.

solve.answer: Starting the axis at 80 makes a small difference look much larger than it is
solve.work: Bars from 80: A shows 10, B shows 5, so A looks twice as tall although the difference is only 5 points. Truncated axis exaggerates the difference.

questions.skill: Reading a point in context
questions.stem: Each point is (minutes of exercise, calories burned): $(10, 80)$, $(20, 150)$, $(30, 200)$ and $(40, 330)$. One point burned the most calories per minute. What is that rate, in calories per minute?
questions.solution: Divide calories by minutes for each point: $80 \div 10 = 8$, $150 \div 20 = 7.5$, $200 \div 30 \approx 6.67$ and $330 \div 40 = 8.25$. The greatest rate is 8.25 calories per minute.

questions.skill: Reading a point in context
questions.stem: Plant heights (week, centimeters) are $(1, 4)$, $(2, 7)$, $(3, 7)$ and $(4, 12)$. Which statement is true?
choices: The plant grew the most between week 1 and week 2
The plant was 12 centimeters tall at week 3
The plant lost height between week 2 and week 3
The plant grew the most between week 3 and week 4
questions.answer: The plant grew the most between week 3 and week 4
questions.solution: The changes in height are $7 - 4 = 3$ (weeks 1 to 2), $7 - 7 = 0$ (weeks 2 to 3) and $12 - 7 = 5$ (weeks 3 to 4). The plant grew the most between week 3 and week 4. It was 7 centimeters tall at week 3, and it did not lose height.

solve.answer: The plant grew the most between week 3 and week 4
solve.work: Changes: week 1-2 +3, week 2-3 0, week 3-4 +5. Largest growth between weeks 3 and 4. No loss; height at week 3 is 7.

questions.skill: Direction of an association
questions.stem: A scatter plot shows the number of days left until a project is due (horizontal) and the number of tasks finished (vertical). Teams finish more tasks as the due date gets closer. What is the direction of the association?
choices: Positive: more tasks are finished as the due date gets closer
Positive: both values are counts, so they rise together
Negative: fewer days left goes with more tasks finished
None: the due date does not change the tasks finished
questions.answer: Negative: fewer days left goes with more tasks finished
questions.solution: The horizontal value is days left. As it goes down, tasks finished goes up, so the two values move in opposite directions: a negative association.

solve.answer: Negative: fewer days left goes with more tasks finished
solve.work: x = days left. As x decreases (due date nearer), tasks finished increase, so larger x goes with fewer tasks: negative.

questions.skill: Direction of an association
questions.stem: A scatter plot with a car's age (horizontal) and its price (vertical) shows a negative association. A new plot is made with price on the horizontal axis and age on the vertical axis. What direction will the new plot show?
choices: Negative: swapping the axes does not change the direction
Positive: swapping the axes reverses the direction of the pattern
None: the variables have changed roles, so the pattern is lost
Negative on the left side and positive on the right side
questions.answer: Negative: swapping the axes does not change the direction
questions.solution: Older cars tend to cost less, and cheaper cars tend to be older. Both statements describe the same negative relationship, so swapping the axes keeps the association negative.

solve.answer: Negative: swapping the axes does not change the direction
solve.work: If price falls as age rises, then age falls as price rises; swapping axes keeps a negative direction.

questions.skill: Form of an association
questions.stem: A scatter plot has the points $(1, 10)$, $(2, 18)$, $(3, 24)$, $(4, 28)$ and $(5, 30)$. Which description fits the pattern?
choices: Positive and linear: y rises by the same amount each step
Positive and nonlinear: y rises by less with each step
Positive and exponential: y rises by more with each step
Negative and nonlinear: y falls by less with each step
questions.answer: Positive and nonlinear: y rises by less with each step
questions.solution: The increases in y are 8, 6, 4 and 2. They are not equal, so the pattern is not linear, and they shrink, so it is not exponential growth. All values rise, so the association is positive but nonlinear, levelling off.

solve.answer: Positive and nonlinear: y rises by less with each step
solve.work: Differences 8, 6, 4, 2: y rises by less each step; positive and nonlinear.

questions.skill: Form of an association
questions.stem: The y-values for $x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4$ are 16, 24, 36, 54 and 81. Which statement describes the pattern best?
choices: Linear: each y is 8 more than the one before
Linear: each y is 12 more than the one before
Exponential: each y is 2 times as large as the one before
Exponential: each y is 1.5 times the one before
questions.answer: Exponential: each y is 1.5 times the one before
questions.solution: The differences are 8, 12, 18 and 27, which are not constant, so the pattern is not linear. The ratios $24 \div 16$, $36 \div 24$, $54 \div 36$ and $81 \div 54$ all equal 1.5, so the pattern is exponential with a factor of 1.5.

solve.answer: Exponential: each y is 1.5 times the one before
solve.work: 24/16 = 1.5, 36/24 = 1.5, 54/36 = 1.5, 81/54 = 1.5: exponential with factor 1.5. Differences 8, 12, 18, 27 not constant.

questions.skill: Strength of an association
questions.stem: A line of best fit is $y = 2.5x + 10$. The data points are $(2, 16)$, $(4, 18)$, $(6, 27)$, $(8, 29)$ and $(10, 31)$. How many units, measured straight up or down, is the point farthest from the line?
questions.solution: The line gives 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 at $x = 2, 4, 6, 8, 10$. The points are off by 1, 2, 2, 1 and 4. The farthest is $(10, 31)$, which is $35 - 31 = 4$ units below the line.

questions.skill: Strength of an association
questions.stem: The points $(0, 3)$, $(1, 6)$, $(2, 12)$, $(3, 24)$ and $(4, 48)$ lie exactly on a smooth curve but not on any straight line. Which statement is correct?
choices: The association is strong, but it is not linear
The association is weak, because the points are not on a line
The association is strong and linear, because y always increases
The association is strong only if a straight line is drawn through the points
questions.answer: The association is strong, but it is not linear
questions.solution: The points follow an exact pattern (each y is double the one before), so the association is strong. A strong association does not have to be linear; this one is exponential.

solve.answer: The association is strong, but it is not linear
solve.work: Values double (3, 6, 12, 24, 48) and lie exactly on a curve: strong but nonlinear.

questions.skill: Strength of an association
questions.stem: A line of best fit is $y = 4x - 2$ and the data points are $(1, 3)$, $(2, 7)$, $(3, 12)$, $(4, 13)$ and $(5, 19)$. Add up the vertical distances from the five points to the line, counting every distance as positive. What is the total?
questions.solution: The line gives 2, 6, 10, 14 and 18 at $x = 1$ to 5. The distances are $1, 1, 2, 1, 1$, and the total is $1 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 6$.

questions.skill: Judging an informal line of best fit
questions.stem: Two students fit lines to the points $(2, 18)$, $(4, 26)$, $(6, 30)$, $(8, 36)$ and $(10, 40)$. Line 1 is $y = 3x + 10$ and line 2 is $y = 2x + 18$. Which line fits better?
choices: Line 1, because its vertical distances to the points add to 10, against 8 for line 2
Neither: the two lines fit the points equally well
Neither: a line of best fit must pass through at least two points
Line 2, because its vertical distances to the points add to 8, against 10 for line 1
questions.answer: Line 2, because its vertical distances to the points add to 8, against 10 for line 1
questions.solution: Line 1 gives 16, 22, 28, 34, 40, which are off by 2, 4, 2, 2, 0 (total 10). Line 2 gives 22, 26, 30, 34, 38, which are off by 4, 0, 0, 2, 2 (total 8). A smaller total distance means a better fit, so line 2 fits better.

solve.answer: Line 2, because its vertical distances to the points add to 8, against 10 for line 1
solve.work: Line 1 values 16, 22, 28, 34, 40: distances 2, 4, 2, 2, 0 = 10. Line 2 values 22, 26, 30, 34, 38: distances 4, 0, 0, 2, 2 = 8. Line 2 fits better (also by squares: 24 vs 28).

questions.skill: Judging an informal line of best fit
questions.stem: A scatter plot has the points $(0, 48)$, $(5, 60)$, $(10, 75)$, $(15, 91)$ and $(20, 100)$. Which equation best describes the trend?
questions.solution: The line should start near 48 at $x = 0$ and end near 100 at $x = 20$. The line $y = 2.6x + 48$ gives 48, 61, 74, 87, 100, which is very close. The line $y = 1.5x + 50$ ends at 80, the line $y = 2.6x + 20$ starts at 20, and the line $y = 4x + 48$ ends at 128.

solve.work: Slope about (100 - 48)/20 = 2.6, start 48. y = 2.6x + 48 gives 48, 61, 74, 87, 100 vs 48, 60, 75, 91, 100: close. Others miss badly (1.5x+50 ends at 80; 4x+48 ends at 128; 2.6x+20 starts at 20).

questions.skill: Predicting from a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit for the number of weeks, $x$, that a gym member has attended and the number of push-ups, $y$, they can do is $y = 2.5x + 12$. After how many weeks does the line predict 37 push-ups?
questions.solution: Set $2.5x + 12 = 37$. Subtract 12 to get $2.5x = 25$, then divide by 2.5 to get $x = 10$ weeks.

questions.skill: Predicting from a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit passes through $(3, 14)$ and $(9, 38)$. Use the line to predict $y$ when $x = 5$.
questions.solution: The slope is $(38 - 14) \div (9 - 3) = 24 \div 6 = 4$. From $x = 3$ to $x = 5$ is 2 steps, so $y = 14 + 4 \times 2 = 22$.

questions.skill: Predicting from a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit has a slope of $-1.5$ and passes through $(4, 22)$. What value of $y$ does the line predict when $x = 10$?
questions.solution: From $x = 4$ to $x = 10$ is 6 steps. Each step changes $y$ by $-1.5$, a total of $-9$. So $y = 22 - 9 = 13$.

questions.skill: Slope of a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit for the outside temperature, $x$ (in degrees), and a monthly heating bill, $y$ (in dollars), passes through $(15, 210)$ and $(55, 122)$. What is the slope of the line?
questions.solution: Slope is $(122 - 210) \div (55 - 15) = -88 \div 40 = -2.2$. The bill drops 2.20 dollars for each degree the temperature rises.

questions.skill: Slope of a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit for the minutes a student plays a game, $x$, and the minutes of homework finished that evening, $y$, is $y = -0.5x + 60$. Which is the best interpretation of the slope, $-0.5$?
choices: Each extra minute of play goes with about half a minute more homework finished
Each extra minute of play goes with about half a minute less homework finished
A student who does not play is predicted to finish half a minute of homework
A student who plays for 60 minutes is predicted to finish no homework
questions.answer: Each extra minute of play goes with about half a minute less homework finished
questions.solution: The slope is the predicted change in $y$ for each increase of 1 in $x$. Here $y$ falls by 0.5 for each extra minute of play. The other statements confuse the slope with the intercept or give a wrong prediction (at $x = 60$ the line gives 30).

solve.answer: Each extra minute of play goes with about half a minute less homework finished
solve.work: Slope -0.5: each extra minute of play goes with about half a minute less homework.

questions.skill: Intercept of a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit passes through $(4, 5)$ and $(10, 17)$. What is its $y$-intercept?
questions.solution: The slope is $(17 - 5) \div (10 - 4) = 12 \div 6 = 2$. Going back from $x = 4$ to $x = 0$ lowers $y$ by $2 \times 4 = 8$, so the intercept is $5 - 8 = -3$.

questions.skill: Outliers, clusters and gaps
questions.stem: A scatter plot has the points $(1, 12)$, $(2, 15)$, $(3, 18)$, $(4, 21)$, $(5, 40)$, $(6, 27)$, $(7, 30)$ and $(8, 33)$. Seven of the points lie on one straight line. What would $y$ be at $x = 5$ if that point were on the line too?
questions.solution: On the line, $y$ rises by 3 for each step in $x$: 12, 15, 18, 21, then 24, 27, 30, 33. At $x = 5$ the line gives 24. The point $(5, 40)$ is the outlier.

solve.work: Other points: slope 3, y = 3x + 9 (12 at x = 1). At x = 5: 15 + 9 = 24.

questions.skill: Outliers, clusters and gaps
questions.stem: A scientist sees one point far from the pattern in a scatter plot of her measurements. What is the best thing to do?
choices: Delete it at once, because every outlier is a mistake in measuring
Keep it and never mention it, because all of the data must be kept
Check whether it was recorded wrongly, and say what was done
Delete the points near it as well, so that the pattern is clear
questions.answer: Check whether it was recorded wrongly, and say what was done
questions.solution: An outlier may be a recording error, or it may be a real and important result. It should be checked, and a scientist should be open about it rather than silently removing or hiding data.

solve.answer: Check whether it was recorded wrongly, and say what was done
solve.work: Investigate the outlier (recording error?) and report what was done; do not silently keep or delete.

questions.skill: Interpolation and extrapolation
questions.stem: A line of best fit was made from data with $x$-values from 20 to 60. For how many of the values $x = 10$, $25$, $40$, $55$ and $75$ would using the line to predict be extrapolation?
questions.solution: Extrapolation means going outside the range of the data. The values 10 and 75 are outside 20 to 60, while 25, 40 and 55 are inside. So 2 of the values would be extrapolation.

questions.skill: Interpolation and extrapolation
questions.stem: A line fits data with $x$-values from 20 to 60 very closely. A student predicts $y$ for $x = 100$ and says the answer is certain because the fit is so close. Which response is best?
choices: The student is right: a close fit means the line works at any x
The student should use only the data point at x = 60 for the prediction
The student is right, but only if the line is steep enough to be reliable
A close fit from 20 to 60 does not guarantee the pattern continues to 100
questions.answer: A close fit from 20 to 60 does not guarantee the pattern continues to 100
questions.solution: A line describes the data it was fitted to. Beyond that range the relationship may change, so a prediction at $x = 100$ is extrapolation and uncertain, however close the fit was.

solve.answer: A close fit from 20 to 60 does not guarantee the pattern continues to 100
solve.work: x = 100 is far outside 20-60; a close fit inside the range does not guarantee the pattern continues.

questions.skill: Critiquing a misleading display
questions.stem: A graph draws ice-cream sales (left axis, 0 to 500) and sunburn cases (right axis, 0 to 50) as two lines that look almost identical. Which is a valid concern about drawing two different vertical scales on one graph?
choices: It means the graph can show only one of the two variables at a time
It makes the values of both variables false, whatever they were
The scales can be chosen so two lines look more alike than they are
It forces the two lines to have exactly equal values everywhere
questions.answer: The scales can be chosen so two lines look more alike than they are
questions.solution: With separate axes the designer can stretch or shrink either line, so unrelated or loosely related data can be made to look closely matched. The values themselves are not changed.

solve.answer: The scales can be chosen so two lines look more alike than they are
solve.work: Two independent scales can be chosen to make lines look alike, suggesting a closer link than exists.

questions.skill: Critiquing a misleading display
questions.stem: A 3-D pie chart is tilted so that the slice nearest the viewer looks larger than another slice of exactly the same size at the back. Why is this misleading?
choices: The slices of a 3-D pie do not have to add up to 100 percent
A pie chart cannot show two slices that have the same size
The slices at the back are always larger than they appear to be
Perspective makes slices near the viewer look larger than they are
questions.answer: Perspective makes slices near the viewer look larger than they are
questions.solution: In a 3-D view, parts closer to the viewer take up more of the picture. Equal shares then look unequal, so readers misjudge the data.

solve.answer: Perspective makes slices near the viewer look larger than they are
solve.work: Perspective in 3-D makes near slices look larger than equal slices at the back.

questions.skill: Critiquing a misleading display
questions.stem: A headline says, "Sales soared 200 percent!" Sales rose from 1 item to 3 items. Why might the headline mislead readers?
choices: A percent increase can never be more than 100 percent, so it is false
The increase is only 2 items, so a large percent hides a small change
The headline is fair, since a percent always describes a change fully
The word soared is wrong, because sales cannot rise by 2 items
questions.answer: The increase is only 2 items, so a large percent hides a small change
questions.solution: Going from 1 to 3 is an increase of 2, which is 200 percent of the starting value. The percent is correct, but because the starting amount is tiny, it makes a very small change sound enormous.

solve.answer: The increase is only 2 items, so a large percent hides a small change
solve.work: 1 to 3 is a 200 percent increase but only 2 items; the big percent hides a tiny change.

questions.skill: Reading non-standard displays
questions.stem: A scatter plot of (hours studied, test score) has blue points for students who sleep 8 hours or more and red points for the others. At every number of hours studied, the blue points are above the red ones. What does this suggest?
choices: Students who study more hours tend to sleep more hours each night
Sleeping for 8 hours makes every student score higher on every test
Students who sleep more tend to score higher after equal study time
Hours studied and test score are not related to each other at all
questions.answer: Students who sleep more tend to score higher after equal study time
questions.solution: The color is a third variable. At each study time the blue points are higher, so the well-rested students tend to score higher. The plot shows a pattern, not a proof of cause.

solve.answer: Students who sleep more tend to score higher after equal study time
solve.work: At equal study hours, the 8+ hour sleepers score higher: those who sleep more tend to score higher after equal study time. D overstates (every, makes).

questions.skill: Reading non-standard displays
questions.stem: A shaded grid shows the number of visitors to a library. The legend says: lightest 0 to 19, light 20 to 39, medium 40 to 59, dark 60 to 79, darkest 80 or more. Visitor counts are whole numbers. Monday morning is in the medium shade and Monday afternoon is in the darkest shade. What is the smallest possible difference between the two counts?
questions.solution: The medium shade allows at most 59 visitors and the darkest allows at least 80. The two counts are closest when the morning has 59 and the afternoon has 80, a difference of $80 - 59 = 21$.

solve.work: Medium: 40-59, darkest: 80 or more. Smallest gap 80 - 59 = 21.

questions.skill: Reading non-standard displays
questions.stem: In a bubble chart of cities, the horizontal value is kilometers of bike lanes, the vertical value is the percent of commuters who bike, and the bubble size is population. The bubbles trend upward from the lower left to the upper right. Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: Building more bike lanes will make a greater percent of commuters bike
Cities with more bike lanes tend to have a greater percent who bike
Cities with larger bubbles also have more kilometers of bike lanes
Larger cities have a greater percent of their commuters who bike
questions.answer: Cities with more bike lanes tend to have a greater percent who bike
questions.solution: The upward trend in position shows an association between bike lanes and biking. It does not prove that lanes cause biking, and bubble size (population) was not the thing that trended.

solve.answer: Cities with more bike lanes tend to have a greater percent who bike
solve.work: The upward trend links bike-lane km and percent who bike: cities with more lanes tend to have a greater percent. Causation (B) and population claims (A, C) are not supported.

questions.skill: Choosing and building a scatter plot
questions.stem: A student is plotting $y$-values from 14 to 87. The vertical axis must start at 0 and go up in steps of 20, so it ends at a multiple of 20 that is at least 87. What number should the axis end at?
questions.solution: The multiples of 20 are 20, 40, 60, 80, 100. The first that is at least 87 is 100, so the axis should end at 100.

questions.skill: Predicting from a line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit for a puppy's age, $x$ (in weeks), and its weight, $y$ (in pounds), is $y = 1.5x + 6$. At what age, in weeks, does the line predict a weight of 27 pounds?
questions.solution: Set the predicted weight equal to 27: $1.5x + 6 = 27$. Subtract 6 to get $1.5x = 21$, then divide by 1.5 to get $x = 14$ weeks.

questions.skill: Informal line of best fit
questions.stem: A line of best fit for children's ages, $x$ (in years), and heights, $y$ (in centimeters), passes through $(5, 108)$ and $(13, 156)$. At what age does the line predict a height of 132 centimeters?
questions.solution: The slope is $\frac{156 - 108}{13 - 5} = 6$ centimeters per year. To go from 108 to 132 the height must rise 24 centimeters, which takes $24 / 6 = 4$ years after age 5. The age is $5 + 4 = 9$.

questions.skill: Strength of a correlation coefficient
questions.stem: Four data sets have these correlation coefficients, $r$. Which value shows the strongest linear relationship?
questions.solution: The strength of a linear relationship depends on how close $r$ is to $1$ or $-1$, not on its sign. Of the four, $-0.9$ is the closest to $-1$, so it is the strongest.

questions.skill: Computing a residual
questions.stem: A residual is the actual value minus the predicted value. A line predicts a quiz score of 47 for a student, but the student actually scored 52. What is the residual?
questions.solution: Residual $=$ actual $-$ predicted $= 52 - 47 = 5$.

questions.skill: Correlation is not causation
questions.stem: Data show that towns with more ice cream sales also have more sunburns. What is the best conclusion?
choices: Eating ice cream causes people to get sunburned
Hot, sunny weather may cause both, so the data do not show that ice cream causes sunburns
Getting sunburned causes people to buy more ice cream
There is no relationship between ice cream sales and sunburns
questions.answer: Hot, sunny weather may cause both, so the data do not show that ice cream causes sunburns
questions.solution: The two go up together, so they are correlated. But a third variable, hot sunny weather, can explain both. A correlation alone does not show that one thing causes the other.

solve.answer: Hot, sunny weather may cause both, so the data do not show that ice cream causes sunburns
solve.work: Correlation is not causation; hot sunny weather is a likely common cause of both.

questions.skill: Least-squares line: meaning and prediction
questions.stem: The least-squares line for a taxi ride is $\hat{y} = 2x + 3$, where $x$ is the number of miles driven and $\hat{y}$ is the predicted fare in dollars. What fare does the line predict for a 10-mile ride?
questions.solution: Put $x = 10$ into the line: $2(10) + 3 = 23$ dollars.

questions.skill: Least-squares line: meaning and prediction
questions.stem: A least-squares line for a bike rental shop is $\hat{y} = 6x + 4$, where $x$ is the hours rented and $\hat{y}$ is the predicted cost in dollars. What does the slope 6 tell you?
choices: A rental of 0 hours is predicted to cost 6 dollars
A rental of 6 hours is predicted to cost 4 dollars
Each extra hour adds about 6 dollars to the predicted cost
Every rental is predicted to last about 6 hours
questions.answer: Each extra hour adds about 6 dollars to the predicted cost
questions.solution: The slope is the change in the predicted $y$ for each 1-unit increase in $x$: 6 dollars more per hour.

solve.answer: Each extra hour adds about 6 dollars to the predicted cost
solve.work: Slope = change in predicted cost per extra hour = 6 dollars.

questions.skill: Least-squares line: meaning and prediction
questions.stem: A least-squares line predicts the height $\hat{h}$ (in centimeters) of a burning candle after $t$ hours: $\hat{h} = 20 - 2t$. What does the 20 represent?
choices: The predicted number of hours the candle will burn
The predicted height lost during each hour
The predicted height of the candle after 2 hours
The predicted height when the candle is first lit
questions.answer: The predicted height when the candle is first lit
questions.solution: The 20 is the value of the line at $t = 0$, the moment the candle is lit.

solve.answer: The predicted height when the candle is first lit
solve.work: At t=0, h=20: height when first lit.

questions.skill: Least-squares line: meaning and prediction
questions.stem: The least-squares line for a data set is $\hat{y} = 3x - 4$. What is the predicted value of $y$ when $x = 5$?

questions.skill: Exponential models
questions.stem: A colony of bacteria doubles every hour. It starts with 5 bacteria. How many bacteria are there after 4 hours?
questions.solution: Doubling 4 times: 5 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 = 5 x 16 = 80.

questions.skill: Exponential models
questions.stem: Which equation shows exponential growth?
questions.solution: Exponential growth has the form $y = a \cdot b^x$ with $b > 1$. The base 1.2 is greater than 1; the base 0.8 would be decay.

questions.skill: Exponential models
questions.stem: A population is modeled by $P = 250(1.04)^t$, where $t$ is the time in years. What is the population when $t = 0$?
questions.solution: When $t = 0$, $(1.04)^0 = 1$, so $P = 250$. The number in front of the base is the starting amount.

questions.skill: Exponential models
questions.stem: Which equation shows exponential decay?
questions.solution: Exponential decay has the form $y = a \cdot b^x$ with $0 < b < 1$. Here $b = 0.9$.

questions.skill: Exponential models
questions.stem: A dose of medicine in the body halves every hour. At first there are 500 milligrams. How many milligrams remain after 3 hours?
questions.solution: Halving 3 times: 500, 250, 125, 62.5. So 62.5 milligrams remain.

questions.skill: Correlation coefficient: sign and strength
questions.stem: Which value of $r$ describes a strong negative linear relationship?
questions.solution: Negative means $y$ decreases as $x$ increases. Strong means $r$ is close to $-1$ or $1$. Only $-0.95$ is both.

questions.skill: Correlation coefficient: sign and strength
questions.stem: In a data set, $y$ tends to get smaller as $x$ gets larger. The correlation coefficient $r$ is most likely
choices: positive
a negative value
a value greater than 1
exactly 0
questions.answer: a negative value
questions.solution: A pattern that falls from left to right has a negative correlation.

solve.answer: a negative value
solve.work: y falls as x rises: negative r.

questions.skill: Correlation coefficient: sign and strength
questions.stem: All the data points lie exactly on the line $y = -3x + 7$. What is the correlation coefficient $r$?
questions.solution: Points exactly on a line with a negative slope give $r = -1$, a perfect negative linear relationship.

solve.work: Perfect line with negative slope: r=-1.

questions.skill: Correlation coefficient: sign and strength
questions.stem: The correlation coefficient $r$ always lies between which two numbers?
questions.solution: By definition $-1 \le r \le 1$.

questions.skill: Residuals and residual plots
questions.stem: A model predicts that a plant will be 80 millimeters tall. The plant is actually 74 millimeters tall. What is the residual (actual minus predicted)?
questions.solution: Residual = actual - predicted = 74 - 80 = -6.

questions.skill: Residuals and residual plots
questions.stem: The residual for one data point is positive. What does that tell you?
choices: The actual value is less than the predicted value
The actual value is greater than the predicted value
The line passes exactly through the point
The point is certainly an outlier
questions.answer: The actual value is greater than the predicted value
questions.solution: Residual = actual - predicted, so a positive residual means the actual value is above the prediction.

solve.answer: The actual value is greater than the predicted value

questions.skill: Residuals and residual plots
questions.stem: The line $\hat{y} = 2x + 5$ is used to predict $y$. At $x = 4$, the actual value of $y$ is 15. What is the residual?
questions.solution: Predicted: 2(4) + 5 = 13. Residual = 15 - 13 = 2.

questions.skill: Residuals and residual plots
questions.stem: A residual plot shows points scattered randomly above and below zero with no pattern. What does this suggest about a linear model?
choices: The two variables have no relationship at all
A curved model is needed instead
A linear model is appropriate for the data
The line fits the data very badly
questions.answer: A linear model is appropriate for the data
questions.solution: Random scatter of residuals about zero is what we expect when a line is a good model.

solve.answer: A linear model is appropriate for the data
solve.work: Random residual scatter: linear model appropriate.

questions.skill: Outliers and influential points
questions.stem: What is an outlier in a scatter plot?
choices: The point with the largest $x$-value in the data set
The point where the line crosses the $y$-axis
The point with the same $x$-value as another point
A point far from the overall pattern of the points
questions.answer: A point far from the overall pattern of the points
questions.solution: An outlier stands apart from the general pattern of the other points.

solve.answer: A point far from the overall pattern of the points

questions.skill: Outliers and influential points
questions.stem: On a scatter plot, one point is far from the line, and it turns out that its value was typed wrongly. What should be done?
choices: Correct the error, since the point was recorded wrongly
Move the line so that it passes through that one wrong point
Remove every other point from the data set, then draw a new line
Leave the error in the data and say nothing about it to anyone
questions.answer: Correct the error, since the point was recorded wrongly
questions.solution: If a point is far from the pattern because of a recording mistake, the right step is to fix the mistake.

solve.answer: Correct the error, since the point was recorded wrongly
solve.work: A known recording error should be corrected.

questions.skill: Outliers and influential points
questions.stem: Ten-year-olds' heights in centimeters are recorded as (age, height) pairs. Which pair is an outlier?
questions.solution: Most ten-year-olds are about 140 centimeters tall. A height of 60 centimeters is far from the others.

questions.skill: Correlation versus causation
questions.stem: A study finds that students who wear glasses tend to read more books. Can we conclude that wearing glasses causes more reading?
choices: Yes, because the two variables go together so clearly in the data
Yes, because the information came from a real study
No; glasses cannot be linked to anything about reading
No; being linked does not show that one causes the other
questions.answer: No; being linked does not show that one causes the other
questions.solution: A correlation shows the variables are associated, not that one causes the other.

solve.answer: No; being linked does not show that one causes the other

questions.skill: Correlation versus causation
questions.stem: Which is the best way to find out whether a new fertilizer causes plants to grow taller?
choices: Randomly choose which plants get the fertilizer, then compare heights
Compare plants that gardeners chose to fertilize with all of the others
Ask gardeners which plants look the tallest
Notice that the tall plants in the garden are often the fertilized plants
questions.answer: Randomly choose which plants get the fertilizer, then compare heights
questions.solution: Random assignment makes the groups alike in every other way, so a difference in height can be traced to the fertilizer.

solve.answer: Randomly choose which plants get the fertilizer, then compare heights

questions.skill: Correlation versus causation
questions.stem: Two variables $X$ and $Y$ have a strong correlation. What does this show?
choices: $X$ is the cause of $Y$, and nothing else is involved in the link
$X$ and $Y$ are associated, but neither need cause the other
$Y$ is the cause of $X$, and nothing else is involved in the link
$X$ and $Y$ are really just one variable that was measured twice
questions.answer: $X$ and $Y$ are associated, but neither need cause the other
questions.solution: Correlation describes association only; cause needs more evidence, such as a well-designed experiment.

solve.answer: $X$ and $Y$ are associated, but neither need cause the other

questions.skill: Correlation versus causation
questions.stem: Teams that practice more tend to win more games. A coach says winning teams may enjoy practice more. What is the coach pointing out?
choices: Practice has no connection with winning of any kind
The data on wins must have been recorded wrongly
The cause and effect might run the other way around in this case
More practice always means more wins in every case
questions.answer: The cause and effect might run the other way around in this case
questions.solution: The coach suggests the cause and effect may run the other way, so the correlation alone does not settle which causes which.

solve.answer: The cause and effect might run the other way around in this case
solve.work: Winning may cause enjoying practice (more practice): reverse causation.

questions.skill: Making and judging predictions
questions.stem: A line is fit to data with $x$-values from 10 to 50. Which prediction is an extrapolation?
choices: Predicting $y$ for $x = 20.5$
Predicting $y$ for $x = 80$
Predicting $y$ for $x = 35.5$
Predicting $y$ for $x = 45.5$
questions.answer: Predicting $y$ for $x = 80$
questions.solution: Extrapolation means predicting outside the range of the data. 80 is outside 10 to 50.

solve.answer: Predicting $y$ for $x = 80$

questions.skill: Making and judging predictions
questions.stem: A line fits the prices of used cars aged 1 to 10 years: $\hat{y} = -1200x + 15000$, where $x$ is the age in years and $\hat{y}$ is the price in dollars. What price does the line predict for a car aged 4 years?
questions.solution: $-1200(4) + 15000 = -4800 + 15000 = 10200$ dollars. Age 4 is inside the range of the data, so this is a reasonable prediction.

questions.skill: Making and judging predictions
questions.stem: A line fit to data predicts a negative number of fish for a lake far beyond the range of the data. What does this tell you?
choices: The lake must truly have no fish in it at that point
The line should be shifted so that it fits that one point
The line should not be trusted that far away from the data it was fit to
The data points near the middle must all have been wrong
questions.answer: The line should not be trusted that far away from the data it was fit to
questions.solution: A negative count is impossible. The line only describes the pattern within the range of the data.

solve.answer: The line should not be trusted that far away from the data it was fit to
solve.work: Extrapolation far beyond data is untrustworthy.

questions.skill: Making and judging predictions
questions.stem: A model predicts that a plant will be 48 centimeters tall. The plant measures 51 centimeters. By how many centimeters was the prediction off?
questions.solution: 51 - 48 = 3 centimeters.

questions.skill: Outliers and influential points
questions.stem: The line $\hat{y} = x + 2$ fits a scatter plot well. Four of the data points are $(1, 3)$, $(2, 4)$, $(3, 20)$ and $(4, 6)$. Which point is an outlier?
questions.solution: At $x = 1, 2, 3, 4$ the line predicts $y = 3, 4, 5, 6$. The points $(1, 3)$, $(2, 4)$ and $(4, 6)$ lie right on the line. The point $(3, 20)$ is 15 units above the predicted 5, far from the pattern, so it is the outlier.

solve.work: Predicted y = x+2: (1)->3, (2)->4, (3)->5, (4)->6. Actual 3,4,20,6. Only (3,20) is far from the line (residual 15); the others have residual 0.

questions.skill: Correlation versus causation
questions.stem: Among children aged 5 to 12, shoe size and reading score have a strong positive correlation. Which explanation is the most reasonable?
choices: Older children tend to have both bigger feet and higher reading scores
Having bigger feet helps a child read more words correctly on the test
Reading more books makes a child's feet grow to a larger shoe size
The correlation must be a mistake, because feet cannot affect reading at all
questions.answer: Older children tend to have both bigger feet and higher reading scores
questions.solution: Age is a third variable. Older children have bigger feet and also have had more time to learn to read. Neither one causes the other, but the correlation is real, so it is not a mistake.

solve.answer: Older children tend to have both bigger feet and higher reading scores
solve.work: Age is a lurking variable: older children have bigger feet and read better. The causal options (B, D) are unreasonable, and C wrongly says the correlation must be a mistake; correlation can exist without causation.

questions.skill: Predicting from a least-squares line
questions.stem: The least-squares line for a plant's height, $y$ (in centimeters), after $x$ weeks is $\hat{y} = 1.5x + 12.4$. Use the line to predict the height after 6 weeks, in centimeters.
questions.solution: Substitute $x = 6$: $\hat{y} = 1.5(6) + 12.4 = 9 + 12.4 = 21.4$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Judging an extrapolated prediction
questions.stem: A line fits the heights of children aged 5 to 12 well. A student uses the line to predict the height of a 40-year-old. Why is this prediction unreliable?
choices: Predictions from a line of best fit are never reliable
A line of best fit must pass through every point to be used
Age 40 is far outside the ages in the data, and the pattern may not continue
Height cannot be predicted from age at all
questions.answer: Age 40 is far outside the ages in the data, and the pattern may not continue
questions.solution: The line was fitted to ages 5 to 12. Predicting far outside that range (extrapolating) assumes the same pattern continues, but people stop growing as they become adults.

solve.answer: Age 40 is far outside the ages in the data, and the pattern may not continue
solve.work: Extrapolation far outside the data range (5-12); growth stops in adulthood so the line will not hold.

questions.skill: Meaning of an exponential growth factor
questions.stem: A town's population is modeled by $P = 2{,}000(1.05)^t$, where $t$ is the number of years. What does the 1.05 tell you?
choices: The population grows by 5 percent each year
The population grows by 105 percent each year
The population grows by 1.05 people each year
The population shrinks by 5 percent each year
questions.answer: The population grows by 5 percent each year
questions.solution: Each year the population is multiplied by 1.05, which is 100 percent plus 5 percent. So it grows by 5 percent each year.

solve.answer: The population grows by 5 percent each year
solve.work: Growth factor 1.05 = 1 + 0.05: the population grows by 5 percent each year (it becomes 105 percent of the previous year, not grows by 105 percent).

questions.skill: Least-squares line: meaning and prediction
questions.stem: For a data set, the mean of the $x$-values is 10 and the mean of the $y$-values is 50. The least-squares line has slope 3. What is its $y$-intercept?
questions.solution: A least-squares line passes through the point (mean of $x$, mean of $y$) = (10, 50). So $50 = 3(10) + b$, which gives $b = 20$.

questions.skill: Least-squares line: meaning and prediction
questions.stem: The least-squares line $\hat{y} = 2.5x + 10$ predicts the weight of a puppy, in pounds, at age $x$ weeks. At what age does the line predict a weight of 35 pounds?

questions.skill: Least-squares line: meaning and prediction
questions.stem: As the temperature $x$ rises, the number of winter coats $y$ sold in a store falls. Which equation could be the least-squares line for these data?
questions.solution: Sales fall as temperature rises, so the slope is negative. The intercept must also be positive: a negative intercept would predict negative sales on a very cold day.

solve.work: Falling y means negative slope; -4.2x-300 gives negative sales for positive temps, so -4.2x+300.

questions.skill: Least-squares line: meaning and prediction
questions.stem: A line of best fit passes through the points $(2, 14)$ and $(6, 30)$. What value of $y$ does the line predict when $x = 10$?

questions.skill: Least-squares line: meaning and prediction
questions.stem: What makes a line the least-squares line for a data set?
choices: It passes through as many of the data points as it possibly can do
It makes the sum of the squared residuals as small as possible
It has the same number of points above it as below it
It connects the first data point in the list to the last data point
questions.answer: It makes the sum of the squared residuals as small as possible
questions.solution: The least-squares line is the one for which the total of the squares of the residuals is smallest.

solve.answer: It makes the sum of the squared residuals as small as possible
solve.work: Definition: minimizes sum of squared residuals.

questions.skill: Exponential models
questions.stem: An account holds 2000 dollars and grows by 10 percent each year, so $A = 2000(1.1)^t$. How many dollars are in the account after 2 years?

questions.skill: Exponential models
questions.stem: The values of $y$ for $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$ are 4, 12, 36, 108. Which equation fits these data?
questions.solution: Each value is 3 times the one before it (12/4 = 3, 36/12 = 3, 108/36 = 3), so the growth factor is 3 and the start is 4.

questions.skill: Exponential models
questions.stem: An exponential model passes through the points $(0, 6)$ and $(1, 15)$. What is its growth factor?
questions.solution: In $y = a \cdot b^x$, $a = 6$ (the value at $x = 0$). At $x = 1$, $y = 6b = 15$, so $b = 15/6 = 2.5$.

questions.skill: Exponential models
questions.stem: The value of a machine is modeled by $V = 3000(0.85)^t$, where $t$ is in years. By what percent does its value decrease each year?
choices: 85 percent a year
0.85 percent a year
15 percent each year
8.5 percent a year
questions.answer: 15 percent each year
questions.solution: Each year the value is 0.85 times the year before, which is 85 percent of it. So it loses 100 - 85 = 15 percent.

solve.answer: 15 percent each year

questions.skill: Correlation coefficient: sign and strength
questions.stem: Compare two data sets: one has $r = -0.8$ and the other has $r = 0.6$. Which statement is true?
choices: The set with $r = 0.6$ has the stronger linear relationship because it is positive
Both sets have equally strong relationships because both are far from 0
The set with $r = -0.8$ has the weaker relationship because it is negative
The set with $r = -0.8$ has the stronger linear relationship
questions.answer: The set with $r = -0.8$ has the stronger linear relationship
questions.solution: Strength depends on how close $|r|$ is to 1, not on the sign. $|{-0.8}| = 0.8$ is greater than $0.6$.

solve.answer: The set with $r = -0.8$ has the stronger linear relationship

questions.skill: Correlation coefficient: sign and strength
questions.stem: Heights in inches and weights in pounds of some adults have $r = 0.7$. Each height is then converted to centimeters. What is the new value of $r$?
questions.solution: Changing the units of a variable does not change $r$, so it is still 0.7.

solve.work: r unchanged by positive linear change of units: 0.7.

questions.skill: Correlation coefficient: sign and strength
questions.stem: The points on a scatter plot follow a clear U-shaped curve, yet the calculated correlation is $r \approx 0$. What does this mean?
choices: There is no straight-line link, but there may be a curved one
There is no relationship of any kind between the variables
The data must contain a mistake that should be corrected
The relationship is strong and negative
questions.answer: There is no straight-line link, but there may be a curved one
questions.solution: $r$ measures only linear association. A curve can be very strong yet have $r$ near 0.

solve.answer: There is no straight-line link, but there may be a curved one
solve.work: r measures only linear association; U-shape is a curved relationship.

questions.skill: Correlation coefficient: sign and strength
questions.stem: A set with $r = 0.6$ shows a moderate linear relationship. How many of these correlation coefficients show a stronger linear relationship than that: 0.35, $-0.92$, 0.78, $-0.5$?
questions.solution: Compare |r| with 0.6: 0.35 is weaker, 0.92 is stronger, 0.78 is stronger, 0.5 is weaker. So 2 of them are stronger.

questions.skill: Correlation coefficient: sign and strength
questions.stem: The points on a scatter plot rise from left to right and lie close to a straight line, but not exactly on it. Which value of $r$ fits best?
questions.solution: Rising means positive, and being close to a line means $|r|$ is near 1. Also, $r$ can never be as big as 9.

solve.work: Rising, close to line: strong positive, 0.9.

questions.skill: Residuals and residual plots
questions.stem: A model predicts a score of 62 for a student. The residual for that student is $-5$. What was the student's actual score?
questions.solution: Actual = predicted + residual = 62 + (-5) = 57.

questions.skill: Residuals and residual plots
questions.stem: The line $\hat{y} = 2x + 3$ is fit to the data points $(2, 9)$, $(4, 11)$ and $(6, 18)$. What is the greatest of the three residuals?
questions.solution: Predicted values: 7, 11, 15. Residuals: 9 - 7 = 2, 11 - 11 = 0, 18 - 15 = 3. The greatest is 3.

questions.skill: Residuals and residual plots
questions.stem: The residual for one student is $-8$ points. Which statement is correct?
choices: The line predicted 8 points fewer than the student actually scored
The student scored exactly 8 points
The line's prediction is off by 8 percent of the student's actual score
The line predicted 8 points more than the student actually scored
questions.answer: The line predicted 8 points more than the student actually scored
questions.solution: Residual = actual - predicted = -8, so the prediction is 8 points higher than the actual score.

solve.answer: The line predicted 8 points more than the student actually scored

questions.skill: Residuals and residual plots
questions.stem: The residuals for four data points are 2, $-3$, 1 and $-2$. What is the sum of the squares of these residuals?
questions.solution: Squares: 4, 9, 1, 4. Their sum is 4 + 9 + 1 + 4 = 18.

questions.skill: Outliers and influential points
